docs.text:
Method Group With ENUMs Total Percentage Account Information 1 1 100% Orders & History 2 3 67% Symbols & Quotes 2 6 33% Trading Operations 2 4 50% Streaming Methods 2 4 50% TOTAL 9 18 50%

MT4 has a single order list (there is no positions/deals split as in MT5) and no Depth-of-Market, order_check or order_calc_* methods — those are MT5-only.

docs.title: Python ENUM Access
docs.text:
Python accesses ENUMs through the mt4_term_api_* protobuf modules:

Correct: 

from MetaRpcMT4 import mt4_term_api_trading_helper_pb2 as trading_helper_pb2

# Using an ENUM value
op = trading_helper_pb2.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY

from MetaRpcMT4 import mt4_term_api_account_helper_pb2 as account_helper_pb2
sort = account_helper_pb2.EnumOpenedOrderSortType.SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC

Incorrect: 

OC_OP_BUY  # NameError: name 'OC_OP_BUY' is not defined

docs.title: Special Cases
docs.text:
1. Order operation enums come in three flavours. OrderSendOperationType (OC_OP_*, used to send an order), OpenedOrderType (OO_OP_*, the type reported back on open/history orders) and SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE (SUB_OP_*, used inside streaming events) describe the same six operations but are distinct enum types — don't mix their value names. OpenedOrderType has two extra non-tradable entries, OO_OP_BALANCE and OO_OP_CREDIT, used for balance/credit history records.

2. Returned codes are not ENUMs. Trade-operation return/error codes are plain integers, not typed enums. See the Return Codes Reference.

docs.title: Getting Started with PyMT4
docs.text: Quick Setup & Overview - Start automating your trading with PyMT4 (Python for MetaTrader 4) in minutes.

docs.title: 🎯 What is PyMT4?
docs.text: PyMT4 is an industrial-grade, type-safe Python client library for interacting with MetaTrader 4 terminals via high-performance gRPC. It eliminates complex C++ DLL wrappers and provides direct, reliable programmatic trading.

docs.title: 🌟 Key Advantages
docs.text:
• High Throughput: Native gRPC streaming for sub-millisecond price ticks and trade execution.
  • Three-Layer Architecture: Low-level gRPC (MT4Account), typed wrapper methods (MT4Service), and high-level convenience (MT4Sugar).
  • Resilient Connection: Auto-reconnect, exponential backoff, and transparent channel healing.
  • Production Ready: Fully verified across institutional accounts, hedge fund systems, and automated retail bots.

docs.title: 📦 Installation
docs.text:
Install PyMT4 via your standard Python package manager:

pip install MetaRpcMT4

docs.title: 🔑 API Key & Authentication
docs.text:
Connecting to MetaRPC production endpoints (mt4.mrpc.pro:443) requires an API key:

  1. Sign Up: Create an account for free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Generate API Key: In your MetaRPC Portal dashboard at https://mrpc.pro/my, go to API Keys to generate and copy your personal API token.
  3. Configure Connection: Pass your API key / token along with the server address (mt4.mrpc.pro:443) in your connection settings.

docs.title: 🆔 Automatic Account ID & Authentication
docs.text:
MetaRPC endpoints require authentication and session management: 1. APIKey: Your personal authentication token from https://mrpc.pro/my (obtained by registering at https://mrpc.pro/signup). Sent in the APIKey header. 2. id: A terminal session GUID returned by Connect / ConnectEx (terminalInstanceGuid).

💡 Seamless Automation: You do not need to call GetId or provide an id header when connecting. The server automatically generates a session GUID upon connection and returns it to the caller. The SDK automatically captures this session ID and attaches it alongside your APIKey to all subsequent requests and streaming subscriptions.

docs.title: 🔌 Minimal Connection Example
docs.text:
Here is how easy it is to initialize MT4Account, connect to your MetaTrader terminal, and retrieve your account balance:

account = MT4Account(user=user, password=password, grpc_server=grpc_server)
await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name, base_chart_symbol="EURUSD", timeout_seconds=30)
summary = await account.account_summary()
print(f"Balance: {summary.account_balance}, Equity: {summary.account_equity}")

docs.title: 🗺️ Documentation Road Map
docs.text:
To get the most out of PyMT4, follow this suggested reading order:

  1. Your First Project - Build and run a working project in 10 minutes.
  2. Project Map - Understand the 3 architectural layers and interaction flow.
  3. Glossary - Essential MetaTrader 4 and algorithmic trading terminology.
  4. MT4 for Beginners - Step-by-step terminal setup and demo account guide.
  5. gRPC Streaming - Subscribe to ticks, trade events, and order ticket / profit updates.
  6. Return Codes - Complete reference of broker and gateway return codes.

docs.title: PyMT4 Glossary
docs.text: Project-specific terms and concepts. This glossary covers PyMT4 architecture, components, and trading automation terminology used throughout the codebase.

docs.title: Three-Tier Architecture
docs.text:
Core design pattern of PyMT4 with three abstraction levels:

  • Tier 1 (MT4Account): Low-level gRPC communication with the MT4 terminal
  • Tier 2 (MT4Service): Typed facade over MT4Account with convenience trade helpers
  • Tier 3 (MT4Sugar): High-level one-liner API with ready-made patterns

docs.title: MT4Account
docs.text:
🔹 Tier 1 - Low-Level API

Base layer providing direct access to the MT4 terminal via the gRPC protocol.

Key characteristics:

  • Raw gRPC calls to the MT4 terminal
  • Built-in connection resilience with automatic reconnection (execute_with_reconnect)
  • Works with protobuf Request/Response objects
  • Full control, maximum complexity
  • 18 core API methods (account, orders, history, symbols/quotes, trading, streaming) plus connection & stream helpers
  • Returns protobuf Data objects
  • Session management via the terminal session GUID (terminalInstanceGuid)

When to use: Advanced users who need granular control, custom integrations, building custom wrappers.

Location: package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py (~1200 lines)

Documentation: MT4Account API Reference

docs.title: MT4Service
docs.text:
🔸 Tier 2 - Typed Facade

Middle layer providing simplified method signatures without proto boilerplate.

Key characteristics:

  • Wraps all 18 MT4Account operations one-to-one (same names: account_summary, opened_orders, orders_history, order_send, quote, …)
  • Adds convenience trade helpers: buy_market / sell_market / buy_limit / sell_limit / buy_stop / sell_stop, close, close_by, close_partial, modify_sl_tp
  • order_send_with_defaults / set_trade_defaults for shared order defaults
  • Exposes the high-level layer via the service.sugar property
  • Primary purpose: architectural middleware layer that MT4Sugar is built on

When to use: Building custom strategies that need more control than Sugar but less boilerplate than MT4Account.

Location: app/MT4Service.py (~985 lines)

Documentation: MT4Service Overview

docs.title: MT4Sugar
docs.text:
🔺 Tier 3 - Convenience API

High-level API for common trading operations.

Key characteristics:

  • Async context-manager support (async with MT4Sugar(service) as sugar)
  • Pips-first helpers (sl_pips / tp_pips, pips_to_price, price_to_pips)
  • Unified order entry (place_order) with smart defaults (set_defaults / with_defaults)
  • One-line operations and background watchers
  • Type hints everywhere
  • ~60 high-level methods
  • Best starting point for most use cases

Key features:

  • buy_market(symbol, lots=...) - one line to open a market order
  • calc_lot_by_risk(symbol, risk_percent, stop_pips) - automatic lot sizing by risk
  • buy_market(symbol, lots=..., sl_pips=..., tp_pips=...) - open with SL/TP in pips
  • set_trailing_stop(ticket, distance_pips=...) - server-side style trailing
  • close_all(symbol=...) - bulk close / emergency exit

When to use: Rapid development, prototyping, simple strategies, quick scripts.

Location: app/MT4Sugar.py (~2230 lines)

Documentation: MT4Sugar Reference

docs.title: Async/Await Pattern
docs.text:
Python's built-in asynchronous programming model.

All methods in PyMT4 are async: 

import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account

async def main():
    # Create and connect
    account = MT4Account(user=user, password=password, grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name, base_chart_symbol="EURUSD", timeout_seconds=30)

    # Must use 'await' for all async operations
    summary = await account.account_summary()
    print(f"Balance: {summary.account_balance}")

    orders = await account.opened_orders()

    await account.channel.close()

# Run async function
asyncio.run(main())

Why async?

  • Non-blocking I/O for gRPC calls
  • Better performance for multiple operations
  • Can handle streaming data efficiently
  • Standard Python pattern for network operations

Documentation: Python asyncio

docs.title: Dataclasses
docs.text:
Python's structured data containers.

The Strategy layer uses @dataclass presets for clean, typed configuration: 

from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class StrategyPreset:
    symbol: str
    use_market: bool = True
    entry_price: float | None = None
    lots: float | None = None
    magic: int = 0
    deviation_pips: float = 2.0
    comment: str | None = None

@dataclass
class RiskPreset:
    risk_percent: float
    sl_pips: float
    tp_pips: float | None = None
    trailing_pips: float | None = None
    be_trigger_pips: float | None = None
    be_plus_pips: float | None = None

Account data (account_summary) comes back as a protobuf object, not a dataclass. Access its typed fields directly:

summary = await service.account_summary()
print(summary.account_balance)       # float
print(summary.account_equity)        # float
print(summary.account_margin_free)   # float

Benefits of dataclasses:

  • Type hints for IDE autocomplete
  • Clean attribute access (no dict keys)
  • Automatic __repr__ and __eq__

docs.title: Async Generators
docs.text:
Python's way to stream data asynchronously.

Low-level streaming methods return async generators: 

# Streaming returns an async generator
async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(["EURUSD"]):
    tick = tick_data.symbol_tick
    print(f"Bid: {tick.bid}, Ask: {tick.ask}")

    # Can break anytime
    if some_condition:
        break

# Auto cleanup when loop exits

Critical rules:

  • Use async for to consume data
  • Generator auto-stops when you break
  • No manual cleanup needed

Example with timeout: 

import asyncio

try:
    async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(["EURUSD"]):
        tick = tick_data.symbol_tick
        await asyncio.wait_for(process_tick(tick), timeout=5.0)
except asyncio.TimeoutError:
    print("Processing timeout")

docs.title: Reading Account State
docs.text:
MT4Sugar does not expose balance/equity as properties. Account state comes from account_summary() (via Service or Account), which returns a protobuf object:

summary = await service.account_summary()

balance      = summary.account_balance
equity       = summary.account_equity
margin        = summary.account_margin
free_margin   = summary.account_margin_free
margin_level  = summary.account_margin_level

For live prices, use the Sugar quote helpers:

q   = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")   # {"bid": ..., "ask": ..., "time": ...}
mid = await sugar.mid_price("EURUSD")    # (bid + ask) / 2
spr = await sugar.spread_pips("EURUSD")  # spread in pips

docs.title: Context Managers
docs.text:
Python's pattern for automatic resource cleanup.

MT4Sugar supports async with: 

account = MT4Account(
    user=12345678,
    password="password",
    grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443",
)

await account.connect_by_server_name(
    server_name="EGlobal-Demo",
    base_chart_symbol="EURUSD",
)

service = MT4Service(account)

# Use sugar with a context manager
async with MT4Sugar(service) as sugar:
    q = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)

# Manual channel cleanup still recommended
await account.channel.close()

Why context managers?

  • Cleaner code structure
  • Standard Python pattern
  • Scoped resource usage

Important: Manual channel cleanup

account.channel is the gRPC connection to the MT4 terminal. Call await account.channel.close() to:

  • Close the persistent gRPC connection
  • Release network resources
  • Prevent connection leaks

Recommended pattern with proper cleanup:

account = MT4Account(
    user=12345678,
    password="password",
    grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443",
)

try:
    await account.connect_by_server_name(
        server_name="EGlobal-Demo",
        base_chart_symbol="EURUSD",
    )

    service = MT4Service(account)
    sugar = service.sugar

    # Work here
    q = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)

finally:
    await account.channel.close()  # Always cleanup

docs.title: Normalization
docs.text:
Adjustment of trading parameters to broker requirements.

What gets normalized:

  • Volumes (lots): Rounded to the broker's volume step (e.g., 0.01)
  • Prices: Rounded to the symbol's digits/tick size (e.g., 5 decimals for EURUSD)

In PyMT4: MT4Sugar exposes explicit helpers so you don't have to guess:

# Round a lot size to the broker's volume step
lots = await sugar.normalize_lot("EURUSD", 0.0234)   # -> 0.02

# Round a price to the symbol's digits
price = await sugar.normalize_price("EURUSD", 1.09876543)  # -> 1.09877

# Point / pip size for the symbol
point = await sugar.point("EURUSD")       # e.g. 0.00001 (5-digit broker)
pip   = await sugar.pip_size("EURUSD")    # e.g. 0.0001

buy_market / buy_limit / … normalize lots and prices internally, so manual normalization is only needed for your own calculations.

docs.title: Risk-Based Lot Calculation
docs.text:
Calculate position size based on account risk rather than a fixed lot size.

Methods (MT4Sugar):

# Lot size for a given % risk and SL distance in pips
lots = await sugar.calc_lot_by_risk("EURUSD", risk_percent=2.0, stop_pips=50)

# Open using the risk-based lot
ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=lots, sl_pips=50, tp_pips=100)

# Monetary risk for a given lot + SL distance
cash_risk = await sugar.calc_cash_risk("EURUSD", lots=0.10, stop_pips=50)

Use case: Consistent risk management across all trades.

docs.title: Points vs Pips
docs.text:
Point: Smallest price movement for a symbol (1 tick).

Pip: Traditional forex unit (0.0001 for most pairs).

Relationship:

  • 5-digit brokers: 1 pip = 10 points (EURUSD: 1.10000 → 1.10010 = 1 pip)
  • 3-digit brokers: 1 pip = 10 points (USDJPY: 110.000 → 110.010 = 1 pip)

In PyMT4: MT4Sugar is pips-first — convert with helpers instead of hand-math:

# pip size / point size
pip   = await sugar.pip_size("EURUSD")              # 0.0001
point = await sugar.point("EURUSD")                 # 0.00001

# Convert pips <-> absolute price delta
delta = await sugar.pips_to_price("EURUSD", 20)     # 20 pips -> 0.0020
pips  = await sugar.price_to_pips("EURUSD", 0.0020) # 0.0020  -> 20 pips

docs.title: Pip-Based Order Entry
docs.text:
Open orders with SL/TP expressed in pips (familiar for forex traders).

Methods (MT4Sugar):

# Market orders with SL/TP in pips
ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=30)
ticket = await sugar.sell_market("GBPUSD", lots=0.01, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=30)

# Pending orders: absolute price + SL/TP in pips
ask = (await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD"))["ask"]
ticket = await sugar.buy_limit("EURUSD", price=ask - 0.0020, lots=0.01, sl_pips=15, tp_pips=30)

bid = (await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD"))["bid"]
ticket = await sugar.sell_limit("EURUSD", price=bid + 0.0020, lots=0.01, sl_pips=15, tp_pips=30)

You can also pass absolute sl_price= / tp_price= instead of the pip variants.

docs.title: Trailing Stop
docs.text:
Dynamic Stop Loss that follows price in the profit direction.

In PyMT4: MT4Sugar runs a background trailing worker for you:

# Start trailing: keep SL ~20 pips behind price, update in 5-pip steps
await sugar.set_trailing_stop(ticket, distance_pips=20, step_pips=5)

# Stop trailing that ticket
await sugar.unset_trailing_stop(ticket)

Use case: Locking in profit on trending markets.

docs.title: Breakeven
docs.text:
Moving the Stop Loss to (or past) the entry price to eliminate risk.

Methods (MT4Sugar): 

# Compute a breakeven price from an entry price (sync helper — no await)
bp = sugar.breakeven_price(entry_price=1.10000, commission=0.0, swap=0.0)

# Auto-move SL to breakeven once the order is far enough in profit
await sugar.auto_breakeven(ticket, trigger_pips=40, plus_pips=1)

# Or move SL to an absolute price manually
await sugar.modify_sl_tp_by_price(ticket, sl_price=bp)

docs.title: Hedging
docs.text:
Opening an opposite order to lock in the current profit/loss level.

Implementation: 

# Main order
buy_ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.10)

# ... price moves against you ...

# Hedge
sell_ticket = await sugar.sell_market("EURUSD", lots=0.10)

WARNING: Not all brokers/regulations allow hedging. US brokers typically do not support it.

docs.title: Pending Order
docs.text:
Order that executes automatically when price reaches a specified level.

Types:

  • BUY LIMIT: Buy at a price BELOW current (expect pullback, then up)
  • SELL LIMIT: Sell at a price ABOVE current (expect rally, then down)
  • BUY STOP: Buy at a price ABOVE current (breakout up)
  • SELL STOP: Sell at a price BELOW current (breakout down)

Methods (MT4Sugar): 

# Buy limit without SL/TP
ticket = await sugar.buy_limit("EURUSD", price=1.09950, lots=0.01)

# Buy limit with SL/TP in pips
ticket = await sugar.buy_limit("EURUSD", price=1.09950, lots=0.01, sl_pips=15, tp_pips=30)

# Sell stop with absolute SL/TP
ticket = await sugar.sell_stop("EURUSD", price=1.09950, lots=0.01,
                               sl_price=1.10000, tp_price=1.09900)

# Cancel pending orders (optionally filtered by symbol/magic)
await sugar.cancel_pendings(symbol="EURUSD")

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text:
High-performance RPC (Remote Procedure Call) framework using HTTP/2.

In PyMT4:

  • The MT4Account tier sends gRPC requests to the MetaRPC gateway
  • Request/Response pattern for all operations
  • Async/await for non-blocking calls

Connection setup: 

account = MT4Account(
    user=12345678,
    password="password",
    grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443",
)

await account.connect_by_server_name(
    server_name="EGlobal-Demo",
    base_chart_symbol="EURUSD",
)

Documentation: gRPC Python

docs.title: Protobuf
docs.text:
Protocol Buffers - Google's language-neutral data serialization format.

In PyMT4:

  • All MT4Account methods use protobuf Request/Response messages
  • Generated into the MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_*_pb2 modules
  • Efficient binary serialization, type-safe message structures

Example:

from MetaRpcMT4 import mt4_term_api_trading_helper_pb2 as trading_helper_pb2

# ENUM values live on the generated pb2 modules
op = trading_helper_pb2.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY

MT4Account returns protobuf Data objects. MT4Service and MT4Sugar unwrap the parts you usually need into plain Python types (float, int, dict, int ticket).

docs.title: Return Codes & Errors
docs.text:
How trade failures surface in PyMT4.

  • MT4Account raises ApiExceptionMT4 when the server returns an error, and ConnectExceptionMT4 if you call a method before connecting.
  • MT4Sugar raises MT4Error subclasses (OrderRejected, ModifyRejected, ConnectivityError, RateLimitExceeded) with structured details.
  • Order helpers return the ticket number (int) on success.

Example:

from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import ApiExceptionMT4
from app.Helper.errors import OrderRejected

try:
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)
    print(f"Trade successful! Ticket: {ticket}")
except OrderRejected as e:
    print(f"Order rejected: {e}")
except ApiExceptionMT4 as e:
    print(f"Server error: {e}")

Documentation: Return Codes Reference

docs.title: 📡 Streaming Pattern
docs.text:
Real-time data streams.

Low-level (async generators on MT4Account): 

# Stream tick data
async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(["EURUSD"]):
    tick = tick_data.symbol_tick
    print(f"Bid: {tick.bid}, Ask: {tick.ask}")
    if should_stop:
        break  # auto cleanup

# Stream trade events
async for ev in account.on_trade():
    print(f"Type: {ev.type}")

# Stream open-order P&L updates
async for ev in account.on_opened_orders_profit():
    for o in ev.opened_orders_with_profit_updated:
        print(o)

High-level (callback watchers on MT4Sugar): 

# Register a callback; returns a watch id
def on_tick(t):
    print(t)

watch_id = await sugar.watch_ticks("EURUSD", on_tick)
# ... later ...
await sugar.unwatch(watch_id)

With timeout (Python 3.11+): 

import asyncio

async with asyncio.timeout(60):  # 60 seconds max
    async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(["EURUSD"]):
        process(tick_data.symbol_tick)

Documentation: gRPC Stream Management

docs.title: Basic Trading Terms
docs.text:
Core trading concepts that every trader must understand before working with MT4.

Term Description Example / Details Bid Price at which the broker buys from you (you sell at Bid) EURUSD Bid: 1.10000 Ask Price at which the broker sells to you (you buy at Ask) EURUSD Ask: 1.10002 Spread Difference between Ask and Bid (broker's commission) Ask 1.10002 − Bid 1.10000 = 2 pips spread Long / Buy Opening a BUY order (profit when price goes up) Buy EURUSD at 1.10000, close at 1.10050 = +50 pips Short / Sell Opening a SELL order (profit when price goes down) Sell EURUSD at 1.10000, close at 1.09950 = +50 pips Order A trade on the account — market or pending (MT4 has a single order list) BUY 0.1 lot EURUSD at 1.10000 Market Order Order that executes immediately at the current price BUY EURUSD at current Ask price Pending Order Order that triggers automatically when price reaches a level BUY LIMIT at 1.09950 Lot / Volume Position size (1 lot = 100,000 units of base currency) 0.01 lot = 1,000 units (micro lot) Stop Loss (SL) Price level for automatic loss-limiting exit SL at 1.09950 limits loss to 50 pips Take Profit (TP) Price level for automatic profit-taking exit TP at 1.10050 locks in 50 pips profit Pip Standard unit of price movement (0.0001 for most forex) EURUSD: 1.10000 → 1.10010 = 1 pip Point Smallest price movement (1 tick) For 5-digit broker: 1 pip = 10 points Leverage Borrowed capital from the broker (e.g., 1:100) With 1:100, control $100,000 with $1,000 margin Margin Funds locked as collateral for open orders 1 lot EURUSD at 1:100 ≈ $1,000 margin Free Margin Available funds for opening new orders Equity − Margin Balance Account funds without considering open orders Initial deposit + closed trades P/L Equity Current account value (Balance ± floating P/L) Balance $10,000 + Floating $500 = Equity $10,500 Floating P/L Unrealized profit/loss of open orders Order currently +$50 (not yet closed) Margin Level Ratio of Equity to Margin (%) Equity $10,500 / Margin $1,000 = 1050% Margin Call Warning when Margin Level drops below a threshold Broker warns at 100% Margin Level Stop Out Forced closure when Margin Level is critically low Broker closes orders at ~50% Margin Level Drawdown Decline from peak balance/equity Peak $11,000 → $10,000 = $1,000 drawdown Slippage Difference between expected and executed price Requested 1.10000, filled 1.10003 = 3 pts slippage

Critical for API usage:

# Prices
q   = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")   # {"bid": ..., "ask": ..., "time": ...}
mid = await sugar.mid_price("EURUSD")

# Account state
summary = await service.account_summary()
balance = summary.account_balance
equity  = summary.account_equity

# Open orders
buy_ticket  = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)
sell_ticket = await sugar.sell_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)

# Close order
await sugar.close(buy_ticket)

# Modify SL/TP (absolute prices)
await sugar.modify_sl_tp_by_price(buy_ticket, sl_price=1.09950, tp_price=1.10050)

docs.title: Risk Amount
docs.text:
Account amount you're willing to risk if the Stop Loss hits.

Used in:

# Lot size for 2% risk with 50-pip SL
lots = await sugar.calc_lot_by_risk("EURUSD", risk_percent=2.0, stop_pips=50)

# Open with the risk-based lot
ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=lots, sl_pips=50, tp_pips=100)

docs.title: Grid Trading
docs.text:
Strategy placing multiple pending orders at equal intervals around current price.

How it works:

  1. Place Buy Limit orders below current price (e.g., every 20 pips)
  2. Place Sell Limit orders above current price (e.g., every 20 pips)
  3. As price oscillates, orders trigger and close at TP
  4. Works best in ranging markets

Implementation: 

grid_step_pips = 20
levels = 5

q   = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")
ask, bid = q["ask"], q["bid"]

for i in range(1, levels + 1):
    offset = await sugar.pips_to_price("EURUSD", i * grid_step_pips)

    # Buy Limit below Ask
    await sugar.buy_limit("EURUSD", price=ask - offset, lots=0.01, sl_pips=15, tp_pips=30)

    # Sell Limit above Bid
    await sugar.sell_limit("EURUSD", price=bid + offset, lots=0.01, sl_pips=15, tp_pips=30)

The project ships a ready grid_dca orchestrator — see the Strategies docs.

WARNING: High volatility can trigger many orders, increasing exposure.

docs.title: Scalping
docs.text:
Fast strategy with small profits (5–25 pips) and tight stops (10–20 pips).

Implementation: 

# Scalp with 10-pip SL, 15-pip TP
ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01, sl_pips=10, tp_pips=15)

docs.title: News Trading (OCO Straddle)
docs.text:
Placing stop orders on both sides of price before a major news event.

Implementation: 

q = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")
offset = await sugar.pips_to_price("EURUSD", 30)   # 30 pips

buy_ticket  = await sugar.buy_stop("EURUSD", price=q["ask"] + offset, lots=0.01)
sell_ticket = await sugar.sell_stop("EURUSD", price=q["bid"] - offset, lots=0.01)

# ... after one side triggers, remove the remaining pending order ...
await sugar.cancel_pendings(symbol="EURUSD")

The project ships a ready oco_straddle orchestrator — see the Strategies docs.

WARNING: Slippage during news can trigger both orders.

docs.title: Volume Limits
docs.text:
Broker restrictions on order size (min / max / step).

In PyMT4: normalize_lot snaps any value into the broker's allowed range and step:

lots = await sugar.normalize_lot("EURUSD", 0.0234)   # -> 0.02 (step 0.01)

The raw min/max/step come from symbol_params_many at the MT4Account level if you need them explicitly.

docs.title: Settings File
docs.text:
The examples read connection settings from examples/0_common/settings.json:

{
  "user": 12345678,
  "password": "YOUR_MT4_PASSWORD",
  "grpc_server": "mt4.mrpc.pro:443",
  "mt_cluster": "EGlobal-Demo",
  "test_symbol": "EURUSD",
  "test_volume": 0.01,
  "api_key": "TRIAL"

examples/0_common/demo_helpers.py loads this file and also honours two environment variables that override the file when set:

MRPC_API_KEY=mrpc_live_...        # overrides api_key
MRPC_GRPC_SERVER=mt4.mrpc.pro:443 # overrides grpc_server

Load in Python: 

from demo_helpers import load_settings, create_and_connect_mt4

config  = load_settings()
account = await create_and_connect_mt4(config)

Never commit real credentials. The committed settings.json ships with placeholders; .terminal_id is git-ignored.

docs.title: Batch Operations
docs.text:
Executing an action across multiple orders at once.

Methods (MT4Sugar): 

# Close all open orders (optionally filtered)
await sugar.close_all()                    # everything
await sugar.close_all(symbol="EURUSD")     # by symbol
await sugar.close_all(only_profit=True)    # only profitable

# Cancel pending orders
await sugar.cancel_pendings(symbol="EURUSD")

Use case: Emergency exits, end-of-session cleanup, strategy resets.

docs.title: 📝 History Queries
docs.text:
Retrieving past orders for analysis.

Low-level (MT4Account): 

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from MetaRpcMT4 import mt4_term_api_account_helper_pb2 as account_helper_pb2

to_time = datetime.utcnow()
from_time = to_time - timedelta(days=30)

history = await account.orders_history(
    sort_mode=account_helper_pb2.EnumOrderHistorySortType.HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC,
    from_time=from_time,
    to_time=to_time,
    page_number=0,
    items_per_page=100,
)

High-level (MT4Sugar): 

closed = await sugar.find_orders(state="closed", symbol="EURUSD")

Use case: Performance analysis, trade logs, strategy validation.

docs.title: Exception Handling
docs.text:
Python's error-handling mechanism for API errors.

Connection / API exceptions: 

from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import ConnectExceptionMT4, ApiExceptionMT4

try:
    await account.connect_by_server_name(
        server_name="EGlobal-Demo",

except ConnectExceptionMT4 as e:

except ApiExceptionMT4 as e:

from app.Helper.errors import MT4Error, OrderRejected

try:
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)

docs.title: Type Hints
docs.text:
Python's optional static typing for better IDE support.

All PyMT4 code uses type hints: 

from typing import Optional

async def buy_market(
    self,
    symbol: str | None = None,
    *,
    lots: float | None = None,
    sl_pips: float | None = None,
    tp_pips: float | None = None,

docs.title: 🧱 Enums
docs.text:
Named constants for protobuf values.

PyMT4 enums live on the generated mt4_term_api_*_pb2 modules: 

from MetaRpcMT4 import mt4_term_api_trading_helper_pb2 as trading_helper_pb2
from MetaRpcMT4 import mt4_term_api_account_helper_pb2 as account_helper_pb2

# Order operation (used by order_send)
op = trading_helper_pb2.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY

# History sort mode
sort = account_helper_pb2.EnumOrderHistorySortType.HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC

At the Sugar level you rarely touch enums directly — you pass "buy" / "sell", pip distances and prices, and the SDK maps them to the right enum values.

docs.title: 1️⃣ Simplest Pattern (Auto-timeout)
docs.text:
Use asyncio.wait_for - automatically stops after time expires:

import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account

async def main():
    # Setup connection
    account = MT4Account(
        user=12345,
        password="password",
        grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443"
    )
    await account.connect_by_server_name(
        server_name="YourBroker-Demo",
        base_chart_symbol="EURUSD"
    )

    # ✅ Stream for 10 seconds - stops automatically!
    try:
        async def process_ticks():
            tick_count = 0
            async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(symbols=["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"]):
                tick_count += 1
                tick = tick_data.symbol_tick
                print(f"[{tick_count}] {tick.symbol}: Bid={tick.bid:.5f}, Ask={tick.ask:.5f}")

                if tick_count >= 10:
                    break

        await asyncio.wait_for(process_ticks(), timeout=10.0)
        print("Stream finished")

    finally:
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(main())

When to use: Quick examples, testing, short monitoring sessions

docs.title: 2️⃣ Manual Control Pattern
docs.text:
For full control - you decide when to stop:

async def main():
    account = MT4Account(
        user=12345,
        password="password",
        grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443"
    )
    await account.connect_by_server_name(
        server_name="YourBroker-Demo",
        base_chart_symbol="EURUSD"
    )

    # ✅ Create cancellation event
    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    async def monitor_prices():
        async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(
            symbols=["EURUSD"],
            cancellation_event=cancel_event
        ):
            tick = tick_data.symbol_tick
            print(f"Price: {tick.bid:.5f}")

    # Start monitoring in background
    monitor_task = asyncio.create_task(monitor_prices())

    # ... do other work ...

    # Stop when needed
    await asyncio.sleep(5)
    cancel_event.set()  # Signal stream to stop
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)  # Give stream time to cleanup

    try:
        await account.channel.close()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(main())

When to use: Long-term monitoring, background services, production applications

docs.title: MT4Account (Low-level Streams)
docs.text:
All streaming methods return async generators that yield data objects.

Method Description Returns (async generator) on_symbol_tick(symbols) Real-time price ticks for symbols OnSymbolTickData on_trade() Trade events (orders opened, updated, removed) OnTradeData on_opened_orders_tickets(pull_interval_milliseconds) Live lists of open & pending order tickets OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData on_opened_orders_profit(timer_period_milliseconds) Open-order P&L updates (+ account snapshot) OnOpenedOrdersProfitData

All support the cancellation_event parameter for graceful stopping.

MT4 has four streaming methods. There is no on_trade_transaction / on_position_profit / DOM streaming — those are MT5-only.

Documentation: - Streaming Methods Overview

Examples:

  • examples/1_lowlevel/03_streaming_methods.py - Low-level streaming examples
  • examples/main.py streaming - runs the same via the single entry point

docs.title: Pattern 1: Quick Example (5-10 seconds)
docs.text:
import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account

async def quick_stream_example():

docs.text:
async def event_limited_streaming():
    account = MT4Account(
        user=12345,
        password="password",
        grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443"
    )
    await account.connect_by_server_name(
        server_name="YourBroker-Demo",
        base_chart_symbol="EURUSD"

            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(event_limited_streaming())

docs.text:
async def condition_based_stop():
    account = MT4Account(
        user=12345,

docs.title: Pattern 4: Background Service with Manual Control
docs.text:
class PriceMonitor:
    def __init__(self, account: MT4Account):
        self.account = account
        self.cancel_event = asyncio.Event()
        self.task = None

    async def start(self, symbols: list[str]):
        """Start monitoring in background"""
        self.task = asyncio.create_task(self._monitor_prices(symbols))

    async def _monitor_prices(self, symbols: list[str]):
        """Internal monitoring loop"""
        async for tick_data in self.account.on_symbol_tick(
            symbols=symbols,
            cancellation_event=self.cancel_event
        ):
            tick = tick_data.symbol_tick
            self._process_tick(tick)

    def _process_tick(self, tick):
        """Process each tick"""
        print(f"{tick.symbol}: {tick.bid:.5f} / {tick.ask:.5f}")
        # Your logic here...

    async def stop(self):
        """Stop monitoring gracefully"""
        self.cancel_event.set()

        if self.task:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)  # Give time to cleanup
            await self.task

# Usage:
async def main():
    account = MT4Account(
        user=12345,
        password="password",
        grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443"
    )
    await account.connect_by_server_name(
        server_name="YourBroker-Demo",
        base_chart_symbol="EURUSD"
    )

    monitor = PriceMonitor(account)
    await monitor.start(["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"])

    print("Monitoring... Press Ctrl+C to stop")
    await asyncio.sleep(30)  # Monitor for 30 seconds

    await monitor.stop()
    try:
        await account.channel.close()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Problem: Why Streams Need Management
docs.text:
When working with gRPC streaming in PyMT4, understanding the stream lifecycle is critical:

Stream subscriptions (on_symbol_tick, on_trade, etc.) are active async tasks with network connections that continue running until explicitly stopped.

docs.title: What Happens Without Proper Cleanup
docs.text:
# ❌ BAD: Stream continues running forever
async def bad_example():
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    count = 0
    async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(symbols=["EURUSD"]):
        count += 1
        print(f"Tick: {tick_data.symbol_tick.bid:.5f}")

        if count >= 10:
            break  # ❌ PROBLEM: Stream still running in background!
                   # ❌ PROBLEM: gRPC connection not closed!

    # ❌ Stream continues consuming resources
    # ❌ Network connection stays open
    # ❌ Memory gradually accumulates

Result:

  • Background async task continues consuming resources
  • MT4 terminal continues sending updates
  • Async task leak - tasks accumulate in event loop
  • Network connection stays open
  • Multiple abandoned streams = serious resource leak

docs.title: Pattern 1: Create cancellation_event early
docs.text:
async def proper_cancellation():
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    # ✅ CRITICAL: Create cancellation event
    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    try:
        async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(
            symbols=["EURUSD"],
            cancellation_event=cancel_event  # ✅ Pass to stream
        ):
            tick = tick_data.symbol_tick
            print(f"Price: {tick.bid:.5f}")

            if some_condition:
                cancel_event.set()  # ✅ CORRECT: Signal to stop
                break

    finally:
        # ✅ CRITICAL: Give stream time to cleanup
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(proper_cancellation())

docs.title: Pattern 2: Timeout with asyncio.wait_for
docs.text:
async def timeout_pattern():
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    try:
        async def stream_with_limit():
            async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(
                symbols=["EURUSD"],
                cancellation_event=cancel_event
            ):
                print(f"Price: {tick_data.symbol_tick.bid:.5f}")

        # ✅ Automatically stops after 30 seconds
        await asyncio.wait_for(stream_with_limit(), timeout=30.0)

    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        print("Stream reached timeout")
        cancel_event.set()

    finally:
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(timeout_pattern())

docs.title: Solution 2: Always Cleanup in finally Block ✅
docs.text: CRITICAL: Always close channel and wait for stream cleanup

docs.title: ✅ CORRECT - Proper Cleanup
docs.text:
async def proper_cleanup():
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    try:
        async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(
            symbols=["EURUSD"],
            cancellation_event=cancel_event
        ):
            # Process data...
            pass

    finally:
        # ✅ CRITICAL: Proper cleanup sequence
        # Step 1: Signal all streams to stop
        cancel_event.set()

        # Step 2: Wait for graceful cleanup (0.5-1.0 seconds)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

        # Step 3: Close gRPC channel
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(proper_cleanup())

docs.title: ❌ Mistake 1: No Cancellation Event
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG: No way to stop stream gracefully
async def bad():
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(symbols=["EURUSD"]):
        print(tick_data.symbol_tick.bid)
        # If you want to stop - YOU CAN'T stop gracefully!

Fix: 

# ✅ CORRECT: Can stop gracefully anytime
async def good():
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(
        symbols=["EURUSD"],
        cancellation_event=cancel_event
    ):
        print(tick_data.symbol_tick.bid)
        # Now can call cancel_event.set() to stop

docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG: Break doesn't cleanup resources
async def bad():
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(symbols=["EURUSD"]):
        if some_condition:
            break  # ❌ Stream still running!

    # ❌ No cleanup - resources leak!

Fix: 

# ✅ CORRECT: Proper cleanup in finally
async def good():
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    try:
        async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(
            symbols=["EURUSD"],
            cancellation_event=cancel_event
        ):
            if some_condition:
                cancel_event.set()
                break

    finally:
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)  # ✅ Cleanup time
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    finally:
        cancel_event.set()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        await account.channel.close()  # ✅ CRITICAL: Always close

docs.title: Example 1: Monitor Trade Events
docs.text:
on_trade yields OnTradeData with type (MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE) and an event_data payload (OnTadeEventData) holding four lists: new_orders, updated_orders, removed_orders and new_history_orders. Each order carries the type field (SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE: SUB_OP_BUY, SUB_OP_SELL, …).

import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_subscriptions_pb2 as sub_pb2

async def monitor_trade_events():
    """Monitor trade events and label the order operation using protobuf enums."""
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    # ✅ Operation-type enum values (SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE)
    BUY  = sub_pb2.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_BUY
    SELL = sub_pb2.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_SELL

    try:
        print("Monitoring trade events...")

        async for ev in account.on_trade(cancellation_event=cancel_event):
            data = ev.event_data

            for o in data.new_orders:
                side = "BUY" if o.type == BUY else ("SELL" if o.type == SELL else str(o.type))
                print(f"[NEW] #{o.ticket} {side} {o.symbol} @ {o.open_price:.5f} "
                      f"lots={o.lots:.2f} SL={o.stop_loss:.5f} TP={o.take_profit:.5f}")

            for upd in data.updated_orders:
                cur = upd.current
                print(f"[UPDATED] #{cur.ticket} {cur.symbol} SL={cur.stop_loss:.5f} "
                      f"TP={cur.take_profit:.5f} profit={cur.order_profit:.2f}")

            for o in data.removed_orders:
                print(f"[REMOVED] #{o.ticket} {o.symbol}")

    finally:
        cancel_event.set()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(monitor_trade_events())

docs.title: Example 2: Sort Open Orders by Profit
docs.text:
on_opened_orders_profit yields OnOpenedOrdersProfitData; the updated orders live in opened_orders_with_profit_updated, and each item exposes ticket, symbol, order_profit, lots, type, etc.

import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account

async def sort_orders_by_profit():
    """Monitor open-order P&L and sort by profit."""
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    try:
        print("Monitoring open orders (sorted by profit)...")
        print("-" * 60)

        async for profit_data in account.on_opened_orders_profit(
            timer_period_milliseconds=1000,
            cancellation_event=cancel_event
        ):
            # ✅ Collect all updated orders
            orders = list(profit_data.opened_orders_with_profit_updated)

            if not orders:
                continue

            # ✅ Sort by profit (descending - winners first)
            orders_sorted = sorted(orders, key=lambda o: o.order_profit, reverse=True)

            print(f"\n[UPDATE] Total open orders: {len(orders_sorted)}")
            print(f"{'Symbol':<10} {'Ticket':<10} {'Profit':<12} {'Status':<10}")
            print("-" * 60)

            # ✅ Show top 5 winners and top 5 losers
            for o in orders_sorted[:5]:  # Top 5 winners
                status = "✅ PROFIT" if o.order_profit > 0 else "❌ LOSS"
                print(f"{o.symbol:<10} {o.ticket:<10} {o.order_profit:>10.2f}  {status:<10}")

            if len(orders_sorted) > 10:
                print("   ... middle orders omitted ...")

            for o in orders_sorted[-5:]:  # Top 5 losers
                status = "✅ PROFIT" if o.order_profit > 0 else "❌ LOSS"
                print(f"{o.symbol:<10} {o.ticket:<10} {o.order_profit:>10.2f}  {status:<10}")

            # ✅ Calculate statistics
            total_profit = sum(o.order_profit for o in orders_sorted)
            winners = sum(1 for o in orders_sorted if o.order_profit > 0)
            losers = sum(1 for o in orders_sorted if o.order_profit < 0)

            print("-" * 60)
            print(f"Total P&L: {total_profit:+.2f} | Winners: {winners} | Losers: {losers}")

    finally:
        cancel_event.set()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(sort_orders_by_profit())

docs.title: Example 3: Filter Pending Orders by Operation Type
docs.text:
MT4 orders carry an operation type (SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE), not an MT5-style order state. Use the SUB_OP_*LIMIT / SUB_OP_*STOP values to pick out pending orders, and read updated_orders (each has previous / current) for SL/TP changes.

import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_subscriptions_pb2 as sub_pb2

async def filter_pending_orders():
    """Monitor trade events and pick out pending (limit/stop) orders."""
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    # ✅ Pending operation-type enum values
    OP = sub_pb2.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE
    PENDING = {
        OP.SUB_OP_BUYLIMIT:  "BUY LIMIT",
        OP.SUB_OP_SELLLIMIT: "SELL LIMIT",
        OP.SUB_OP_BUYSTOP:   "BUY STOP",
        OP.SUB_OP_SELLSTOP:  "SELL STOP",
    }

    try:
        print("Monitoring pending orders...")
        print("-" * 70)

        async for trade_data in account.on_trade(cancellation_event=cancel_event):
            event = trade_data.event_data

            # ✅ New orders - keep pending ones only
            for order in event.new_orders:
                label = PENDING.get(order.type)
                if label:
                    print(f"[NEW PENDING] {label} #{order.ticket}: "
                          f"{order.symbol} @ {order.open_price:.5f} "
                          f"lots={order.lots:.2f} SL={order.stop_loss:.5f}")

            # ✅ Updated orders - report SL/TP changes
            for upd in event.updated_orders:
                cur, prev = upd.current, upd.previous
                if (cur.stop_loss, cur.take_profit) != (prev.stop_loss, prev.take_profit):
                    print(f"[MODIFIED] #{cur.ticket} {cur.symbol}: "
                          f"SL {prev.stop_loss:.5f} -> {cur.stop_loss:.5f}, "
                          f"TP {prev.take_profit:.5f} -> {cur.take_profit:.5f}")

            # ✅ Removed orders (filled or cancelled)
            for order in event.removed_orders:
                print(f"[REMOVED] #{order.ticket} {order.symbol}")

    finally:
        cancel_event.set()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(filter_pending_orders())

docs.title: Example 4: Multi-Symbol Tick Aggregation with Sorting
docs.text:
import asyncio
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account

async def aggregate_and_sort_ticks():
    """
    Aggregate ticks from multiple symbols and sort by spread.
    Shows advanced data processing with multiple symbols.
    """
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    # ✅ Track latest tick for each symbol
    latest_ticks = {}
    tick_counts = defaultdict(int)

    symbols = ["EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "USDJPY", "AUDUSD", "USDCAD"]

    try:
        print(f"Monitoring {len(symbols)} symbols, sorting by spread...")
        print("-" * 80)

        update_interval = 5  # Print sorted results every 5 ticks
        total_ticks = 0

        async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(
            symbols=symbols,
            cancellation_event=cancel_event
        ):
            tick = tick_data.symbol_tick

            # ✅ Update latest tick for symbol
            latest_ticks[tick.symbol] = tick
            tick_counts[tick.symbol] += 1
            total_ticks += 1

            # ✅ Every N ticks, show sorted summary
            if total_ticks % update_interval == 0:
                print(f"\n[{datetime.now().strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] Tick Summary (sorted by spread):")
                print("-" * 80)
                print(f"{'Rank':<6} {'Symbol':<10} {'Bid':<12} {'Ask':<12} {'Spread':<10} {'Ticks':<8}")
                print("-" * 80)

                # ✅ Calculate spreads and sort
                symbol_spreads = []
                for symbol, tick in latest_ticks.items():
                    spread = tick.ask - tick.bid
                    symbol_spreads.append((symbol, tick, spread))

                # Sort by spread (ascending - tightest first)
                symbol_spreads.sort(key=lambda x: x[2])

                # ✅ Display sorted results
                for rank, (symbol, tick, spread) in enumerate(symbol_spreads, 1):
                    spread_pips = spread * 10000  # For 4-digit pairs
                    print(f"{rank:<6} {symbol:<10} {tick.bid:<12.5f} {tick.ask:<12.5f} "
                          f"{spread_pips:<10.1f} {tick_counts[symbol]:<8}")

                print("-" * 80)
                print(f"Total ticks received: {total_ticks}")

    finally:
        cancel_event.set()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(aggregate_and_sort_ticks())

docs.title: Example: Run Multiple Streams Simultaneously
docs.text:
import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account

async def multiple_concurrent_streams():
    """
    Run multiple streaming methods concurrently.
    Shows proper management of multiple streams.
    """
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    # ✅ Single cancellation event for ALL streams
    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    async def stream_ticks():
        """Monitor tick data"""
        try:
            async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(
                symbols=["EURUSD"],
                cancellation_event=cancel_event
            ):
                tick = tick_data.symbol_tick
                print(f"[TICK] {tick.symbol}: {tick.bid:.5f}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[TICK ERROR] {e}")

    async def stream_trades():
        """Monitor trade events"""
        try:
            async for trade_data in account.on_trade(cancellation_event=cancel_event):
                print(f"[TRADE] Event received: {trade_data.type}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[TRADE ERROR] {e}")

    async def stream_profits():
        """Monitor open-order profits"""
        try:
            async for profit_data in account.on_opened_orders_profit(
                timer_period_milliseconds=2000,
                cancellation_event=cancel_event
            ):
                total_orders = len(profit_data.opened_orders_with_profit_updated)
                print(f"[PROFIT] {total_orders} orders updated")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[PROFIT ERROR] {e}")

    async def auto_stop(duration: float):
        """Auto-stop after duration"""
        await asyncio.sleep(duration)
        print(f"\n[STOP] Auto-stopping after {duration} seconds...")
        cancel_event.set()

    try:
        print("Starting multiple concurrent streams...")
        print("-" * 60)

        # ✅ Run all streams concurrently
        await asyncio.gather(
            stream_ticks(),
            stream_trades(),
            stream_profits(),
            auto_stop(30.0)  # Stop all after 30 seconds
        )

    finally:
        # ✅ Ensure cancellation event is set
        cancel_event.set()

        # ✅ Wait for all streams to cleanup
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

        # ✅ Close channel
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
            print("[DONE] All streams stopped gracefully")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

asyncio.run(multiple_concurrent_streams())

docs.title: How Python Streaming Works in MT4Account
docs.text:
🔑 Critical Understanding:

ALL streaming methods (on_symbol_tick, on_trade, on_opened_orders_tickets, on_opened_orders_profit) internally use the same hidden mechanism: execute_stream_with_reconnect.

This is why: - The while loop behavior applies to ALL streaming operations - The cancellation_event mechanism is required for ALL streaming methods - Resource cleanup rules are identical for all streaming operations

Users don't see this directly - when you call account.on_symbol_tick(), internally it calls execute_stream_with_reconnect which contains the infinite reconnection loop.

Data flow:

User code (async for loop)
    ↓
Async generator (yields data)
    ↓
execute_stream_with_reconnect (background async task)
    ↓
gRPC ClientStream
    ↓
Network (to MT4 terminal)

Cancellation propagation: 

User code → cancellation_event → async generator → gRPC call → Network

When you set cancellation_event:

  1. User calls cancel_event.set() in their code
  2. While loop checks condition on next iteration: 
    while cancellation_event is None or not cancellation_event.is_set():
# After .set() → both conditions False → loop STOPS
  3. Current iteration finishes (async for yields last data)
  4. finally block executes → stream.cancel() closes gRPC stream ✅
  5. Loop breaks (no new streams created)
  6. Network connection closes
  7. Resources freed ✅

Key insight: The while loop checks cancellation_event.is_set() on each iteration. Calling .set() makes the loop exit after current stream finishes.

docs.title: MT4Account Cleanup Mechanism
docs.text:
⚠️ Important: This mechanism is internal to ALL streaming methods. When you call any streaming method (on_symbol_tick, on_trade, etc.), you're actually using execute_stream_with_reconnect behind the scenes.

The execute_stream_with_reconnect method has built-in reconnection logic with automatic stream cleanup:

# In MT4Account (real structure)
async def execute_stream_with_reconnect(..., cancellation_event):
    # ⚠️ CRITICAL: Infinite reconnection loop
    while cancellation_event is None or not cancellation_event.is_set():
        reconnect_required = False
        stream = None

        try:
            stream = stream_invoker(request, headers)
            async for response in stream:
                # Yield data to user
                yield data

        except grpc.aio.AioRpcError as ex:
            if ex.code() == grpc.StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE:
                reconnect_required = True  # Network error → try reconnect
            else:
                raise

        finally:
            if stream:
                stream.cancel()  # ✅ ALWAYS closes current gRPC stream

        # Reconnection logic
        if reconnect_required:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
            await self.reconnect()
            # ⚠️ Loop continues → creates NEW stream
        else:
            break  # Exit only here

What this means:

✅ What it DOES do: - Closes current gRPC stream automatically (in finally block) - Handles network errors with automatic reconnection - Cleans up resources for each individual stream

⚠️ What it DOESN'T do: - Stop the reconnection loop without cancellation_event - Prevent new streams from being created

Critical understanding:

# ❌ WITHOUT cancellation_event:
async for tick in account.on_symbol_tick(["EURUSD"]):  # No cancellation_event!
    if count >= 10:
        break  # User breaks → current stream closes ✅
                # BUT while loop continues → creates NEW stream ❌
                # → LEAK: orphaned stream keeps running

# ✅ WITH cancellation_event:
cancel_event = asyncio.Event()
async for tick in account.on_symbol_tick(["EURUSD"], cancellation_event=cancel_event):
    if count >= 10:
        cancel_event.set()  # Stops while loop ✅
        break               # Current stream closes ✅
                            # → CLEAN: no new streams created

Bottom line: - ✅ stream.cancel() cleans up current stream - ❌ Only cancellation_event.set() stops the reconnection while loop - 🔑 How it works: while cancellation_event is None or not cancellation_event.is_set() checks on each iteration - 🔴 Without cancellation_event → while condition is always True → loop runs forever → LEAK - 🔴 With cancellation_event but no .set() → while condition stays True → loop runs forever → LEAK - ✅ With cancellation_event.set() → while condition becomes False → loop stops → CLEAN - ✅ You MUST close channel to free gRPC connection

docs.title: ✅ DO:
docs.text:
1. Always use cancellation_event with streaming methods
  2. Always call cancel_event.set() before exiting
  3. Always use try/finally blocks for cleanup
  4. Always wait 0.5-1.0 seconds after setting cancellation_event
  5. Always close channel in finally block: await account.channel.close()
  6. Use asyncio.wait_for() for automatic timeouts
  7. Use asyncio.gather() to run multiple streams concurrently

docs.title: ❌ DON'T:
docs.text:
1. Never start streaming without cancellation_event
  2. Never break from loop without setting cancellation_event
  3. Never forget finally block with cleanup code
  4. Never skip waiting period after cancellation
  5. Never leave channel open after streaming
  6. Never ignore exceptions from streams

docs.title: Checking for Task Leaks
docs.text:
import asyncio

async def check_task_leaks():
    # Before streaming
    before = len(asyncio.all_tasks())
    print(f"Tasks before: {before}")

    # Your streaming code here...
    account = MT4Account(user=12345, password="password", grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="YourBroker-Demo", base_chart_symbol="EURUSD")

    cancel_event = asyncio.Event()

    try:
        count = 0
        async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(
            symbols=["EURUSD"],
            cancellation_event=cancel_event
        ):
            count += 1
            if count >= 5:
                break

    finally:
        cancel_event.set()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        try:
            await account.channel.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Disconnect warning: {e}")

    # After streaming (wait a bit for cleanup)
    await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
    after = len(asyncio.all_tasks())
    print(f"Tasks after: {after}")
    print(f"Leaked tasks: {after - before}")
    # Should be 0-1 if properly cleaned up

asyncio.run(check_task_leaks())

docs.title: Debugging Pending Tasks
docs.text:
import asyncio

async def debug_pending_tasks():
    # Get all tasks
    tasks = asyncio.all_tasks()

    print(f"Total pending tasks: {len(tasks)}")
    print("-" * 60)

    for i, task in enumerate(tasks, 1):
        print(f"Task {i}: {task.get_name()}")
        print(f"  Coro: {task.get_coro()}")
        print(f"  Done: {task.done()}")
        if not task.done():
            print(f"  ⚠️  STILL RUNNING!")
        print()

docs.title: Common Leak Patterns
docs.text:
1. Not using cancellation_event: 

    # ❌ Leak: stream never stops
async for data in account.on_symbol_tick(symbols=["EURUSD"]):
    # Forgot cancellation_event parameter
    pass

  2. Not setting cancellation_event: 

    # ❌ Leak: stream keeps running after break
cancel_event = asyncio.Event()
async for data in account.on_symbol_tick(symbols=["EURUSD"], cancellation_event=cancel_event):
    if condition:
        break  # Forgot cancel_event.set()

  3. Not closing channel: 

    # ❌ Leak: connection stays open
cancel_event.set()
await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
# Forgot await account.channel.close()

docs.title: MT4 for Beginners: Your First Steps in Trading
docs.text: Welcome! This guide is designed for complete beginners who have never worked with MetaTrader 4 or trading. We'll walk you through everything you need to know to get started.

docs.title: What is MetaTrader 4 (MT4)?
docs.text:
MetaTrader 4 is a powerful trading platform used by millions of traders worldwide. It allows you to:

  • Trade forex, stocks, commodities, and cryptocurrencies
  • Analyze markets with charts and indicators
  • Execute automated trading strategies
  • Monitor your positions in real-time

Think of MT4 as your "cockpit" for accessing financial markets. PyMT4 allows you to programmatically control this cockpit using Python.

docs.title: Demo vs Live Account: Start Safely
Why start with a demo account?
docs.text:
A demo account is a risk-free practice account with virtual money. We strongly recommend starting with demo for several reasons:

  • ✅ Zero risk - practice with virtual funds (typically $10,000 - $100,000)
  • ✅ Real market conditions - live prices and market behavior
  • ✅ Learn the platform - understand how MT4 works before risking real money
  • ✅ Test your code - perfect for developing and testing your PyMT4 applications

docs.title: Live Account
docs.text:
A live account uses your real money. Only move to live trading when you:

  • Understand how MT4 works
  • Have thoroughly tested your strategies on demo
  • Are aware of the risks involved

docs.title: Quick Start: Creating a Demo Account
docs.text: The fastest way to get started is to create a demo account directly through the MT4 terminal application.

docs.title: Step 1️⃣: Download and Install MT4 Terminal
docs.text:
1. Visit the official MetaTrader 4 website: https://www.metatrader4.com/en/download

  2. Download the version for your operating system (Windows/Mac/Linux)

  3. Install the application

docs.title: Step 2️⃣: Launch MT4 and Locate the Navigator Panel
docs.text:
When you open the MetaTrader 4 application, you'll typically see a popup window offering to:

  • Register for the MQL community

  • Open a new account or log into an existing one

If this popup doesn't appear automatically, you need to find the Navigator panel.

Finding the Navigator Panel:

The Navigator panel is usually located on the left side of the screen, below the Market Watch panel.

Inside the Navigator panel you'll see several sections: - Accounts - Subscriptions - Indicators - Expert Advisors - And others

docs.title: Step 3️⃣: Opening a New Demo Account
docs.text:
1. In the Navigator panel, find the Accounts section
  2. Right-click on "Accounts"
  3. Select "Open an account" from the context menu

This will open the broker server search panel.

docs.title: Step 4️⃣: Select MetaQuotes Demo Server
docs.text:
In the broker search window, you'll see a list of available MT4 servers.

For your first demo account, we'll use the simplest option:

  • Look for "MetaQuotes-Demo" or "MetaQuotes Ltd" in the list
  • This is the standard demo server provided by MetaTrader developers
  • If you don't see it immediately, use the search field at the top to find it

Select the MetaQuotes server and click Next.

docs.title: Step 5️⃣: Account Type Selection
docs.text:
On the next screen, you'll have options:

  • Open a new demo account (top option)
  • Log into an existing account (demo or live)

Select "Open a new demo account" and click Next.

docs.title: Step 6️⃣: Fill in Your Personal Information
docs.text:
Now you'll see a form requesting your details:

  • Name: Your first name
  • Last Name: Your last name
  • Email: Your email address
  • Phone: Optional (can skip for demo)
  • Account Type: Choose your preferred account settings
  • Deposit: Virtual amount (e.g., $10,000)
  • Leverage: 1:100 is a good starting point
  • Currency: USD, EUR, etc.

Check the box to agree to the terms and conditions, then click Next.

docs.title: Step 7️⃣: Save Your Account Credentials
docs.text:
MT4 will now create your demo account and display your credentials:

Important credentials displayed:

  • Login: Your account number (e.g., 591129415)
  • Password: Your master password for trading
  • Investor Password: Read-only password (for monitoring)
  • Server: Server name (e.g., "MetaQuotes-Demo")

⚠️ CRITICALLY IMPORTANT: Save these credentials immediately! You'll need them for: - Logging back into MT4 - Configuring PyMT4 in examples/0_common/settings.json

Click Finish to complete account creation.

docs.title: Step 8️⃣: Configure PyMT4 with Your Credentials
docs.text:
Now that you have an MT4 demo account, you need to configure PyMT4 to connect to it.

  1. Open your PyMT4 project
  2. Navigate to examples/0_common/settings.json
  3. Fill in the credentials you just saved:
{
  "user": 591129415,
  "password": "YourPasswordHere",
  "grpc_server": "mt4.mrpc.pro:443",
  "mt_cluster": "MetaQuotes-Demo",
  "test_symbol": "EURUSD",
  "test_volume": 0.01,
  "api_key": "TRIAL"
}

Important notes:

  • user: Replace with your login number
  • password: Replace with your password
  • mt_cluster: Use the exact server name from MT4 (e.g., "MetaQuotes-Demo")
  • grpc_server: MetaRPC gateway address — leave as is for the demo
  • api_key: "TRIAL" works out of the box (1 terminal per IP); use your key from mrpc.pro/my to lift the limit

docs.title: Step 9️⃣: Verify MT4 Connection
docs.text:
Back in the MT4 terminal:

  1. MT4 should automatically log you into your new demo account
  2. Check the bottom right corner of the terminal window - you should see:
  3. Green connection indicator (means connected to server)
  4. Your account balance (e.g., $10,000)

You're now ready to test!

docs.title: Step 🔟: Start Testing PyMT4
docs.text:
With your MT4 demo account created and settings.json configured, you can start running examples:

# Navigate to the examples folder
cd examples

# Run your first example
python main.py 1

# Or run interactively
python main.py

When trading operations occur, your demo account balance will increase or decrease accordingly. Experiment freely - it's virtual money, so there's no risk!

All trades executed by PyMT4 will appear in your MT4 terminal in real-time.

docs.title: 🧩 Understanding MT4 Password Types
docs.text: MT4 uses two types of passwords for security and flexibility:

docs.title: Master Password (Main Password)
docs.text:
• Full access to your trading account
  • Can open/close trades, deposit/withdraw funds, change settings
  • This is the password you created during account registration
  • Use this password for:
  • Trading (including PyMT4 applications)
  • Changing account settings
  • Withdrawing funds (live accounts)

docs.title: Investor Password (Read-Only Password)
docs.text:
• View-only access to your account
  • Can see trades, balance, history - but cannot trade
  • Useful for:
  • Sharing your trading performance with others (investors, friends)
  • Monitoring your account without risk
  • Audit and analytics tools

How to get your investor password:

  1. In MT4, go to Tools → Options
  2. Select the Server tab
  3. Click Change next to "Investor Password"
  4. Set a new investor password

docs.title: Choosing a Broker (Optional)
docs.text:
While you can use the MetaQuotes demo server for practice, you may want to choose a specific broker for:

  • Live trading later
  • Better demo conditions (spreads, instruments)
  • Specific regional support

docs.title: Popular MT4 Brokers:
docs.text:
Note: This is not financial advice. Always do your own research before choosing a broker.

  • IC Markets - Popular for forex and low spreads
  • Pepperstone - Well-regulated, beginner-friendly
  • OANDA - Strong reputation, accepts US clients
  • XM - Easy account opening, many account types
  • RoboForex - Good for automated trading
  • FxPro - Excellent demo trading conditions

docs.title: What to look for:
docs.text:
• ✅ Regulation - Check if regulated by FCA, ASIC, CySEC, etc.

  • ✅ MT4 Support - Make sure they offer MetaTrader 4 (not only MT5).

  • ✅ Demo Account - Free demo without expiration (though demo accounts typically last 30 days, then become inactive).

  • ✅ Good Spreads - Lower spreads = lower trading costs.

  • ✅ Customer Support - Responsive support in your language.

docs.title: What's Next?
docs.text: Now that you have a demo account and understand the basics, you're ready for:

docs.title: 1. Setting Up PyMT4
docs.text:
Follow our main getting started guide to connect PyMT4 to your MT4 account:

👉 Getting Started with PyMT4

docs.title: 2. Understanding API Architecture
docs.text: PyMT4 is built in three levels, from low-level to high-level. You can choose where to start depending on your needs:

docs.title: Level 1: MT4Account (Low-Level gRPC Foundation)
docs.text:
👉 MT4Account Overview

  • Direct gRPC calls to MT4 terminal
  • Foundation of everything - all other levels use this internally
  • Maximum control and flexibility
  • Best for: Advanced users who need fine-grained control

docs.title: Level 2: MT4Service (Convenient Wrappers)
docs.text:
👉 MT4Service Overview

  • Wrapper methods over MT4Account gRPC calls
  • Simplified error handling and response parsing
  • Easier to work with than raw gRPC
  • Best for: Most common trading scenarios

docs.title: Level 3: MT4Sugar (High-Level Helpers)
docs.text:
👉 MT4Sugar API Overview

  • Syntactic sugar and convenience methods
  • Chainable operations, smart defaults
  • Most intuitive and beginner-friendly
  • Best for: Rapid prototyping and simple strategies

docs.title: 🛡️ Security
docs.text:
• Never share your master password with anyone
  • Use investor password for monitoring/analytics tools
  • Keep your credentials safe (use password managers)

docs.title: 📊 Risk Management
docs.text:
• Demo accounts are risk-free, but form good habits:
  • Always use Stop Loss
  • Don't risk more than 1-2% per trade
  • Understand position sizing calculations

docs.title: 🧪 Testing
docs.text:
• Test all your PyMT4 code on demo first
  • Verify strategies over weeks/months, not days
  • Paper trading (demo) doesn't guarantee live results

docs.title: 📚 Education
docs.text:
• Trading has a steep learning curve
  • Focus on learning, not earning
  • Consider courses, books, and communities

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Install PyMT4 package with all dependencies
pip install MetaRpcMT4

docs.title: Running Examples
docs.text:
# Navigate to examples folder first
cd examples

# Option 1: Run specific example by number
python main.py 1

# Option 2: Interactive menu
python main.py

# Option 3: Run example file directly
python 1_lowlevel/01_general_operations.py
python 3_sugar/06_sugar_basics.py

docs.title: Checking Environment
docs.text:
# Verify Python version (requires 3.8+)
python --version

Ready to start coding? Head over to Getting Started to connect PyMT4 to your MT4 account!

Good luck with your trading journey! 🚀

docs.title: 🗺️ PyMT4 Project Map
docs.text: The whole project as one annotated tree, with links. Links point to section overviews, never to individual method pages — open an overview to drill down into its methods.

docs.title: 🧱 The three layers
docs.text:
PyMT4 is built in three decoupled layers. Your code can enter at any level.

Layer Source What it does Overview 3 · MT4Sugar app/MT4Sugar.py Convenience on top of Service: pips-based SL/TP, risk-based sizing, price/volume normalization, trailing/breakeven, batch close/cancel, watchers. MT4Sugar overview 2 · MT4Service app/MT4Service.py Typed facade: friendly signatures (string timeframes, masks, sort), unpacked Python data (no raw proto). What most code uses. MT4Service overview 1 · MT4Account package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py Low-level gRPC: proto request/reply, connect/session, auto-reconnect, streaming. Everything else builds on it. MT4Account overview 
Your code  →  MT4Sugar  →  MT4Service  →  MT4Account  →  gRPC  →  MetaRPC gateway → MT4 terminal

docs.text:
• PyMT4/ — repo root (SDK layers + runnable demo project)
  • app/ — the mid/high-level layers

    • MT4Sugar.py — Layer 3 source → MT4Sugar overview
    • Helper/ — errors.py (domain exceptions), rate_limit.py
  • package/MetaRpcMT4/ — low-level gRPC layer (vendored)
    • mt4_account.py — Layer 1 source → MT4Account overview
    • *_pb2.py / *_pb2_grpc.py — generated gRPC / protobuf stubs (the raw contract)
  • Strategy/ — the strategy library (imported by the orchestrator examples)
    • orchestrator/ — the five orchestrators → Strategies overview
    • presets/ — strategy & risk presets
  • examples/ — runnable demos (the numbered menu), launched from main.py
    • main.py — interactive menu / CLI runner → Getting Started
    • 0_common/ — shared helpers (demo_helpers.py, progress_bar.py) + settings.json (your MT4 credentials) · protobuf inspector (18) → Protobuf Inspector
    • 1_lowlevel/ — 01–03 → MT4Account overview
    • 2_service/ — 04 → MT4Service overview
    • 3_sugar/ — 06–08 → MT4Sugar overview
    • 4_orchestrators/ — 11–16 → Strategies overview
    • 5_usercode/ — 17 → UserCode Sandbox
  • docs/ — this documentation site (see the map below)

docs.text:
• docs/
  • Home — landing page
  • All_Guides/ — the guides (Getting Started, Your First Project, Glossary, Sync vs Async, gRPC Streaming, ENUMs, Return Codes, …); browse them in the left nav or on the docs site
  • MT4Account/ — low-level gRPC docs → overview (per-method pages inside)
  • MT4Service/ — typed facade docs → overview (per-group pages inside)

The MT4Account/, MT4Service/, MT4Sugar/ and Strategies/ folders hold the detail pages. By design this map links only their overviews — each overview is the index into its own pages.

docs.title: 🎯 Which layer should you use?
docs.text:
• Most trading apps → MT4Sugar. Pips-based SL/TP, risk sizing and auto-normalization protect you from off-quote and invalid-volume rejections.
  • Custom execution → MT4Service. Typed calls when you manage your own sizing/normalization.
  • Protocol-level control → MT4Account. Raw proto structures and streams.

docs.title: Protobuf Inspector - Interactive Type Explorer
docs.text: Interactive developer utility for exploring MT4 protobuf types, fields, enums, and data structures from the MT4 gRPC API

docs.title: 🏛️ What This Tool Does
docs.text:
The Protobuf Inspector is an interactive command-line tool that helps you explore the structure of the MT4 gRPC API:

  • Interactive search for types, fields, and enums
  • Inspection of protobuf message structures
  • Field-level discovery - find which types contain a specific field
  • Field type discovery - find fields by their data type (double, string, enum, etc.)
  • Enum value exploration - see all possible enum values
  • Enum usage tracking - find where a specific enum is used
  • Type browsing with filters
  • JSON export - export type structures for documentation
  • Statistics - field types, enum counts, comprehensive metrics

It is offline — it reads the generated MetaRpcMT4 protobuf descriptors, so no MT4 connection is required.

docs.title: Running the Inspector
docs.text:
cd examples
python main.py inspect

You will see an interactive prompt:

===========================================================
MT4 PROTOBUF TYPES INSPECTOR
===========================================================

  Discovered 193 protobuf message types
  Discovered 18 enum types

  Type 'help' to see available commands
  Type 'list' to see all types
===========================================================

>

Show help message help exit / quit / q Exit the inspector exit
