docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text:
The Protobuf Inspector uses Python reflection to:

  1. Register all protobuf types at startup
  2. Build in-memory indexes (field name → types, field type → fields, enum → usage)
  3. Provide instant search and lookup
  4. Export to JSON with complete metadata

Source file: examples/0_common/16_protobuf_inspector.py

Modules scanned:

  • mt4_term_api_account_helper_pb2
  • mt4_term_api_trade_stats_pb2
  • mt4_term_api_market_info_pb2
  • mt4_term_api_admin_pb2
  • mt4_term_api_trading_helper_pb2
  • mt4_term_api_subscriptions_pb2 (streaming events)
  • mt4_term_api_charts_pb2 (chart / EA operations)
  • mt4_term_api_connection_pb2 (connection management)

docs.title: Technical Notes
docs.text:
• No MT4 connection required — purely offline; it inspects type definitions.
  • Instant search — in-memory indexes for fast lookup.
  • Development only — not intended for production use.
  • Python reflection — uses the protobuf DESCRIPTOR API for introspection.
  • JSON export — compatible with external documentation tools.

docs.title: When to Use This Tool
docs.text:
Use the inspector when:

  • Learning the MT4 gRPC API structure
  • Debugging "field not found" errors
  • Exploring available protobuf types
  • Looking up enum values
  • Finding the correct request/response types for an API call
  • Understanding message structures before writing code

Don't use for:

  • Inspecting runtime data (use a debugger instead)
  • Production code (this is a development tool)
  • Testing API connectivity (use a demo connection instead)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Q: Type not found

> PositionInfo
[!] Type 'PositionInfo' not found

A: That's an MT5-style name; it doesn't exist in MT4. Use search with a partial name (e.g. search Order) to find the right MT4 type.

Q: What's the difference between the *Request, *Reply, *Data, *Info types?

  • *Request — input for an API method (what you send)
  • *Reply — the full response envelope (wraps data or error)
  • *Data — the payload inside a reply (e.g. OrderSendData, AccountSummaryData)
  • *Info — a structured record inside a payload (e.g. OpenedOrderInfo, HistoryOrderInfo)

Q: Which fields are double vs int32?

> findtype double    # prices, volumes, profits
> findtype int32     # tickets, magic numbers, indices
> findtype string    # symbols, comments

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The Protobuf Inspector is a handy first stop when working with the MT4 gRPC API. Use it to:

  1. Discover available types and their structure
  2. Learn message field names and types
  3. Debug field-name and type issues
  4. Verify enum values and usage
  5. Export JSON documentation for your team

Remember: type help at any time for the command reference.

docs.title: MT4 Error / Return Codes Reference - Python
🛡️ How MT4 reports errors
docs.text:
Unlike MT5 (which returns a numeric returned_code / TRADE_RETCODE_* on every trade result), MT4 reports failures as Python exceptions. A trading call either:

  • succeeds — and returns its data (e.g. order_send returns a ticket), or
  • fails — and raises an exception carrying a structured error.

There is no returned_code field and no TRADE_RETCODE_* constants in PyMT4. The classic MQL4 error codes live in the MqlErrorCode enum (see below).

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import ApiExceptionMT4

try:
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)
    print(f"✓ Order opened: #{ticket}")
except ApiExceptionMT4 as e:
    # e.error is the structured protobuf Error
    print(f"✗ Trade failed: {e.error.mql_error_description} "
          f"(code {e.error.mql_error_int_code})")

Key point: no exception = the trade went through; an exception tells you why it did not.

docs.title: Where do the codes come from?
docs.text: The error codes are the standard MQL4 error codes, defined in the protobuf enum MqlErrorCode inside package/MetaRpcMT4/mrpc_mt4_error_pb2.py. They are returned by the trading server and mirror the codes GetLastError() returns inside an MQL4 EA.

docs.title: How errors surface in the API
Low level — MT4Account
docs.text:
MT4Account raises two exception types (defined in MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account):

Exception When ConnectExceptionMT4 A method was called before connect_by_server_name / connect_by_host_port ApiExceptionMT4 The server returned an error for the request

ApiExceptionMT4.error is a protobuf Error message with these fields:

Field Type Meaning type ErrorType High-level category: MRPC, MRPC_VALIDATION, MRPC_TIMEOUT, TERMINAL_API_TIMEOUT, … error_code string Gateway error code (e.g. GETTING_CONNECTION_EX_DATA_FROM_INCOMING_REQUEST_ERROR) error_message string Human-readable gateway message mql_error_code MqlErrorCode Symbolic MQL4 error (e.g. ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY) mql_error_int_code int Numeric MQL4 error (e.g. 134) mql_error_description string Description of the MQL4 error stack_trace string Server-side stack trace (diagnostics) command_type_name string Which RPC produced the error

docs.title: High level — MT4Service / MT4Sugar
docs.text:
The Sugar layer translates backend errors into domain exceptions from app/Helper/errors.py:

Exception Raised for (by context) OrderRejected order_send / place_order failures ModifyRejected order_modify / order_close_delete / order_close_by failures ConnectivityError reconnect / session / handshake issues RateLimitExceeded client-side rate-limit guard tripped MT4Error base class / anything else

Each MT4Error has optional .code and .details attributes, and its message wraps the original low-level error.

docs.title: Trade server & common codes
docs.text:
Code Constant Meaning 0 ERR_NO_ERROR No error (success) 1 ERR_NO_RESULT No error, but result unknown 2 ERR_COMMON_ERROR Common error 3 ERR_INVALID_TRADE_PARAMETERS Invalid trade parameters 4 ERR_SERVER_BUSY Trade server is busy 5 ERR_OLD_VERSION Old terminal version 6 ERR_NO_CONNECTION No connection to trade server 7 ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_RIGHTS Not enough rights 8 ERR_TOO_FREQUENT_REQUESTS Too frequent requests 9 ERR_MALFUNCTIONAL_TRADE Malfunctional trade operation 64 ERR_ACCOUNT_DISABLED Account disabled 65 ERR_INVALID_ACCOUNT Invalid account 128 ERR_TRADE_TIMEOUT Trade timeout 129 ERR_INVALID_PRICE Invalid price 130 ERR_INVALID_STOPS Invalid stops (SL/TP too close to price) 131 ERR_INVALID_TRADE_VOLUME Invalid trade volume 132 ERR_MARKET_CLOSED Market is closed 133 ERR_TRADE_DISABLED Trading is disabled 134 ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY Not enough money 135 ERR_PRICE_CHANGED Price changed 136 ERR_OFF_QUOTES Off quotes (no prices) 137 ERR_BROKER_BUSY Broker is busy 138 ERR_REQUOTE Requote 139 ERR_ORDER_LOCKED Order is locked 140 ERR_LONG_POSITIONS_ONLY_ALLOWED Only long positions allowed 141 ERR_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS Too many requests 145 ERR_TRADE_MODIFY_DENIED Modification denied (order too close to market) 146 ERR_TRADE_CONTEXT_BUSY Trade context is busy 147 ERR_TRADE_EXPIRATION_DENIED Expiration setting denied by broker 148 ERR_TRADE_TOO_MANY_ORDERS Too many open orders / pending orders 149 ERR_TRADE_HEDGE_PROHIBITED Hedging prohibited 150 ERR_TRADE_PROHIBITED_BY_FIFO Prohibited by FIFO rule

Codes 4000+ (ERR_NO_MQLERROR, ERR_ZERO_DIVIDE, …) are MQL4 runtime errors and rarely appear for API trading. The full enum has 112 entries — introspect MqlErrorCode in mrpc_mt4_error_pb2 for the complete list.

docs.title: Low level (MT4Account)
docs.text:
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import ApiExceptionMT4
from MetaRpcMT4 import mrpc_mt4_error_pb2 as err_pb2

try:
    result = await account.order_send(request)
    print(f"✓ Order #{result.ticket} @ {result.price:.5f}")
except ApiExceptionMT4 as e:
    code = e.error.mql_error_int_code
    if code == err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY:   # 134
        print("Not enough money — reduce volume or add margin")
    elif code == err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_MARKET_CLOSED:    # 132
        print("Market is closed — try during trading hours")
    else:
        print(f"Trade failed: {e.error.mql_error_description} (code {code})")

docs.title: High level (MT4Sugar)
docs.text:
from app.Helper.errors import OrderRejected, MT4Error

try:
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("GBPUSD", lots=0.5)
    print(f"✓ Order #{ticket} opened")
except OrderRejected as e:
    print(f"Order rejected: {e}")      # message wraps the server error
    print(f"details: {e.details}")     # payload (symbol, lots, …)
except MT4Error as e:
    print(f"SDK error: {e}")

docs.title: Retrying transient errors
docs.text:
Some codes are temporary and safe to retry (ideally with a short backoff):

ERR_SERVER_BUSY (4), ERR_NO_CONNECTION (6), ERR_TOO_FREQUENT_REQUESTS (8), ERR_TRADE_TIMEOUT (128), ERR_PRICE_CHANGED (135), ERR_OFF_QUOTES (136), ERR_BROKER_BUSY (137), ERR_REQUOTE (138), ERR_TRADE_CONTEXT_BUSY (146), ERR_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS (141).

import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import ApiExceptionMT4
from MetaRpcMT4 import mrpc_mt4_error_pb2 as err_pb2

RETRYABLE = {
    err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_SERVER_BUSY,
    err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_NO_CONNECTION,
    err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_TOO_FREQUENT_REQUESTS,
    err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_TRADE_TIMEOUT,
    err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_PRICE_CHANGED,
    err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_OFF_QUOTES,
    err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_BROKER_BUSY,
    err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_REQUOTE,
    err_pb2.MqlErrorCode.ERR_TRADE_CONTEXT_BUSY,
}

async def buy_with_retry(sugar, symbol, lots, max_retries=3):
    for attempt in range(1, max_retries + 1):
        try:
            return await sugar.buy_market(symbol, lots=lots)
        except ApiExceptionMT4 as e:
            if e.error.mql_error_int_code in RETRYABLE and attempt < max_retries:
                await asyncio.sleep(attempt)   # 1s, 2s, …
                continue
            raise
    raise RuntimeError(f"failed after {max_retries} attempts")

Permanent errors (don't retry): ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY (134), ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130), ERR_INVALID_TRADE_VOLUME (131), ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132), ERR_TRADE_DISABLED (133). Fix the request or conditions.

docs.title: ✅ DO
docs.text:
1. Wrap trading calls in try/except — that's how MT4 reports failures.
  2. Inspect e.error.mql_error_int_code to branch on the exact reason.
  3. Use the MqlErrorCode enum instead of magic numbers (ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY, not 134).
  4. Retry only transient codes with a short backoff.

docs.title: ❌ DON'T
docs.text:
1. Don't poll a returned_code — MT4 has none; a returned ticket already means success.
  2. Don't retry permanent errors (insufficient money, invalid stops, market closed).
  3. Don't swallow exceptions silently — log e.error.mql_error_description.

docs.title: Quick Reference Table
docs.text: Category Codes Action Success 0 (ERR_NO_ERROR) + a returned ticket Continue Transient 4, 6, 8, 128, 135, 136, 137, 138, 141, 146 Retry with delay Invalid request 3, 129, 130, 131 Fix parameters Restrictions 132, 133, 140, 149, 150 Check trading conditions Limits 134, 148 Reduce volume / close orders Account / rights 7, 64, 65 Check account & permissions

docs.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Methods - When to Use What (Python)
docs.text: Understanding the execution model in PyMT4: it is async-first, and how to drive it from scripts, notebooks and bots.

docs.title: 🎯 The short version
docs.text:
PyMT4 is asynchronous end-to-end. Every network method on MT4Account, MT4Service and MT4Sugar is an async def and must be await-ed inside an asyncio event loop. There are no blocking synchronous network wrappers — the only non-async members are small local helpers (config setters like set_defaults, pure calculations like breakeven_price).

So "sync vs async" in PyMT4 is really two practical questions:

  1. How do I run the event loop? — asyncio.run(...) in a script, direct await in a notebook (Jupyter/IPython already runs a loop).
  2. Sequential or concurrent? — plain await calls run one after another; asyncio.gather and async for streams run work concurrently.

docs.title: 🧭 Choosing a pattern
docs.text: Aspect Sequential await Concurrent (gather / streaming) Thread blocking Non-blocking (awaits yield the loop) Non-blocking Throughput One operation at a time Many operations / events in flight Real-time data ⚠️ Not ideal for continuous streams ✅ Perfect for tick & trade streams Simplicity Simplest, linear to read Needs care with ordering/cancellation Use for Scripts, notebooks, one-offs Bots, multi-symbol trading, services

docs.title: ▶️ Running from a script
docs.text:
Use asyncio.run() to start the loop, then await inside:

import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account

async def main():
    account = MT4Account(user=user, password=password, grpc_server=grpc_server)
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name, base_chart_symbol="EURUSD", timeout_seconds=30)
    summary = await account.account_summary()
    print(f"Balance: {summary.account_balance}, Equity: {summary.account_equity}")
    await account.channel.close()

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: 📓 Running from a notebook (Jupyter / IPython)
docs.text:
A notebook already runs an event loop, so you await directly — do not call asyncio.run() (it would error with "event loop is already running"):

account = MT4Account(user=user, password=password, grpc_server=grpc_server)
await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name, base_chart_symbol="EURUSD", timeout_seconds=30)
summary = await account.account_summary()
print(summary.account_balance)

docs.title: 1. Market data streaming
docs.text:
Ticks arrive continuously. Consume them with async for so your loop never blocks:

cancel = asyncio.Event()
async for tick_data in account.on_symbol_tick(["EURUSD"], cancellation_event=cancel):
    tick = tick_data.symbol_tick
    print(f"{tick.symbol}: Bid={tick.bid:.5f} Ask={tick.ask:.5f}")

See gRPC Stream Management for cancellation and cleanup.

docs.title: 2. Concurrent requests across symbols
docs.text:
Run independent calls at the same time with asyncio.gather instead of awaiting them one by one:

eur, gbp, usdjpy = await asyncio.gather(
    sugar.last_quote("EURUSD"),
    sugar.last_quote("GBPUSD"),
    sugar.last_quote("USDJPY"),
)

docs.title: 💡 Summary
docs.text:
• Everything that touches the network is async — always await it.
  • In a script, wrap your code in async def and launch with asyncio.run().
  • In a notebook, await directly (the loop already exists).
  • Reach for asyncio.gather and async for when you need concurrency or live streams.

docs.title: What is this?
docs.text: This is your sandbox for writing custom MT4 trading code in Python. Connection setup is already done - you only need to add your trading logic!

docs.title: 🏁 Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Already wired into main.py
  2. Open examples/main.py

  3. Entry 17 ("Your sandbox") is ready to use

  4. Open examples/5_usercode/17_usercode.py

  5. Write your code or uncomment the examples inside run_user_code(account, service, sugar)

  6. Run: 

    cd examples
python main.py usercode

That's it! Your code runs with a live MT4 connection already established.

docs.title: How to use
docs.text:
The sandbox hands you three ready objects inside run_user_code(account, service, sugar):

  • account - low-level gRPC client (MT4Account)
  • service - typed facade (MT4Service)
  • sugar - high-level helpers (MT4Sugar)

docs.title: Option 1: Uncomment an example
docs.text:
# q = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")
# print(f"EURUSD: Bid={q['bid']:.5f} Ask={q['ask']:.5f}")

Just remove # to activate.

docs.title: Available commands
docs.text:
# From the examples directory
python main.py usercode
python main.py 17
python main.py user
python main.py sandbox

docs.title: What's already configured
docs.text:
• Connection - MT4 terminal connected via gRPC
  • Configuration - loaded from examples/0_common/settings.json
  • account - low-level gRPC client (MT4Account)
  • service - typed facade (MT4Service)
  • sugar - high-level Sugar API (MT4Sugar)
  • async/await - all methods are asynchronous

docs.title: 🧩 Can I mix API levels?
docs.text:
Yes! All three objects talk to the same connection:

# Low-level (direct gRPC protobuf)
summary = await account.account_summary()
balance_pb = summary.account_balance

# Mid-level (MT4Service) - same protobuf object, via the facade
summary_svc = await service.account_summary()
balance_svc = summary_svc.account_balance

# High-level (MT4Sugar) - convenience helpers
q = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")
  • account - for full control (gRPC protobuf)
  • service - the typed facade over MT4Account
  • sugar - for the simplest one-liners

docs.title: Get account information
docs.text:
# Account state comes from account_summary() (protobuf object)
summary = await service.account_summary()
print(f"Balance: {summary.account_balance:.2f} {summary.account_currency}")
print(f"Equity:  {summary.account_equity:.2f}")
print(f"Free margin: {summary.account_margin_free:.2f}")

docs.title: Get current price
docs.text:
# Sugar API
q = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")          # {"bid": ..., "ask": ..., "time": ...}
print(f"EURUSD: Bid={q['bid']:.5f}, Ask={q['ask']:.5f}")
mid = await sugar.mid_price("EURUSD")

# Service API
tick = await service.quote("EURUSD")
print(f"EURUSD Bid: {tick.bid:.5f}, Ask: {tick.ask:.5f}")

docs.title: Open market order
docs.text:
# Sugar API (lots is keyword-only)
try:
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)
    print(f"Order opened: #{ticket}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Order failed: {e}")

# With SL/TP in pips
ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=30)

# Lot size based on risk (2% with 50-pip SL)
lots = await sugar.calc_lot_by_risk("EURUSD", risk_percent=2.0, stop_pips=50)
ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=lots, sl_pips=50, tp_pips=100)

docs.title: Place pending order
docs.text:
# Buy Limit with absolute price and SL/TP in pips
ticket = await sugar.buy_limit("EURUSD", price=1.0850, lots=0.01, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=30)

# Buy Stop with absolute price
ticket = await sugar.buy_stop("EURUSD", price=1.0950, lots=0.01)

# Sell Limit with absolute SL/TP prices
ticket = await sugar.sell_limit("EURUSD", price=1.1050, lots=0.01,
                                sl_price=1.1070, tp_price=1.1030)

docs.title: List open orders
docs.text:
# Sugar API - returns a list of dicts
orders = await sugar.find_orders(symbol="EURUSD")
print(f"Open orders: {len(orders)}")
for o in orders:
    print(o)

# Service API - low-level protobuf
data = await service.opened_orders()
for o in data.order_infos:
    print(f"  #{o.ticket} {o.symbol} {o.lots:.2f} lot, profit: {o.profit:.2f}")

docs.title: Close orders
docs.text:
# Close a specific order (market) or delete a pending one
await sugar.close(ticket)

# Close all orders for a symbol
await sugar.close_all(symbol="EURUSD")

# Close all orders (all symbols)
await sugar.close_all()

# Cancel pending orders only
await sugar.cancel_pendings(symbol="EURUSD")

docs.title: Modify order
docs.text:
# Modify SL/TP by absolute prices
await sugar.modify_sl_tp_by_price(ticket, sl_price=1.0850, tp_price=1.0950)

# Modify SL/TP by pips relative to entry
await sugar.modify_sl_tp_by_pips(ticket, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=40)

docs.title: Calculate lot size
docs.text:
# Lot size based on risk
lots = await sugar.calc_lot_by_risk("EURUSD", risk_percent=2.0, stop_pips=20)
print(f"Lots for 2% risk with 20-pip SL: {lots:.2f}")

# Then use it
ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=lots)

docs.title: ℹ️ Error handling
docs.text:
PyMT4 surfaces failures as Python exceptions (there is no MT5-style returned_code to poll). Order helpers return the ticket number on success.

  • MT4Account raises ApiExceptionMT4 on server errors, ConnectExceptionMT4 if you call a method before connecting.
  • MT4Sugar raises MT4Error subclasses (OrderRejected, ModifyRejected, ConnectivityError, RateLimitExceeded).

docs.title: Recommended pattern
docs.text:
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import ApiExceptionMT4
from app.Helper.errors import OrderRejected, MT4Error

try:
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)
    print(f"[OK] Order opened: #{ticket}")
except OrderRejected as e:
    print(f"[X] Order rejected: {e}")
except (ApiExceptionMT4, MT4Error) as e:
    print(f"[X] Error: {e}")

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
1. Start simple - uncomment one example at a time
  2. Use Sugar API - buy_market(..., sl_pips=, tp_pips=) and calc_lot_by_risk() are easier than low-level calls
  3. Handle exceptions - wrap trading calls in try/except
  4. Test on demo - make sure you're on a demo account first
  5. Read the docs - RETURN_CODES_REFERENCE.md explains error codes
  6. Use async/await - all methods are asynchronous
  7. Type hints - rely on IDE autocomplete
  8. Check the examples - the examples/ folder has a full set of working examples

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
[X] Forgot to use await 

q = sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")  # DON'T forget await!

[+] Always use await 

q = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")

[X] Passing lots positionally 

ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.01)  # lots is keyword-only!

[+] Pass lots as a keyword 

ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)

[X] Not handling exceptions 

ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)  # no try/except!

[+] Always handle exceptions 

try:
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)
    print(f"Order opened: #{ticket}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")

docs.text:

  • Error codes: see RETURN_CODES_REFERENCE.md
  • Examples: check the examples/ folder for working code
  • API documentation: see the API Reference section

docs.title: Example: Complete sandbox function
docs.text:
This mirrors the real run_user_code(account, service, sugar) in examples/5_usercode/17_usercode.py — connection is already done for you, so you just add logic:

async def run_user_code(account, service, sugar):
    """Your sandbox. `account`, `service`, `sugar` are connected and ready."""

    # Account state
    try:
        summary = await service.account_summary()
        print(f"Balance: {summary.account_balance:.2f} {summary.account_currency}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Balance error: {e}")
        return

    # Lot size based on risk (1% with 50-pip SL)
    try:
        lots = await sugar.calc_lot_by_risk("EURUSD", risk_percent=1.0, stop_pips=50)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Lot-size error: {e}")
        return

    # Open a market order with SL/TP in pips
    try:
        ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=lots, sl_pips=50, tp_pips=100)
        print(f"[OK] Order opened: #{ticket} with {lots:.2f} lot")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Order error: {e}")
        return

    print("Strategy execution completed!")

Happy trading!

docs.title: Your First Project in 10 Minutes (Python)
docs.text: Hands-on Quick Start - Create a working trading project with MetaTrader 4 and PyMT4 from scratch.

docs.title: Step 0: Obtain Your API Key
docs.text: To connect to MetaRPC endpoints (mt4.mrpc.pro:443), obtain your API key: 1. Register for free at https://mrpc.pro/signup. 2. Generate your API token in your dashboard at https://mrpc.pro/my. 3. Set your token in your environment or connection config.

docs.title: Step 1: Create Your Project
docs.text:
Create a new directory for your trading bot:

mkdir my_pymt4_bot
cd my_pymt4_bot

Install the package:

pip install MetaRpcMT4

docs.title: Step 2: Write Your Trading Code
docs.text:
Create main.py and paste the following complete program:

import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account

async def main():
    # Session ID generation on Connect and authentication are handled automatically
    account = MT4Account(
        user=12345678,            # your MT4 login
        password="your_password",   # your MT4 password
        grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443",
        api_key="TRIAL",            # or your key from mrpc.pro/my
    )
    await account.connect_by_server_name(
        server_name="MetaQuotes-Demo",   # your broker's MT4 server name
        base_chart_symbol="EURUSD",
        timeout_seconds=30,
    )

    summary = await account.account_summary()
    print(f"Balance: {summary.account_balance}, Equity: {summary.account_equity}")

    await account.channel.close()

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Step 3: Run the Program
docs.text:
Run your application:

python main.py

Expected output (values depend on your account):

Balance: 10000.00, Equity: 10000.00

docs.title: 🚀 Next Steps
docs.text: Congratulations! You have successfully established a direct gRPC connection to MetaTrader 4. Next: - Explore gRPC Streaming to listen to live ticks. - Check the API Reference for all 18 core terminal methods. - Learn about high-level risk management and auto-normalization in MT4Sugar.

docs.title: MT4Account — Master Overview
docs.text:
One page to orient fast: the low-level gRPC client for MetaTrader 4. Jump to any group overview or method spec from here.

MT4Account is Layer 1 — direct gRPC/protobuf calls to the MT4 terminal gateway. MT4Service (typed facade) and MT4Sugar (high-level helpers) build on top of it.

It exposes 25 feature methods across 5 groups (plus connection & stream helpers). MT4 has a single order list — no positions/deals split, Depth-of-Market, order_check or order_calc_* (those are MT5-only).

docs.title: 🚦 Start here — Section Overviews
docs.text:
• 1. Account Information — Overview Account snapshot plus performance: balance/equity/margin, trade statistics, equity curve and unrealized-P/L extrema.
  • 2. Orders & History — Overview Currently open orders (market + pending), their ticket lists, and closed-order history.
  • 3. Symbols & Quotes — Overview Symbol list, live quotes, OHLC bar history, per-symbol parameters, tick value, Market Watch select and server timezone.
  • 4. Trading Operations — Overview Send market/pending orders, modify SL/TP/price, close or delete, and close-by.
  • 5. Streaming Methods — Overview Real-time async generators: ticks, trade events, ticket lists and open-order profit.

docs.title: 🧭 Method groups
docs.text: Group Methods Account Information account_summary, trade_stats, trade_unrealized_pl, equity_history, trade_stats_equity_history Orders & History opened_orders, opened_orders_tickets, orders_history Symbols & Quotes symbols, quote, quote_many, quote_history, symbol_params_many, tick_value_with_size, symbol_select, server_timezone Trading Operations order_send, order_modify, order_close_delete, order_close_by Streaming Methods on_symbol_tick, on_trade, on_opened_orders_tickets, on_opened_orders_profit, on_connect_state

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (Python async/await)
docs.text:
import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account

async def main():
    account = MT4Account(
        user=12345678,
        password="your_password",
        grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443",
        api_key="TRIAL",
    )
    await account.connect_by_server_name(
        server_name="MetaQuotes-Demo",
        base_chart_symbol="EURUSD",
        timeout_seconds=30,
    )

    summary = await account.account_summary()
    print(summary.account_balance, summary.account_equity)

    await account.channel.close()

asyncio.run(main())

Every method is async and must be awaited. Errors surface as exceptions (ApiExceptionMT4 / ConnectExceptionMT4) — see the Return Codes Reference.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• Account Summary — Complete account snapshot (balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, server time) in a single call. (RECOMMENDED)
  • Trade Statistics — Aggregated trade statistics — profit factor, drawdowns, per-market breakdown, win/loss metrics.
  • Unrealized P/L Extrema — Per-open-order unrealized P/L extrema (best/worst floating P/L with timestamps).
  • Equity Curve — Time series of equity/balance points with running drawdowns — the equity curve.
  • Stats + Equity + Trades — Combined statistics, equity-chart points and the trade list in a single call.

docs.title: Account Summary (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
Complete account snapshot (balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, server time) in a single call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.account_summary(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: AccountSummary(AccountSummaryRequest) -> AccountSummaryReply
  • Payload: AccountSummaryData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One call that returns every essential account property.
  • Why you need it. The most efficient way to read balance/equity/margin at once — one round-trip instead of many single-field calls.
  • When to use. At session start (banner / sanity check), and right before any risk decision or order.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• RECOMMENDED way to read account state
  • Balance, equity, credit in one round-trip
  • Login, name, server, company
  • Leverage and trade mode (DEMO/REAL)
  • Currency and server time

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def account_summary(
    self,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message AccountSummaryRequest {
}

Payload message:

message AccountSummaryData {
  int64 account_login = 1;
  double account_balance = 2;
  double account_equity = 3;
  string account_user_name = 4;
  int64 account_leverage = 5;
  EnumAccountTradeMode account_trade_mode = 6;
  string account_company_name = 7;
  string account_currency = 8;
  Timestamp server_time = 9;
  Timestamp server_time_utc = 15;
  double account_credit = 10;
  bool is_investor = 11;
  int32 utc_server_time_shift_minutes = 12;
  int32 server_utc_offset_seconds = 14;
  double account_margin = 13;
  double account_margin_free = 16;
  double account_margin_level = 17;
  EnumAccountMarginMode account_margin_mode = 18;
  bool account_trade_allowed = 19;
  bool account_trade_expert = 20;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountSummaryData
docs.text: Field Proto Type Python Type Description account_login int64 int Account number account_balance double float Balance in deposit currency (excludes floating P/L) account_equity double float Equity = balance + floating P/L of open orders account_user_name string str Account owner account_leverage int64 int Leverage (e.g. 100 = 1:100) account_trade_mode EnumAccountTradeMode int DEMO / CONTEST / REAL account_company_name string str Broker name account_currency string str Deposit currency (e.g. USD) server_time Timestamp datetime Current server time server_time_utc Timestamp datetime Current server time in UTC account_credit double float Credit in deposit currency is_investor bool bool True if connected with the investor (read-only) password utc_server_time_shift_minutes int32 int Server time shift from UTC, minutes server_utc_offset_seconds int32 int Server UTC offset, seconds account_margin double float Margin currently used by open orders account_margin_free double float Free margin available for new orders account_margin_level double float Margin level % = equity / margin × 100 account_margin_mode EnumAccountMarginMode int Margin calculation mode account_trade_allowed bool bool Trading allowed on the account account_trade_expert bool bool Expert/automated trading allowed

docs.title: EnumAccountTradeMode
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO 0 Demo / practice account ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST 1 Contest account ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL 2 Real (live) account

docs.title: EnumAccountMarginMode
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_NETTING 0 Retail, netting ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_EXCHANGE 1 Exchange margin model ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING 2 Retail, hedging (typical MT4)

In Python, access values via the pb2 module, e.g. account_helper_pb2.EnumAccountTradeMode.ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call beats many. account_summary() returns balance, equity, margin, free margin and margin level together — don't fan out into several calls for these.
  • balance vs equity. Balance ignores open orders; equity includes their floating P/L. On a flat account they're equal; with open orders, equity − balance is your current floating P/L.
  • Money is in the deposit currency. Every monetary field is in account_currency. Don't mix it with an instrument's quote currency without converting.
  • margin_level is 0 with no open orders (division by zero margin is reported as 0), so guard before comparing it to a stop-out threshold.
  • Server time. server_time / server_time_utc are protobuf Timestamps — use .ToDatetime(); server_utc_offset_seconds tells you the broker's offset.
  • Read-only sessions. If is_investor is true (investor password) or account_trade_allowed is false, trading calls will be rejected — check these before placing orders.

docs.title: 1) Session-start banner
docs.text:
Print a clean account banner when your bot connects — handy for logs and sanity checks.

import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_account_helper_pb2 as ah

MODE = {
    ah.EnumAccountTradeMode.ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO: "DEMO",
    ah.EnumAccountTradeMode.ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST: "CONTEST",
    ah.EnumAccountTradeMode.ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL: "REAL",
}

async def print_banner(account):
    s = await account.account_summary()
    floating = s.account_equity - s.account_balance
    print("=" * 52)
    print(f" Account #{s.account_login}  ({MODE.get(s.account_trade_mode, '?')})")
    print(f" Broker : {s.account_company_name}")
    print(f" Balance: {s.account_balance:,.2f} {s.account_currency}")
    print(f" Equity : {s.account_equity:,.2f}  (floating {floating:+,.2f})")
    print(f" Margin : used {s.account_margin:,.2f} / free {s.account_margin_free:,.2f}")
    print(f" Leverage 1:{s.account_leverage}")
    print("=" * 52)

docs.title: 2) Pre-trade risk gate
docs.text:
Refuse to open a new order unless the account can actually take it — a guard you call before every entry.

async def can_open(account, *, min_free_margin: float, min_margin_level: float = 200.0) -> bool:
    s = await account.account_summary()

    if not s.account_trade_allowed or s.is_investor:
        print("Trading not allowed on this account (read-only / disabled).")
        return False

    if s.account_margin_free < min_free_margin:
        print(f"Free margin too low: {s.account_margin_free:.2f} < {min_free_margin:.2f}")
        return False

    # margin_level is 0 when nothing is open — only enforce it once there is margin in use
    if s.account_margin > 0 and s.account_margin_level < min_margin_level:
        print(f"Margin level too low: {s.account_margin_level:.1f}% < {min_margin_level:.1f}%")
        return False

    return True

# usage:
# if await can_open(account, min_free_margin=500):
#     await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.10)

docs.title: 3) Equity / drawdown monitor
docs.text:
Poll equity on an interval and alert when drawdown from the session peak crosses a limit.

import asyncio

async def watch_drawdown(account, *, max_dd_percent: float = 10.0, interval: float = 5.0):
    peak = None
    while True:
        s = await account.account_summary()
        eq = s.account_equity
        peak = eq if peak is None else max(peak, eq)
        dd = (peak - eq) / peak * 100 if peak > 0 else 0.0
        print(f"equity={eq:,.2f} peak={peak:,.2f} drawdown={dd:.2f}%")
        if dd >= max_dd_percent:
            print(f"[ALERT] drawdown {dd:.2f}% ≥ {max_dd_percent}% — consider de-risking")
            break
        await asyncio.sleep(interval)

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Snapshot, not a stream. Equity/margin are a point-in-time read — re-query right before a risk check or order, don't cache them across time.
  • margin_level == 0 with nothing open. Guard account_margin > 0 before comparing the level to a stop-out/entry threshold.
  • Currency mismatch. All money fields are in account_currency; converting instrument P/L into account currency is on you.
  • Read-only / disabled accounts. is_investor or account_trade_allowed == False means orders will be rejected even though this call succeeds.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo). Fields are populated; account_currency non-empty; on a flat account equity == balance and account_margin == 0.
  • With open orders. equity != balance, account_margin > 0, and account_margin_level is a sensible percentage.
  • Risk gate. Unit-test can_open() against synthetic summaries (low free margin, investor session, trading disabled) and assert it refuses.

docs.title: Equity Curve
docs.text:
Time series of balance/equity points with running drawdowns — your equity curve, ready to chart or export.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.equity_history(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • RPC: EquityHistory(EquityHistoryRequest) -> EquityHistoryReply
  • Payload: EquityHistoryData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A chronological list of points, each with balance, equity, running drawdowns and the cash flow at that moment.
  • Why you need it. To plot the equity curve, measure maximum drawdown, or export performance to a spreadsheet.
  • When to use. Reporting, charting, drawdown analysis.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Balance & equity over time (the curve)
  • Running balance/equity drawdowns (money and %)
  • Realized / unrealized P/L and cash flow per point
  • Feed charts, CSV exports and risk reports

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def equity_history(
    self,
    from_time: Optional[datetime] = None,
    exclude_same_bars: Optional[bool] = None,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message EquityHistoryRequest {
  string from = 1;              // ISO-8601 start; empty = full history
  string from_utc = 2;          // ISO-8601 start in UTC
  bool exclude_same_bars = 3;   // collapse consecutive equal points
}

Payload message:

message EquityHistoryData {
  repeated EquityPointData points = 1;
}

message EquityPointData {
  Timestamp time = 1;
  Timestamp time_utc = 2;
  double balance = 3;
  double equity = 4;
  double balance_drawdown_raw = 5;
  double balance_drawdown_relative = 6;   // percent
  double equity_drawdown_raw = 7;
  double equity_drawdown_relative = 8;     // percent
  double realized_pl = 9;
  double unrealized_pl = 10;
  double cash_flow = 11;                   // deposits/withdrawals at this point
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description from_time datetime, optional Start of the window; serialized to an ISO-8601 string. Omit for full history. exclude_same_bars bool, optional Collapse consecutive equal points to shrink the payload. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — EquityHistoryData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description points list[EquityPointData] The equity-curve points, in time order

Each EquityPointData:

Field Python Type Description time / time_utc datetime Point timestamp (server / UTC) balance float Balance at this point equity float Equity at this point balance_drawdown_raw / _relative float Balance drawdown (money / %) equity_drawdown_raw / _relative float Equity drawdown (money / %) realized_pl float Realized P/L to this point unrealized_pl float Floating P/L at this point cash_flow float Deposit/withdrawal applied at this point

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Drawdowns are precomputed. You don't have to derive the running peak yourself — equity_drawdown_relative is already the % below the high-water mark at each point.
  • cash_flow separates deposits from trading. A jump in balance with a matching cash_flow is a deposit/withdrawal, not a trade — exclude it when measuring trading performance.
  • This payload can be large. A long-lived account has many points; pass from_time to scope the window and/or exclude_same_bars=True to drop flat stretches.
  • Timestamps are protobuf Timestamps — convert with .ToDatetime().
  • Pairs with trade_stats. Use trade_stats for the headline ratios and equity_history for the curve, or trade_stats_equity_history to fetch both at once.

docs.title: 1) Export the curve to CSV
docs.text:
Dump the equity curve so you can chart it in a spreadsheet or notebook.

import csv

async def export_equity_csv(account, path: str = "equity.csv"):
    data = await account.equity_history(exclude_same_bars=True)
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(["time_utc", "balance", "equity", "equity_dd_%"])
        for p in data.points:
            w.writerow([p.time_utc.ToDatetime().isoformat(),
                        f"{p.balance:.2f}", f"{p.equity:.2f}",
                        f"{p.equity_drawdown_relative:.2f}"])
    print(f"wrote {len(data.points)} points -> {path}")

docs.title: 2) Maximum drawdown from the curve
docs.text:
Find the deepest equity drawdown and when it happened.

async def max_drawdown(account):
    data = await account.equity_history()
    if not data.points:
        print("no equity history")
        return
    worst = max(data.points, key=lambda p: p.equity_drawdown_relative)
    when = worst.time_utc.ToDatetime()
    print(f"Max equity drawdown: {worst.equity_drawdown_relative:.2f}% "
          f"({worst.equity_drawdown_raw:,.2f}) at {when:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC")

docs.title: 3) Trading-only result (strip deposits)
docs.text:
Separate trading performance from deposits/withdrawals using cash_flow.

async def trading_pnl(account):
    data = await account.equity_history()
    if not data.points:
        return 0.0
    net_cash = sum(p.cash_flow for p in data.points)
    start, end = data.points[0].balance, data.points[-1].balance
    trading = (end - start) - net_cash
    print(f"balance {start:,.2f} -> {end:,.2f} | deposits/withdrawals {net_cash:+,.2f} "
          f"| trading P/L {trading:+,.2f}")
    return trading

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Large payloads. Full history can be big — scope with from_time and/or exclude_same_bars=True; print counts rather than every point.
  • Deposits skew raw balance deltas. Use cash_flow to isolate trading P/L from account funding.
  • Empty history. A fresh account returns an empty points list — guard before indexing points[0] / points[-1].

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo with history). points is non-empty and ordered by time; equity_drawdown_relative >= 0 for every point.
  • exclude_same_bars. The collapsed call returns no more points than the full call.
  • Windowing. A recent from_time returns fewer points than full history.

docs.title: Trade Statistics
docs.text:
Aggregated trade statistics — profit factor, win/loss, drawdowns, expectancy and a per-market breakdown, in one call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.trade_stats(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • RPC: TradeStats(TradeStatsRequest) -> TradeStatsReply
  • Payload: StatsData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A rollup of your trading performance: headline ratios, drawdowns, and a breakdown per market.
  • Why you need it. The numbers a dashboard or weekly review needs — without computing them yourself from raw history.
  • When to use. Reporting, periodic performance checks, "how am I doing?" screens.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Profit factor, expectancy, Sharpe ratio, GHPR, Z-score
  • Win/loss counts and percentages
  • Balance & equity drawdowns (absolute and relative)
  • Per-market breakdown (trades, lots, profit, win rate)
  • Account totals: deposits, withdrawals, growth %

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def trade_stats(
    self,
    from_time: Optional[datetime] = None,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message TradeStatsRequest {
  string from = 1;       // ISO-8601 start; empty = full history
  string from_utc = 2;   // ISO-8601 start in UTC
}

Payload message (top level):

message StatsData {
  TradeSummaryData summary = 1;              // open/day/week/month/total profit
  double max_balance_drawdown_raw = 2;
  double max_balance_drawdown_relative = 3;  // percent
  double max_equity_drawdown_raw = 4;
  double max_equity_drawdown_relative = 5;   // percent
  repeated MarketTradeCountData markets = 6; // per-symbol breakdown
  ProfitabilityData profitability = 7;       // won/lost counts & percentages
  double pips = 8;
  double lots = 9;
  double comissions = 10;
  AveragePipsUsdData average_win = 11;
  AveragePipsUsdData average_lost = 12;
  WonData longs_won = 13;
  WonData shorts_won = 14;
  ProfitData best_trade = 15;
  ProfitData worst_trade = 16;
  ProfitData best_trade_pips = 17;
  ProfitData worst_trade_pips = 18;
  string average_trade_length = 19;
  double profit_factor = 20;
  double standard_deviation = 21;
  double sharpe_ratio = 22;
  ZScoreData z_score = 23;
  ExpectancyData expectancy = 24;            // pips & dollar
  double ghpr = 25;                          // geometric holding period return
  int64 trades = 26;
  double growth_percent = 27;
  double deposits = 28;
  double withdrawals = 29;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description from_time datetime, optional Start of the window; serialized to an ISO-8601 string. Omit for full history. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — StatsData
docs.text:
Headline scalars:

Field Python Type Description profit_factor float Gross profit ÷ gross loss (> 1 is profitable) expectancy ExpectancyData Expected result per trade (.pips, .dollar) sharpe_ratio float Risk-adjusted return ghpr float Geometric holding-period return standard_deviation float Std-dev of trade results pips / lots / comissions float Total pips, lots traded, commissions trades int Total number of trades growth_percent float Account growth, % deposits / withdrawals float Totals in deposit currency max_balance_drawdown_raw float Worst balance drawdown (money) max_balance_drawdown_relative float Worst balance drawdown (%) max_equity_drawdown_raw float Worst equity drawdown (money) max_equity_drawdown_relative float Worst equity drawdown (%) average_trade_length str Average holding time

Nested submessages:

Field Message Key fields summary TradeSummaryData open_trades, open_profit, day_profit, week_profit, month_profit, total_profit profitability ProfitabilityData won_trades, won_trades_percent, lost_trades, lost_trades_percent markets (repeated) MarketTradeCountData market_name, count, lots, profit, win_rate, won_count, lost_count average_win / average_lost AveragePipsUsdData average_pips, average_usd longs_won / shorts_won WonData won_count, all, won_persent best_trade / worst_trade ProfitData tiket, date, profit

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• summary is the "today/this week/this month" block — perfect for a compact P/L widget, separate from the all-time ratios.
  • Drawdowns come in two flavours: balance vs equity, each as raw money and relative %. Equity drawdown is usually the one that matters for risk.
  • markets is your per-symbol attribution — iterate it to see which instruments actually make or lose money.
  • Watch the proto spelling. Field names carry the server's spelling: comissions, tiket, won_persent — use them as-is.
  • from_time trims the window. Omit it for the full account history; pass it to scope stats to a period (e.g. this month) — it is sent as an ISO-8601 string.
  • Pairs with equity_history. Use trade_stats for the numbers and equity_history for the curve, or trade_stats_equity_history to get both in one round-trip.

docs.title: 1) Weekly performance report
docs.text:
Turn the stats into a readable report line — the kind you log or post to a channel.

async def performance_report(account):
    s = await account.trade_stats()
    p = s.profitability
    win_rate = p.won_trades_percent
    print("── Performance ──────────────────────────────")
    print(f" Trades        : {s.trades}  (win {win_rate:.1f}%)")
    print(f" Profit factor : {s.profit_factor:.2f}")
    print(f" Expectancy    : {s.expectancy.dollar:+.2f} / trade")
    print(f" Growth        : {s.growth_percent:+.2f}%")
    print(f" Max DD (eq)   : {s.max_equity_drawdown_relative:.1f}%"
          f"  ({s.max_equity_drawdown_raw:,.2f})")
    print(f" This week     : {s.summary.week_profit:+,.2f}")

docs.title: 2) Which markets make money?
docs.text:
Rank the per-market breakdown so you can cut the losers and size up the winners.

async def markets_by_profit(account, top: int = 5):
    s = await account.trade_stats()
    rows = sorted(s.markets, key=lambda m: m.profit, reverse=True)
    print(f"{'Symbol':<10}{'Trades':>7}{'Win%':>7}{'Profit':>12}")
    for m in rows[:top]:
        print(f"{m.market_name:<10}{m.count:>7}{m.win_rate:>6.1f}%{m.profit:>12,.2f}")
    worst = rows[-1] if rows else None
    if worst and worst.profit < 0:
        print(f"Worst: {worst.market_name} ({worst.profit:,.2f}) — review or disable")

docs.title: 3) Month-to-date health check
docs.text:
Scope the stats to the current month and flag a weak profit factor.

from datetime import datetime

async def month_health(account, min_profit_factor: float = 1.2) -> bool:
    start = datetime.utcnow().replace(day=1, hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
    s = await account.trade_stats(from_time=start)
    ok = s.profit_factor >= min_profit_factor
    print(f"MTD: trades={s.trades} PF={s.profit_factor:.2f} "
          f"result={s.summary.month_profit:+,.2f} -> {'OK' if ok else 'WEAK'}")
    return ok

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Empty history. A brand-new account with no closed trades returns zeroed stats — guard divisions (e.g. don't trust profit_factor when trades == 0).
  • Potentially heavy. The markets list grows with the number of traded symbols; it's fine to summarize rather than print everything.
  • Spelling quirks. comissions, tiket, won_persent are the real field names — a typo-looking attribute access is correct.
  • Scope awareness. Numbers reflect the from_time window (or all history if omitted) — don't compare a month-scoped call with an all-time one.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo with history). trades > 0, profit_factor finite, len(markets) >= 1.
  • Fresh account. With no closed trades, assert the call still succeeds and your report handles zeros without dividing by zero.
  • Windowing. A from_time of today vs a year ago returns different trades counts; assert the scoped count ≤ the full count.

docs.title: Stats + Equity + Trades
docs.text:
Statistics, the equity curve and the trade list — everything a performance report needs, in a single round-trip.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.trade_stats_equity_history(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • RPC: TradeStatsEquityHistory(TradeStatsEquityHistoryRequest) -> TradeStatsEquityHistoryReply
  • Payload: StatsWithChartsData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A combined payload: the same StatsData as trade_stats, the equity charts (same points as equity_history), plus the closed and open trade lists.
  • Why you need it. Build a full report (numbers + curve + trades) without three separate calls.
  • When to use. Report/export screens where you want everything consistent and in one shot.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Headline statistics (stats)
  • Equity-curve points (charts)
  • Closed trades (trades) and currently open trades (open_trades)
  • One round-trip for a complete report

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def trade_stats_equity_history(
    self,
    from_time: Optional[datetime] = None,
    exclude_same_bars: Optional[bool] = None,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

  string from_utc = 2;          // ISO-8601 start in UTC
  bool exclude_same_bars = 3;   // collapse consecutive equal equity points
}

Payload message:

message StatsWithChartsData {
  StatsData stats = 1;                         // see trade_stats
  repeated EquityPointData charts = 2;         // see equity_history
  repeated TradeHistoryItemData trades = 3;    // closed trades
  repeated TradeHistoryItemData open_trades = 4;
}

message TradeHistoryItemData {
  int64 ticket = 1;
  string symbol = 2;
  bool is_buy = 3;
  double lots = 4;
  double open_price = 5;
  double close_price = 6;
  Timestamp open_time = 7;
  Timestamp open_time_utc = 8;
  Timestamp close_time = 9;
  Timestamp close_time_utc = 10;
  double profit = 11;
  double commission = 12;
  double swap = 13;
  string comment = 14;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description from_time datetime, optional Start of the window; serialized to an ISO-8601 string. Omit for full history. exclude_same_bars bool, optional Collapse consecutive equal equity points to shrink charts. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — StatsWithChartsData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description stats StatsData Headline statistics — see trade_stats charts list[EquityPointData] Equity-curve points — see equity_history trades list[TradeHistoryItemData] Closed trades open_trades list[TradeHistoryItemData] Currently open trades

Each TradeHistoryItemData:

Field Python Type Description ticket int Trade ticket symbol str Symbol is_buy bool True = buy, False = sell lots float Volume open_price / close_price float Entry / exit price open_time / close_time (+ _utc) datetime Entry / exit time profit float Trade profit (excl. commission/swap) commission / swap float Costs comment str Order comment

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call, three views. stats is the summary, charts is the curve, trades/open_trades are the raw rows — everything stays consistent because it's a single snapshot.
  • Net result per trade is profit + commission + swap (commission and swap are usually negative). Don't forget the costs when totalling.
  • is_buy is the side — there's no separate order-type enum here; True = long, False = short.
  • Can be large. charts and trades grow with account age — scope with from_time and exclude_same_bars=True for the curve.
  • Prefer this over three calls when you need all three together; use the individual methods when you only need one.

docs.title: 1) Full report in one round-trip
docs.text:
Pull everything and print a compact report header.

async def full_report(account):
    r = await account.trade_stats_equity_history(exclude_same_bars=True)
    s = r.stats
    print("── Report ───────────────────────────────────")
    print(f" Profit factor : {s.profit_factor:.2f}")
    print(f" Trades        : {s.trades}  (open now: {len(r.open_trades)})")
    print(f" Growth        : {s.growth_percent:+.2f}%")
    print(f" Equity points : {len(r.charts)}")
    print(f" Closed trades : {len(r.trades)}")

docs.title: 2) Recent closed trades table
docs.text:
Show the last few closed trades with side, size and net result.

async def recent_trades(account, n: int = 10):
    r = await account.trade_stats_equity_history()
    rows = sorted(r.trades, key=lambda t: t.close_time_utc.ToDatetime(), reverse=True)[:n]
    print(f"{'Ticket':>10} {'Sym':<8} {'Side':<5} {'Lots':>6} {'Net':>10}")
    for t in rows:
        net = t.profit + t.commission + t.swap
        side = "BUY" if t.is_buy else "SELL"
        print(f"{t.ticket:>10} {t.symbol:<8} {side:<5} {t.lots:>6.2f} {net:>10.2f}")

docs.title: 3) Open exposure right now
docs.text:
Summarize current open trades (count, lots, floating P/L) straight from open_trades.

async def open_exposure(account):
    r = await account.trade_stats_equity_history()
    lots = sum(t.lots for t in r.open_trades)
    floating = sum(t.profit + t.commission + t.swap for t in r.open_trades)
    print(f"open trades: {len(r.open_trades)} | lots: {lots:.2f} | floating: {floating:+.2f}")

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Heaviest call in the group. It returns stats + curve + every trade — scope it (from_time, exclude_same_bars) and summarize rather than dumping all rows.
  • Costs are separate. profit excludes commission and swap; add them for the true net.
  • Empty account. trades, open_trades and charts can all be empty — guard before indexing.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo with history). stats.trades equals len(r.trades) for the same window; charts is non-empty.
  • Open vs closed. len(open_trades) matches what opened_orders reports.
  • Consistency. stats here equals a separate trade_stats call over the same from_time.

docs.title: Unrealized P/L Extrema
docs.text:
For each open order, the best and worst floating P/L it has reached (with timestamps) — classic MFE / MAE excursion data.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.trade_unrealized_pl(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradeStats
  • RPC: TradeUnrealizedPL(TradeUnrealizedPLRequest) -> TradeUnrealizedPLReply
  • Payload: TradeUnrealizedPLData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Per open order, the maximum favorable (max_unrealized_pl) and maximum adverse (min_unrealized_pl) floating P/L reached since it opened, each with a timestamp.
  • Why you need it. MFE/MAE analysis — how far trades run in your favor before you exit, and how deep they dip before recovering.
  • When to use. Tuning stop-loss / take-profit placement and trailing logic from real behaviour.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• See the peak profit each open order reached (MFE)
  • See the deepest drawdown each open order survived (MAE)
  • Timestamps of both extrema (server and UTC)
  • Drive data-informed SL/TP and trailing decisions

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def trade_unrealized_pl(
    self,
    from_time: Optional[datetime] = None,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message TradeUnrealizedPLRequest {
  string from = 1;       // ISO-8601 start; empty = full history
  string from_utc = 2;   // ISO-8601 start in UTC
}

Payload message:

message TradeUnrealizedPLData {
  repeated TradeUnrealizedExtremaData extrema = 1;
}

message TradeUnrealizedExtremaData {
  int64 ticket = 1;
  string symbol = 2;
  Timestamp max_unrealized_time = 3;      // when peak profit was reached
  Timestamp max_unrealized_time_utc = 4;
  double max_unrealized_pl = 5;           // MFE — best floating P/L
  Timestamp min_unrealized_time = 6;      // when deepest loss was reached
  Timestamp min_unrealized_time_utc = 7;
  double min_unrealized_pl = 8;           // MAE — worst floating P/L
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description from_time datetime, optional Start of the window; serialized to an ISO-8601 string. Omit for full history. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — TradeUnrealizedPLData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description extrema list[TradeUnrealizedExtremaData] One entry per order with excursion data

Each TradeUnrealizedExtremaData:

Field Python Type Description ticket int Order ticket symbol str Symbol max_unrealized_pl float MFE — highest floating P/L reached max_unrealized_time / _utc datetime When the MFE occurred (server / UTC) min_unrealized_pl float MAE — lowest floating P/L reached min_unrealized_time / _utc datetime When the MAE occurred (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• MFE vs MAE. max_unrealized_pl is how good the trade got (Maximum Favorable Excursion); min_unrealized_pl is how bad it got (Maximum Adverse Excursion). Both are floating values seen while the order was open, not the realized result.
  • Use it to size stops. If winners routinely dip to −15 pips (MAE) before running, a −10 pip stop was too tight. If MFE far exceeds your actual exits, your TP is leaving money on the table.
  • Signs matter. max_unrealized_pl is usually ≥ 0 and min_unrealized_pl usually ≤ 0, but a trade that was never in profit can have a negative MFE — don't assume positivity.
  • Timestamps are protobuf Timestamps — convert with .ToDatetime().
  • from_time scopes the set; omit for everything available.

docs.title: 1) MFE / MAE table
docs.text:
Show, per order, how far it ran in your favor and how deep it dipped.

async def excursion_table(account):
    data = await account.trade_unrealized_pl()
    print(f"{'Ticket':>10} {'Symbol':<8} {'MFE':>10} {'MAE':>10}")
    for e in data.extrema:
        print(f"{e.ticket:>10} {e.symbol:<8} {e.max_unrealized_pl:>10.2f} {e.min_unrealized_pl:>10.2f}")

docs.title: 2) Were my stops too tight?
docs.text:
Find winners that first went underwater — their MAE tells you the stop distance they actually needed.

async def stop_pressure(account, threshold: float = -10.0):
    data = await account.trade_unrealized_pl()
    deep = [e for e in data.extrema if e.min_unrealized_pl <= threshold]
    deep.sort(key=lambda e: e.min_unrealized_pl)  # deepest first
    print(f"{len(deep)} order(s) dipped below {threshold:.2f} before now:")
    for e in deep[:10]:
        when = e.min_unrealized_time.ToDatetime()
        print(f"  #{e.ticket} {e.symbol}: MAE {e.min_unrealized_pl:.2f} at {when:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M}")

docs.title: 3) Profit give-back detector
docs.text:
Highlight orders that reached a solid peak — candidates where a trailing stop or earlier TP would have locked in more.

async def giveback(account, min_peak: float = 20.0):
    data = await account.trade_unrealized_pl()
    for e in data.extrema:
        if e.max_unrealized_pl >= min_peak:
            print(f"#{e.ticket} {e.symbol}: peaked at {e.max_unrealized_pl:.2f} "
                  f"(worst {e.min_unrealized_pl:.2f}) — review exit/trailing")

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Open orders only. These extrema describe currently-open orders' journey so far; for closed-trade results use orders_history or trade_stats.
  • Floating, not realized. A high MFE doesn't mean you captured it — that's exactly the point of the give-back check.
  • Empty when flat. With no open orders, extrema is empty — handle the zero case.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• With open orders. extrema is non-empty; for each entry max_unrealized_pl >= min_unrealized_pl.
  • Flat account. Returns an empty extrema list without error.
  • Timestamp sanity. min_unrealized_time / max_unrealized_time convert to datetimes that fall after the order's open time.

docs.title: Opened Orders
docs.text:
Every currently open order (market and pending) with full detail, in the sort order you choose.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.opened_orders(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: OpenedOrders(OpenedOrdersRequest) -> OpenedOrdersReply
  • Payload: OpenedOrdersData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The full list of live orders on the account — market positions and resting pending orders — each with price, SL/TP, profit, magic and times.
  • Why you need it. To inspect, manage, or close current exposure.
  • When to use. Whenever you need order details. If you only need ticket numbers, use opened_orders_tickets (cheaper).

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• All open market & pending orders in one call
  • Full per-order detail (price, SL/TP, profit, swap, magic)
  • Choose the sort order
  • Filter in your code by symbol / magic / side

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def opened_orders(
    self,
    sort_mode: EnumOpenedOrderSortType = EnumOpenedOrderSortType.SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

message OpenedOrdersRequest {
  EnumOpenedOrderSortType sort_type = 1;
}

Payload message:

message OpenedOrdersData {

}

  string comment = 1;
  double commision = 2;
  Timestamp expiration_time = 3;
  double lots = 4;
  int32 magic_number = 5;
  double open_price = 6;
  double profit = 7;
  double stop_loss = 8;
  double swap = 9;
  string symbol = 10;
  double take_profit = 11;
  int32 ticket = 12;
  int32 position_index = 13;
  OpenedOrderType order_type = 14;
  int32 sort_index = 15;
  Timestamp open_time = 16;

  Timestamp open_time_utc = 19;
}

docs.text: Parameter Type Description sort_mode EnumOpenedOrderSortType Sort order; default SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OpenedOrdersData
docs.text:
order_infos — a list of OpenedOrderInfo:

Field Python Type Description ticket int Order ticket symbol str Symbol order_type OpenedOrderType (int) Operation (OO_OP_*) lots float Volume open_price float Open / pending price stop_loss / take_profit float SL / TP price (0 if unset) profit float Current floating profit swap / commision float Swap / commission (note proto spelling commision) magic_number int Expert/magic id comment str Order comment open_time / _utc datetime Open time (server / UTC) expiration_time / _utc datetime Pending-order expiration

docs.title: EnumOpenedOrderSortType — input sort_mode
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC 0 By open time, ascending SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC 1 By open time, descending SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_ASC 2 By ticket id, ascending SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_DESC 3 By ticket id, descending

docs.title: OpenedOrderType — field order_type
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning OO_OP_BUY 0 Market buy OO_OP_SELL 1 Market sell OO_OP_BUYLIMIT 2 Buy limit (pending) OO_OP_SELLLIMIT 3 Sell limit (pending) OO_OP_BUYSTOP 4 Buy stop (pending) OO_OP_SELLSTOP 5 Sell stop (pending) OO_OP_BALANCE 6 Balance record (non-tradable) OO_OP_CREDIT 7 Credit record (non-tradable)

In Python, access values via account_helper_pb2.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUY.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Market and pending in one list. order_type tells them apart: OO_OP_BUY/OO_OP_SELL are filled market orders; the *LIMIT/*STOP variants are resting pending orders.
  • Buy vs sell side. Buy side = OO_OP_BUY, OO_OP_BUYLIMIT, OO_OP_BUYSTOP; the odd values (1,3,5) are the sell side.
  • OO_OP_BALANCE / OO_OP_CREDIT are bookkeeping records, not tradable orders — skip them when summing exposure.
  • profit is floating and excludes swap/commision; add them for the true carry cost.
  • Proto spelling: the commission field is commision (single s) — use it as-is.
  • Lightweight alternative: opened_orders_tickets returns just ticket numbers for fast polling.

docs.title: 1) Open orders table
docs.text:
Print a readable snapshot of everything currently open.

import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_account_helper_pb2 as ah

TYPE = {
    ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUY: "BUY",   ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_SELL: "SELL",
    ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUYLIMIT: "BUY LIMIT",  ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_SELLLIMIT: "SELL LIMIT",
    ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUYSTOP: "BUY STOP",    ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_SELLSTOP: "SELL STOP",
}

async def print_open(account):
    data = await account.opened_orders()
    print(f"{'Ticket':>10} {'Symbol':<8} {'Type':<10} {'Lots':>6} {'Price':>10} {'Profit':>10}")
    for o in data.order_infos:
        print(f"{o.ticket:>10} {o.symbol:<8} {TYPE.get(o.order_type,'?'):<10} "
              f"{o.lots:>6.2f} {o.open_price:>10.5f} {o.profit:>10.2f}")
    print(f"total floating: {sum(o.profit for o in data.order_infos):+.2f}")

docs.title: 2) Only my bot's orders
docs.text:
Filter by magic_number to isolate orders a given strategy opened.

async def my_orders(account, magic: int):
    data = await account.opened_orders()
    mine = [o for o in data.order_infos if o.magic_number == magic]
    floating = sum(o.profit + o.swap + o.commision for o in mine)
    print(f"magic {magic}: {len(mine)} order(s), net {floating:+.2f}")
    return mine

docs.title: 3) Net exposure per symbol
docs.text:
Aggregate signed lots per symbol to see your real directional exposure (market orders only).

import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_account_helper_pb2 as ah
from collections import defaultdict

BUY  = {ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUY}
SELL = {ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_SELL}

async def net_exposure(account):
    data = await account.opened_orders()
    net = defaultdict(float)
    for o in data.order_infos:
        if o.order_type in BUY:
            net[o.symbol] += o.lots
        elif o.order_type in SELL:
            net[o.symbol] -= o.lots
    for sym, lots in sorted(net.items()):
        side = "long" if lots > 0 else "short" if lots < 0 else "flat"
        print(f"{sym:<8} {lots:+.2f} lots ({side})")
    return dict(net)

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Pending orders have no profit yet. A *LIMIT/*STOP order isn't filled — its profit is 0; don't count it as exposure.
  • Skip balance/credit rows. OO_OP_BALANCE / OO_OP_CREDIT appear here but aren't trades — exclude them from lot/exposure math.
  • SL/TP of 0 means "unset", not a price of zero.
  • Snapshot. The list reflects the moment of the call; use on_opened_orders_tickets to react to changes live.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Flat account. order_infos is empty; the table prints a zero total without error.
  • With a market order open. The new ticket appears with order_type == OO_OP_BUY/OO_OP_SELL and a sensible open_price.
  • Magic filter. Open two orders with different magics and assert my_orders() returns only the matching one.

docs.title: Opened Order Tickets
docs.text:
Just the ticket numbers of currently open orders — the cheapest way to poll "what's open now".

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.opened_orders_tickets(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: OpenedOrdersTickets(OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest) -> OpenedOrdersTicketsReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A flat list of open ticket numbers — no prices, no profit, just ids.
  • Why you need it. Minimal payload for high-frequency "is anything open / did it change?" checks.
  • When to use. Polling loops. When you need the actual details, call opened_orders.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Minimal payload — ticket ids only
  • Cheap to call in a tight loop
  • Pair with opened_orders to fetch detail only when something changed

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def opened_orders_tickets(
    self,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {
}

Payload message:

message OpenedOrdersTicketsData {
  repeated int32 tickets = 1;   // open order tickets (market + pending)
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OpenedOrdersTicketsData
docs.text: Field Python Type Description tickets list[int] Ticket numbers of all open orders (market + pending)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One flat list. Unlike the streaming on_opened_orders_tickets (which splits positions from pending), this returns a single tickets list covering both.
  • Set math is your friend. Convert to a set to diff against a previous poll and spot what opened or closed.
  • Fetch detail on change only. Poll this; when the set changes, call opened_orders once to get the new details — far cheaper than pulling full detail every tick.

docs.title: 1) Is anything open?
docs.text:
A one-liner liveness/exposure check.

async def has_open_orders(account) -> bool:
    data = await account.opened_orders_tickets()
    return len(data.tickets) > 0

docs.title: 2) Detect opened / closed between polls
docs.text:
Diff two snapshots to react only when the set of open orders changes.

import asyncio

async def watch_changes(account, interval: float = 1.0):
    prev = set()
    while True:
        now = set((await account.opened_orders_tickets()).tickets)
        opened, closed = now - prev, prev - now
        if opened:
            print("opened:", sorted(opened))
        if closed:
            print("closed:", sorted(closed))
        prev = now
        await asyncio.sleep(interval)

docs.title: 3) Poll cheap, fetch detail on change
docs.text:
Only pull full order detail when the ticket set actually changes.

async def refresh_on_change(account, prev_tickets: set[int]):
    now = set((await account.opened_orders_tickets()).tickets)
    if now != prev_tickets:
        details = await account.opened_orders()     # one detailed call, only when needed
        print(f"{len(details.order_infos)} open order(s) now")
        return now, details
    return now, None

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Ids only. No prices, SL/TP or profit here — don't try to make risk decisions from this call alone.
  • Market + pending mixed. The list doesn't tell you which tickets are filled vs resting; use opened_orders for that.
  • Empty when flat. No open orders → empty tickets list.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Flat account. tickets is empty.
  • After opening an order. The new ticket appears in tickets and matches the ticket returned by order_send.
  • Diff logic. Open then close an order across two polls and assert the change-detector reports it once as opened, once as closed.

• What it is. The list of closed orders in a time window, each with open/close price & time and realized profit.
  • Why you need it. Reporting, P/L analysis, win-rate stats, strategy validation.
  • When to use. After sessions, or any time you audit what actually happened.

docs.text:

  • Pagination for large histories (total_count, next_page_token)
