  int32 page_number = 6;
  int32 items_per_page = 7;
  // ... input_from_utc / input_to_utc / page_token / page_size
}

Payload message:

message OrdersHistoryData {
  repeated HistoryOrderInfo orders_info = 1;
  int32 total_count = 2;
  string next_page_token = 3;
}

message HistoryOrderInfo {
  string symbol = 11;
  int32 ticket = 13;
  OpenedOrderType order_type = 15;
  double lots = 5;
  double open_price = 7;
  double close_price = 21;
  double profit = 8;
  double swap = 10;
  double commision = 2;
  int32 magic_number = 6;
  string comment = 1;
  Timestamp open_time = 17;    // (+ open_time_utc)
  Timestamp close_time = 19;   // (+ close_time_utc)
  // ... stop_loss, take_profit, expiration_time, account_login
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description sort_mode EnumOrderHistorySortType Sort order; default HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC. from_time datetime, optional Start of the window (UTC). to_time datetime, optional End of the window (UTC). page_number int, optional Zero-based page index. items_per_page int, optional Page size. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrdersHistoryData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description orders_info list[HistoryOrderInfo] The closed orders for this page total_count int Total orders matching the query (across pages) next_page_token str Token/cursor for the next page (if paging by token)

Each HistoryOrderInfo (adds close fields to the open-order shape):

Field Python Type Description ticket int Order ticket symbol str Symbol order_type OpenedOrderType (int) Operation (OO_OP_*) lots float Volume open_price / close_price float Entry / exit price profit float Realized profit (excl. swap/commission) swap / commision float Costs (note proto spelling commision) open_time / close_time (+ _utc) datetime Entry / exit time magic_number int Expert/magic id comment str Order comment

docs.title: EnumOrderHistorySortType — input sort_mode
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning HISTORY_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC 0 By open time, ascending HISTORY_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC 1 By open time, descending HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC 2 By close time, ascending HISTORY_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC 3 By close time, descending (default) HISTORY_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_ASC 4 By ticket id, ascending HISTORY_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_DESC 5 By ticket id, descending

order_type uses the same OpenedOrderType (OO_OP_*) enum as opened_orders.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Bound the window. Pass both from_time and to_time; omitting them returns the default page of all history.
  • total_count drives paging. It's the full match count — loop pages while page_number * items_per_page < total_count.
  • Net result per trade is profit + swap + commision (costs are usually negative).
  • Balance/credit rows. As with open orders, OO_OP_BALANCE/OO_OP_CREDIT can appear — skip them for trade stats.
  • Prefer trade_stats for ratios. It computes profit factor, win rate, drawdowns for you; use orders_history when you need the raw rows.

docs.title: 1) Last 30 days — closed trades table
docs.text:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_account_helper_pb2 as ah

async def recent_history(account, days: int = 30):
    end = datetime.utcnow()
    hist = await account.orders_history(from_time=end - timedelta(days=days), to_time=end)
    print(f"{hist.total_count} closed order(s) in {days}d")
    for o in hist.orders_info[:20]:
        side = "BUY" if o.order_type == ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUY else "SELL"
        net = o.profit + o.swap + o.commision
        print(f"  #{o.ticket} {o.symbol:<8} {side:<4} {o.lots:.2f} "
              f"{o.open_price:.5f}->{o.close_price:.5f}  net={net:+.2f}")

docs.title: 2) Realized P/L and win rate for a window
docs.text:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

async def window_pnl(account, days: int = 7):
    end = datetime.utcnow()
    hist = await account.orders_history(from_time=end - timedelta(days=days), to_time=end)
    trades = [o for o in hist.orders_info]
    realized = sum(o.profit + o.swap + o.commision for o in trades)
    wins = sum(1 for o in trades if (o.profit + o.swap + o.commision) > 0)
    wr = wins / len(trades) * 100 if trades else 0.0
    print(f"{len(trades)} trades | realized {realized:+.2f} | win rate {wr:.1f}%")
    return realized

docs.title: 3) Page through a long history
docs.text:
Use total_count + items_per_page to walk every page.

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

async def all_history(account, days: int = 365, page_size: int = 100):
    end = datetime.utcnow()
    start = end - timedelta(days=days)
    out, page = [], 0
    while True:
        res = await account.orders_history(
            from_time=start, to_time=end,
            page_number=page, items_per_page=page_size,
        )
        out.extend(res.orders_info)
        if (page + 1) * page_size >= res.total_count or not res.orders_info:
            break
        page += 1
    print(f"collected {len(out)} / {res.total_count} orders")
    return out

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Costs are separate. profit excludes swap/commision — add them for the true net.
  • Window required for meaningful results. Without from_time/to_time you get the default page, not "everything".
  • Page bounds. Stop when you've collected total_count (or a page comes back empty) to avoid an infinite loop.
  • Proto spelling: commision (single s).

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Known window. On a demo account with history, len(orders_info) <= total_count and timestamps fall inside [from_time, to_time].
  • Round-trip. Open then close an order, then query a window covering now — the ticket appears with a close_time and realized profit.
  • Paging. With items_per_page smaller than total_count, concatenated pages equal the full set with no duplicates.

docs.title: Quote
docs.text:
The latest quote for a single symbol — bid, ask, day high/low and timestamp.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.quote(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: Quote(QuoteRequest) -> QuoteReply
  • Payload: QuoteData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A one-shot price read for one symbol: current bid/ask, session high/low, and the quote time.
  • Why you need it. To read the market before placing or managing an order.
  • When to use. Single reads. For a continuous feed, use on_symbol_tick.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Current bid / ask for a symbol
  • Session high / low
  • Quote timestamp (server / UTC)
  • Compute spread and check tradability

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def quote(
    self,
    symbol: str,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message QuoteRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
}

Payload message:

message QuoteData {
  string symbol = 1;
  double bid = 2;
  double ask = 3;
  Timestamp date_time = 4;
  Timestamp date_time_utc = 5;
  double high = 6;      // session high
  double low = 7;       // session low
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol str Symbol name, e.g. "EURUSD". deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — QuoteData
docs.text: Field Python Type Description symbol str Symbol bid float Current bid (you sell at bid) ask float Current ask (you buy at ask) high / low float Session high / low date_time / date_time_utc datetime Quote time (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Spread = ask − bid. In price terms; divide by the symbol's pip size to express it in pips.
  • Buy at ask, sell at bid. A market buy fills near ask, a market sell near bid — the spread is the immediate cost of entry.
  • Time field is date_time (not time). It's a protobuf Timestamp — convert with .ToDatetime().
  • One symbol per call. For several symbols use quote_many; for a live stream use on_symbol_tick.
  • Market Watch. If a broker returns no price, the symbol may need selecting first — see symbol_select.

docs.title: 1) Bid / ask / spread
docs.text:
async def show_quote(account, symbol: str = "EURUSD"):
    q = await account.quote(symbol)
    spread = q.ask - q.bid
    print(f"{q.symbol}: bid={q.bid:.5f} ask={q.ask:.5f} spread={spread:.5f}")
    return q

docs.title: 2) Only trade when the spread is tight
docs.text:
A guard you call before entering — skip entries when the spread is abnormally wide (news, illiquid hours).

async def spread_ok(account, symbol: str, max_spread: float) -> bool:
    q = await account.quote(symbol)
    spread = q.ask - q.bid
    if spread > max_spread:
        print(f"{symbol}: spread {spread:.5f} > {max_spread:.5f} — skip entry")
        return False
    return True

# usage: if await spread_ok(account, "EURUSD", 0.00020): ...

docs.title: 3) Where is price in today's range?
docs.text:
Position the current mid inside the session high/low (0% = low, 100% = high).

async def range_position(account, symbol: str = "EURUSD"):
    q = await account.quote(symbol)
    mid = (q.bid + q.ask) / 2
    span = q.high - q.low
    pct = (mid - q.low) / span * 100 if span > 0 else 0.0
    print(f"{symbol}: mid={mid:.5f} in [{q.low:.5f}, {q.high:.5f}] -> {pct:.0f}% of range")
    return pct

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Snapshot, not a stream. The quote is the price at call time; don't poll it in a tight loop — use on_symbol_tick for live updates.
  • Spread is in price units. Convert to pips with the symbol's pip size (see symbol_params_many) before comparing across symbols.
  • Unselected symbols. Some brokers return an error/empty price until the symbol is in Market Watch.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. ask >= bid, both positive; low <= bid <= high (roughly) during the session.
  • Unknown symbol. A bogus name surfaces an ApiExceptionMT4, not a silent zero.
  • Spread gate. spread_ok() returns False for a tiny max_spread and True for a generous one.

docs.title: Quote History (OHLC)
docs.text:
OHLC bar history for a symbol and timeframe over a time range — candles for charts, indicators and backtests.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.quote_history(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: QuoteHistory(QuoteHistoryRequest) -> QuoteHistoryReply
  • Payload: QuoteHistoryData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A list of OHLC bars for one symbol at a chosen timeframe, between from_time and to_time.
  • Why you need it. Charting, indicators (SMA/ATR/…), and backtests.
  • When to use. Any analysis that needs candles rather than a single live price.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• OHLC bars for a timeframe (M1 … MN1)
  • Bounded by a from/to time range
  • Tick volume and spread per bar
  • Feed indicators, charts and backtests

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def quote_history(
    self,
    symbol: str,
    timeframe: ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME,
    from_time: datetime,
    to_time: datetime,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message QuoteHistoryRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME timeframe = 2;
  Timestamp fromTime = 3;      // (+ fromTimeUtc)
  Timestamp toTime = 5;        // (+ toTimeUtc)
}

Payload message:

message QuoteHistoryData {
  repeated HistoryQuote historical_quotes = 1;
}

message HistoryQuote {
  string symbol = 1;
  int32 index = 2;
  Timestamp time = 3;
  Timestamp time_utc = 4;
  double open = 5;
  double close = 6;
  double high = 7;
  double low = 8;
  int64 real_volume = 9;
  int64 tick_volume = 10;
  int32 spread = 11;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol str Symbol name. timeframe ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME Bar timeframe (QH_PERIOD_*). from_time datetime Start of the range (UTC). to_time datetime End of the range (UTC). deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — QuoteHistoryData
docs.text:
historical_quotes — a list of HistoryQuote bars:

Field Python Type Description time / time_utc datetime Bar open time (server / UTC) open / high / low / close float OHLC prices tick_volume int Number of ticks in the bar real_volume int Real volume (0 if the broker doesn't provide it) spread int Spread at the bar, in points symbol str Symbol index int Bar index in the series

docs.title: ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME — input timeframe
docs.text:
Constant Meaning QH_PERIOD_M1 1 minute QH_PERIOD_M5 5 minutes QH_PERIOD_M15 15 minutes QH_PERIOD_M30 30 minutes QH_PERIOD_H1 1 hour QH_PERIOD_H4 4 hours QH_PERIOD_D1 1 day QH_PERIOD_W1 1 week QH_PERIOD_MN1 1 month

Access via market_info_pb2.ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME.QH_PERIOD_H1. (Note: this is the market_info enum the method expects — not the similarly named QHB_PERIOD_* from the standalone quote_history module.)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Use the right enum. The method expects market_info_pb2.ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME (QH_PERIOD_*). Passing a value from another module won't match.
  • from_time / to_time are required and are datetimes (UTC) — the range bounds the number of bars you get back.
  • tick_volume vs real_volume. On FX most brokers report tick volume; real_volume is often 0.
  • Bars are time-ordered by time; index is their position in the series.
  • For a single live price use quote; for a live stream use on_symbol_tick.

docs.title: 1) Fetch the last N hourly bars
docs.text:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_market_info_pb2 as mi

async def recent_bars(account, symbol: str = "EURUSD", hours: int = 48):
    end = datetime.utcnow()
    data = await account.quote_history(
        symbol, mi.ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME.QH_PERIOD_H1,
        end - timedelta(hours=hours), end,
    )
    bars = data.historical_quotes
    print(f"{len(bars)} H1 bars")
    for b in bars[-3:]:
        print(f"  {b.time.ToDatetime():%m-%d %H:%M}  O={b.open:.5f} H={b.high:.5f} "
              f"L={b.low:.5f} C={b.close:.5f} vol={b.tick_volume}")
    return bars

docs.title: 2) Simple moving average of closes
docs.text:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_market_info_pb2 as mi

async def sma(account, symbol: str, period: int = 20):
    end = datetime.utcnow()
    data = await account.quote_history(
        symbol, mi.ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME.QH_PERIOD_H1,
        end - timedelta(hours=period * 2), end,
    )
    closes = [b.close for b in data.historical_quotes][-period:]
    if len(closes) < period:
        return None
    value = sum(closes) / period
    print(f"SMA({period}) {symbol} = {value:.5f}")
    return value

docs.title: 3) Average daily range (last 14 days)
docs.text:
A quick ATR-style volatility read from daily bars.

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_market_info_pb2 as mi

async def avg_daily_range(account, symbol: str = "EURUSD", days: int = 14):
    end = datetime.utcnow()
    data = await account.quote_history(
        symbol, mi.ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME.QH_PERIOD_D1,
        end - timedelta(days=days * 2), end,
    )
    ranges = [b.high - b.low for b in data.historical_quotes][-days:]
    adr = sum(ranges) / len(ranges) if ranges else 0.0
    print(f"ADR({days}) {symbol} = {adr:.5f}")
    return adr

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Wrong timeframe enum. Use market_info_pb2.ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME.QH_PERIOD_* — not QHB_PERIOD_* from the other module.
  • Range too wide. A tight timeframe over a long range returns a lot of bars — scope the window to what you need.
  • Partial last bar. The most recent bar may still be forming; treat it as provisional.
  • Empty result. Weekends/holidays or an out-of-session range can yield few or no bars — guard before indexing.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. H1 over the last 48h returns a sensible bar count with high >= low and low <= close <= high.
  • Ordering. Bars are ascending in time; the last bar's time is close to now.
  • Timeframe scaling. D1 over 14 days returns ~10–14 bars (trading days), far fewer than H1.

docs.title: Many Quotes
docs.text:
Latest quotes for several symbols in a single round-trip.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.quote_many(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: QuoteMany(QuoteManyRequest) -> QuoteManyReply
  • Payload: QuoteManyData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A batch price read — one call returns a QuoteData for each requested symbol.
  • Why you need it. One round-trip for a basket instead of N separate quote calls.
  • When to use. Dashboards, multi-symbol strategies, correlation/spread scans.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Quotes for a list of symbols at once
  • Fewer round-trips than looping quote
  • Same per-symbol fields as a single quote

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def quote_many(
    self,
    symbols: list[str],
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message QuoteManyRequest {
  repeated string symbols = 1;
}

Payload message:

message QuoteManyData {
  repeated QuoteData quotes = 1;   // one QuoteData per symbol
}

message QuoteData {
  string symbol = 1;
  double bid = 2;
  double ask = 3;
  Timestamp date_time = 4;
  Timestamp date_time_utc = 5;
  double high = 6;
  double low = 7;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbols list[str] Symbol names, e.g. ["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"]. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — QuoteManyData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description quotes list[QuoteData] One quote per requested symbol

Each QuoteData has symbol, bid, ask, high, low, date_time / date_time_utc — see quote for the field details.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Prefer this over a loop. For several symbols, one quote_many beats N quote calls — fewer round-trips and a consistent snapshot.
  • Match by symbol, not position. Index the result by q.symbol rather than assuming the response order matches your request order.
  • Same shape as a single quote — spread is ask − bid, times are protobuf Timestamps.
  • Big baskets. Requesting many symbols is fine, but keep the list to what you actually use.

docs.title: 1) Quote a basket into a dict
docs.text:
Index by symbol so lookups are order-independent.

async def quote_basket(account, symbols: list[str]) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]]:
    data = await account.quote_many(symbols)
    by_symbol = {q.symbol: (q.bid, q.ask) for q in data.quotes}
    for sym in symbols:
        bid, ask = by_symbol.get(sym, (None, None))
        print(f"{sym:<8} bid={bid} ask={ask}")
    return by_symbol

docs.title: 2) Rank symbols by spread
docs.text:
Find which instruments are cheapest/most expensive to enter right now.

async def spreads(account, symbols: list[str]):
    data = await account.quote_many(symbols)
    rows = sorted(((q.symbol, q.ask - q.bid) for q in data.quotes), key=lambda x: x[1])
    for sym, sp in rows:
        print(f"{sym:<8} spread={sp:.5f}")
    return rows

docs.title: 3) Refresh a watchlist snapshot
docs.text:
Pull the whole watchlist at once for a dashboard tick.

WATCH = ["EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "USDJPY", "XAUUSD"]

async def watchlist(account):
    data = await account.quote_many(WATCH)
    for q in data.quotes:
        mid = (q.bid + q.ask) / 2
        print(f"{q.symbol:<8} {mid:.5f}  (bid {q.bid:.5f} / ask {q.ask:.5f})")

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Don't assume order. Map results by q.symbol; the response list may not mirror the request order, and unknown symbols may be omitted.
  • Snapshot, not a stream. For continuous updates use on_symbol_tick with a list of symbols.
  • Spreads differ by symbol. Compare in pips (via symbol_params_many) when ranking across instruments with different pip sizes.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Coverage. Requesting 3 valid symbols returns up to 3 quotes; each symbol is one of those requested.
  • Order-independence. Build the dict and assert lookups by name succeed regardless of response order.
  • Parity with single quote. A symbol's quote_many entry matches a separate quote call taken at the same moment (within tick noise).

docs.title: Server Timezone
docs.text:
The trade server's timezone / UTC offset — align timestamps and sessions to broker time.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.server_timezone(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.ServerTimezone
  • RPC: ServerTimezone(ServerTimezoneRequest) -> ServerTimezoneReply
  • Payload: ServerTimezoneData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The broker server's UTC offset (and a label/source for it).
  • Why you need it. Server timestamps are in broker time; this lets you convert to/from UTC and reason about trading sessions.
  • When to use. When displaying times, scheduling around sessions, or comparing server time to UTC.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Server UTC offset (seconds)
  • Server/timezone label
  • Source and validation info for the offset

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def server_timezone(
    self,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message ServerTimezoneRequest {
}

Payload message:

message ServerTimezoneData {
  string server = 1;             // server / timezone label
  int32 utc_offset_seconds = 2;  // offset from UTC, in seconds
  string source = 3;             // how the offset was determined
  string validated_utc = 4;      // validation reference
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — ServerTimezoneData
docs.text: Field Python Type Description server str Server / timezone label utc_offset_seconds int Offset from UTC, in seconds (e.g. 3600 = UTC+1) source str How the offset was determined validated_utc str Validation reference

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Offset is in seconds. Divide by 3600 for hours (e.g. 3600 → UTC+1, 10800 → UTC+3).
  • Server time vs UTC. account_summary returns both server_time and server_time_utc; this call gives you the offset to convert any server timestamp yourself.
  • DST. Many FX servers shift with daylight saving — read this at session start rather than hard-coding an offset.
  • Rarely changes within a session — fetch once and cache; refresh daily or on reconnect.

docs.title: 1) Print the server offset
docs.text:
async def show_timezone(account):
    tz = await account.server_timezone()
    hours = tz.utc_offset_seconds / 3600
    print(f"{tz.server}: UTC{hours:+.0f} ({tz.utc_offset_seconds}s)  source={tz.source}")
    return tz

docs.title: 2) Convert server time ↔ UTC
docs.text:
Use the offset to turn a server timestamp into UTC (and back).

from datetime import timedelta

async def server_to_utc(account, server_dt):
    tz = await account.server_timezone()
    return server_dt - timedelta(seconds=tz.utc_offset_seconds)

async def utc_to_server(account, utc_dt):
    tz = await account.server_timezone()
    return utc_dt + timedelta(seconds=tz.utc_offset_seconds)

docs.title: 3) Is it the weekend (server time)?
docs.text:
Gate trading around the broker's week using server-local time.

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

async def is_weekend_server(account) -> bool:
    tz = await account.server_timezone()
    server_now = datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=tz.utc_offset_seconds)
    return server_now.weekday() >= 5   # Sat/Sun in server time

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Seconds, not hours. utc_offset_seconds is seconds — convert before formatting.
  • DST drift. Don't cache the offset across days; brokers shift with daylight saving.
  • Session math. Trading sessions and rollover are defined in server time — convert before comparing to UTC schedules.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path. utc_offset_seconds is a plausible value (typically a multiple of 1800) and server is non-empty.
  • Consistency. account_summary().server_time minus server_time_utc roughly equals utc_offset_seconds.
  • Conversion round-trip. utc_to_server(server_to_utc(dt)) returns the original datetime.

docs.title: Symbol Parameters
docs.text:
The per-symbol rulebook: digits, lot limits, stops level, tick value, trade mode and more — for one symbol or all of them.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.symbol_params_many(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: SymbolParamsMany(SymbolParamsManyRequest) -> SymbolParamsManyReply
  • Payload: SymbolParamsManyData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The trading specification for symbols — the numbers you need to size, round and validate orders.
  • Why you need it. To normalize volume/price, respect the broker's minimum stop distance, and compute money-per-pip.
  • When to use. Before sizing or sending orders; cache the result and refresh occasionally.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Volume min / max / step / limit
  • Digits and point size (precision)
  • Stops & freeze levels (minimum SL/TP distance)
  • Tick value / tick size / contract size (P/L math)
  • Trade mode, execution mode, margin calc mode
  • Swaps, margins, base/profit/margin currencies

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def symbol_params_many(
    self,
    symbol_name: Optional[str] = None,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message SymbolParamsManyRequest {
  string symbol_name = 1;   // one symbol; omit/empty for all
}

Payload message:

message SymbolParamsManyData {
  repeated SymbolParamsManyInfo symbol_infos = 1;
}

SymbolParamsManyInfo has ~75 fields; the trading-relevant ones are below.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol_name str, optional Restrict to one symbol; omit for all symbols. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolParamsManyData
docs.text:
symbol_infos — a list of SymbolParamsManyInfo. Key fields (note the PascalCase names):

Identity & precision

Field Python Type Description SymbolName str Symbol name Digits int Price decimal places Point float Point size (e.g. 0.00001) SymDescription str Human description Path str Market Watch path/category

Volume (lots)

Field Python Type Description VolumeMin / VolumeMax float Min / max lots per order VolumeStep float Lot increment VolumeLimit float Max total volume per symbol (0 = none)

Trade rules

Field Python Type Description TradeStopsLevel int Min distance (points) for SL/TP from price TradeFreezeLevel int Freeze distance (points) near price TradeMode SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE What's allowed (full / long-only / …) TradeExeMode SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION Execution model TradeCalcMode SP_ENUM_TRADE_CALC_MODE Margin calculation mode

P/L & cost math

Field Python Type Description TradeTickValue float Money per tick for 1 lot TradeTickSize float Price change of one tick TradeContractSize float Units per lot SwapLong / SwapShort float Swap rates MarginInitial float Initial margin per lot CurrencyBase / CurrencyProfit / CurrencyMargin str Symbol currencies

Prices (Bid, BidHigh, BidLow, AskHigh, AskLow, SessionOpen, SessionClose, …) are also present for convenience.

docs.title: SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE — field TradeMode
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_DISABLED 0 Trading disabled SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_LONGONLY 1 Longs only SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_SHORTONLY 2 Shorts only SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_CLOSEONLY 3 Close only SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_FULL 4 Full access

docs.title: SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION — field TradeExeMode
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_REQUEST 0 Request execution SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_INSTANT 1 Instant execution SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_MARKET 2 Market execution SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_EXCHANGE 3 Exchange execution

docs.title: SP_ENUM_TRADE_CALC_MODE — field TradeCalcMode
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning SYMBOL_TRADE_MARGINE_CALC_MODE_FOREX 0 Forex margin calc SYMBOL_TRADE_MARGINE_CALC_MODE_FUTURES 1 Futures margin calc SYMBOL_TRADE_MARGINE_CALC_MODE_CFD 2 CFD margin calc

Access via account_helper_pb2.SP_ENUM_SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE.SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_FULL, etc.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• PascalCase field names. Most fields are Digits, Point, VolumeMin, TradeMode — capitalized, unlike the snake_case elsewhere in the API.
  • Stops level is in points, not pips. TradeStopsLevel is the minimum SL/TP distance in points — convert with Point (and remember 1 pip = 10 points on 5-digit symbols).
  • This is the source for normalization. VolumeMin/Max/Step round lots; Digits/Point round prices. MT4Sugar's normalize_lot / normalize_price are built on these.
  • Request one or all. Pass symbol_name for a single symbol; omit it to fetch the whole table (can be large).
  • Cache it. These rarely change intraday — fetch once and reuse, refreshing occasionally.

docs.title: 1) Normalize a lot to the broker's rules
docs.text:
Round any desired volume into the allowed [min, max] range on the correct step.

async def normalize_lot(account, symbol: str, lots: float) -> float:
    info = (await account.symbol_params_many(symbol)).symbol_infos[0]
    step, lo, hi = info.VolumeStep, info.VolumeMin, info.VolumeMax
    lots = max(lo, min(hi, lots))
    steps = round(lots / step)
    return round(steps * step, 8)

# normalize_lot(account, "EURUSD", 0.0234) -> 0.02

docs.title: 2) Is my SL far enough from price?
docs.text:
Validate a stop distance against TradeStopsLevel before sending an order.

async def sl_distance_ok(account, symbol: str, sl_distance_price: float) -> bool:
    info = (await account.symbol_params_many(symbol)).symbol_infos[0]
    min_distance = info.TradeStopsLevel * info.Point
    if sl_distance_price < min_distance:
        print(f"SL too close: {sl_distance_price:.5f} < min {min_distance:.5f}")
        return False
    return True

docs.title: 3) Money per pip for a lot
docs.text:
Compute the P/L value of one pip for sizing by risk.

async def money_per_pip(account, symbol: str, lots: float = 1.0) -> float:
    info = (await account.symbol_params_many(symbol)).symbol_infos[0]
    # pip = 10 points on 5/3-digit symbols, else 1 point
    pip_points = 10 if info.Digits in (3, 5) else 1
    value = info.TradeTickValue * (pip_points * info.Point / info.TradeTickSize) * lots
    print(f"{symbol}: ~{value:.2f} {info.CurrencyProfit} per pip for {lots} lot")
    return value

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• PascalCase, not snake_case. info.VolumeMin, not info.volume_min — an easy AttributeError.
  • Points vs pips. TradeStopsLevel, TradeFreezeLevel and Point are in points; convert to pips before comparing to pip-based SL/TP.
  • TradeStopsLevel may be 0. Some brokers report 0 (no minimum) — your SL/TP can then sit anywhere, but still normalize to Digits.
  • Large payload for "all". Omitting symbol_name returns every symbol — request one when you only need one.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Single symbol. symbol_params_many("EURUSD").symbol_infos has one entry with SymbolName == "EURUSD".
  • Normalization. normalize_lot(..., 0.0234) returns a multiple of VolumeStep within [VolumeMin, VolumeMax].
  • All symbols. Omitting symbol_name returns many entries; each has positive Digits and VolumeStep.

docs.title: Symbol Select (Market Watch)
docs.text:
Add a symbol to, or remove it from, Market Watch.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.symbol_select(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolSelect(SymbolSelectRequest) -> SymbolSelectReply
  • Payload: SymbolSelectData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Toggle a symbol in the terminal's Market Watch (select = add, deselect = remove).
  • Why you need it. Some brokers won't quote or trade a symbol until it's selected.
  • When to use. Before quoting/trading a symbol that might not be in Market Watch yet.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Add a symbol to Market Watch
  • Remove a symbol from Market Watch
  • Confirm the operation via success

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def symbol_select(
    self,
    symbol: str,
    select: bool = True,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message SymbolSelectRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  bool select = 2;     // True = add to Market Watch, False = remove
}

Payload message:

message SymbolSelectData {
  bool success = 1;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol str Symbol name. select bool True to add to Market Watch, False to remove. Default True. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolSelectData
docs.text: Field Python Type Description success bool True if the select/deselect was applied

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Select before you quote/trade symbols that aren't in Market Watch — some brokers reject data/orders for unselected symbols.
  • Deselect to tidy up (select=False), but don't remove a symbol that still has open orders or active subscriptions.
  • Idempotent-ish. Selecting an already-selected symbol just returns success=True.
  • Validate the name first with symbols — selecting a non-existent symbol fails.

docs.title: 1) Ensure a symbol is ready to use
docs.text:
A helper to call before quoting/trading an unfamiliar symbol.

async def ensure_selected(account, symbol: str) -> bool:
    res = await account.symbol_select(symbol, True)
    if not res.success:
        print(f"could not select {symbol}")
    return res.success

# usage:
# if await ensure_selected(account, "XAUUSD"):
#     q = await account.quote("XAUUSD")

docs.title: 2) Add then remove
docs.text:
async def temp_select(account, symbol: str):
    await account.symbol_select(symbol, True)
    q = await account.quote(symbol)
    print(f"{symbol}: bid={q.bid} ask={q.ask}")
    await account.symbol_select(symbol, False)   # tidy up

docs.title: 3) Prepare a watchlist
docs.text:
Select everything a strategy needs up front.

async def prepare_watchlist(account, symbols: list[str]):
    ok = {}
    for s in symbols:
        ok[s] = (await account.symbol_select(s, True)).success
    missing = [s for s, good in ok.items() if not good]
    if missing:
        print("failed to select:", missing)
    return ok

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Invalid symbol. Selecting a name that isn't on the account fails (or raises) — resolve it against symbols first.
  • Don't deselect active symbols. Removing a symbol with open orders or live streams can disrupt them.
  • Selection ≠ data guarantee. success=True means it's in Market Watch; the first quote may still lag a moment while it populates.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Select a valid symbol. Returns success=True; a following quote works.
  • Deselect. select=False returns success=True for a selected symbol.
  • Invalid name. A bogus symbol returns success=False or raises ApiExceptionMT4.

docs.title: Symbols
docs.text:
The full list of symbols available on the account — names and their index.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.symbols(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: Symbols(SymbolsRequest) -> SymbolsReply
  • Payload: SymbolsData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Every instrument the broker exposes on this account, as (name, index) pairs.
  • Why you need it. To discover tradable symbols at runtime and validate user input.
  • When to use. On startup, when building symbol pickers, or before quoting/trading an unknown name.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Full symbol list from the broker
  • Validate a symbol name before using it
  • Build lookups (name → index) for other calls

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def symbols(
    self,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message SymbolsRequest {
}

Payload message:

message SymbolsData {
  repeated SymbolNameInfo SymbolNameInfos = 1;
}

message SymbolNameInfo {
  string symbol_name = 1;
  int32 symbol_index = 2;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolsData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description SymbolNameInfos list[SymbolNameInfo] All available symbols

Each SymbolNameInfo:

Field Python Type Description symbol_name str Symbol name (e.g. "EURUSD") symbol_index int Broker-assigned index

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Mind the field name. The repeated field is SymbolNameInfos (PascalCase) — data.SymbolNameInfos, not symbol_name_infos.
  • Names are the broker's. Symbols may carry suffixes (EURUSD.m, EURUSD-ECN) — never assume the bare "EURUSD" exists; check the list.
  • This is the catalog, not the rules. For lot limits, digits and trade mode, use symbol_params_many; for prices, use quote.
  • Market Watch. Some brokers require a symbol be selected before quoting it — see symbol_select.

docs.title: 1) List and count
docs.text:
async def list_symbols(account):
    data = await account.symbols()
    names = [s.symbol_name for s in data.SymbolNameInfos]
    print(f"{len(names)} symbols, e.g. {names[:8]}")
    return names

docs.title: 2) Does a symbol exist (allowing suffixes)?
docs.text:
Validate a desired symbol, tolerating broker suffixes.

async def resolve_symbol(account, wanted: str = "EURUSD"):
    data = await account.symbols()
    names = [s.symbol_name for s in data.SymbolNameInfos]
    if wanted in names:
        return wanted
    # fall back to the first name that starts with the base symbol
    matches = [n for n in names if n.startswith(wanted)]
    if matches:
        print(f"'{wanted}' not found; using '{matches[0]}'")
        return matches[0]
    raise ValueError(f"no symbol matching {wanted!r}")

docs.title: 3) Name → index map
docs.text:
Build a lookup you can reuse elsewhere.

async def symbol_index_map(account) -> dict[str, int]:
    data = await account.symbols()
    return {s.symbol_name: s.symbol_index for s in data.SymbolNameInfos}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Wrong field name. It's SymbolNameInfos (capital S, plural) — a common AttributeError source.
  • Suffixes. Don't hard-code "EURUSD"; resolve against the real list to survive brokers that use suffixes.
  • Catalog only. No prices or trading rules here — pair with quote / symbol_params_many.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Non-empty. On a connected demo account, SymbolNameInfos has many entries and names are unique.
  • Resolution. resolve_symbol("EURUSD") returns a real name present in the list.
  • Map integrity. The name→index map has the same length as the symbol list (no duplicate names).

docs.title: Tick Value & Size
docs.text:
Tick value, tick size and contract size per symbol — the inputs for P/L and risk-based position sizing.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.tick_value_with_size(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: TickValueWithSize(TickValueWithSizeRequest) -> TickValueWithSizeReply
  • Payload: TickValueWithSizeData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. For each requested symbol: the money value of one tick, the price size of one tick, and the contract size (units per lot).
  • Why you need it. To turn pips into money — money-per-pip, P/L estimates, and risk-based lot sizing.
  • When to use. When computing position size from a dollar/percent risk, or valuing a move.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Tick value (money per tick for 1 lot)
  • Tick size (price change of one tick)
  • Contract size (units per lot)
  • Lightweight — just the numbers needed for sizing

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def tick_value_with_size(
    self,
    symbol_names: list[str],
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message TickValueWithSizeRequest {
  repeated string symbol_names = 1;
}

Payload message:

message TickValueWithSizeData {
  repeated SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo infos = 1;
}

message SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo {
  int32 index = 1;
  string symbolName = 2;
  double TradeTickValue = 3;      // money per tick, 1 lot
  double TradeTickSize = 4;       // price change per tick
  double TradeContractSize = 5;   // units per lot
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol_names list[str] Symbols to query, e.g. ["EURUSD", "XAUUSD"]. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — TickValueWithSizeData
docs.text:
infos — a list of SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo:

Field Python Type Description symbolName str Symbol (note camelCase) TradeTickValue float Money value of one tick, for 1 lot (in deposit currency) TradeTickSize float Price change of one tick TradeContractSize float Units per lot index int Position in the request

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• This is the subset of symbol_params_many needed for sizing — use this when you only need the tick/contract numbers for several symbols at once.
  • Money per pip = TradeTickValue × (pip_size / TradeTickSize), where pip_size is 10 × point on 5/3-digit FX (get Point/Digits from symbol_params_many).
  • Field names are mixed case. symbolName is camelCase; TradeTickValue / TradeTickSize / TradeContractSize are PascalCase.
  • Values are per 1 lot in the account's deposit currency — multiply by your lot size.
  • MT4Sugar builds on this for calc_lot_by_risk / calc_cash_risk.

docs.title: 1) Tick value for a basket
docs.text:
async def tick_values(account, symbols: list[str]):
    data = await account.tick_value_with_size(symbols)
    for i in data.infos:
        print(f"{i.symbolName:<8} tick_value={i.TradeTickValue:.5f} "
              f"tick_size={i.TradeTickSize:.5f} contract={i.TradeContractSize:.0f}")
    return {i.symbolName: i for i in data.infos}

docs.title: 2) Money per pip
docs.text:
Convert tick value to per-pip value (needs the symbol's pip size).

async def money_per_pip(account, symbol: str, lots: float = 1.0) -> float:
    tv = (await account.tick_value_with_size([symbol])).infos[0]
    p  = (await account.symbol_params_many(symbol)).symbol_infos[0]
    pip_size = p.Point * (10 if p.Digits in (3, 5) else 1)
    value = tv.TradeTickValue * (pip_size / tv.TradeTickSize) * lots
    print(f"{symbol}: {value:.2f} per pip for {lots} lot")
    return value

docs.title: 3) Risk-based lot size
docs.text:
Size a position so a stop-loss hit costs a fixed amount.

async def lot_for_risk(account, symbol: str, risk_amount: float, sl_pips: float) -> float:
    mpp = await money_per_pip(account, symbol, lots=1.0)   # per-pip for 1 lot
    if mpp <= 0 or sl_pips <= 0:
        return 0.0
    raw = risk_amount / (sl_pips * mpp)
    # round to the broker's volume step
    p = (await account.symbol_params_many(symbol)).symbol_infos[0]
    lots = max(p.VolumeMin, min(p.VolumeMax, round(raw / p.VolumeStep) * p.VolumeStep))
    print(f"risk {risk_amount:.2f} @ {sl_pips} pip SL -> {lots:.2f} lot")
    return round(lots, 2)

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Mixed-case fields. symbolName (camelCase) but TradeTickValue (PascalCase) — match them exactly.
  • Per 1 lot. Remember to scale by lot size; the raw values assume one lot.
  • Pip vs tick. Tick ≠ pip. Convert via the symbol's pip size (Point/Digits from symbol_params_many).
  • Deposit currency. TradeTickValue is already in your account currency — no FX conversion needed.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Known symbol. For EURUSD on a USD account, TradeTickValue ≈ 1.0 for 1 lot at 0.00001 tick size.
  • Batch. Requesting 3 symbols returns up to 3 infos; match by symbolName.
  • Sizing sanity. lot_for_risk(risk=50, sl_pips=50) on EURUSD returns ~0.10 lot (≈ $1/pip) — adjust for the actual tick value.

docs.title: MT4Account — Trading Operations — Overview
docs.text: Send market/pending orders, modify SL/TP/price, close or delete, and close-by.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• Order Send — Send a market or pending order.
  • Order Modify — Modify an existing order's price, SL, TP or expiration.
  • Order Close / Delete — Close a market order (fully or partially) or delete a pending order.
  • Order Close By — Close an order by an opposite order on the same symbol.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text:
Method What it does order_send Send a market or pending order. order_modify Modify an existing order's price, SL, TP or expiration. order_close_delete Close a market order (fully or partially) or delete a pending order. order_close_by Close an order by an opposite order on the same symbol.
  • Back to: MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Order Close By
docs.text:
Close an order by an opposite order on the same symbol — net a hedge in one operation.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.order_close_by(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderCloseBy(OrderCloseByRequest) -> OrderCloseByReply
  • Payload: OrderCloseByData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Closes one order using an opposite-direction order on the same symbol, netting them against each other.
  • Why you need it. To unwind a hedge (a buy and a sell on the same symbol) in a single operation instead of closing each leg.
  • When to use. When you hold opposite orders on one symbol and want to net them.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Close-by between two opposite tickets
  • Net a hedge in one call
  • Get the resulting close price / profit

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def order_close_by(
    self,
    ticket_to_close: int,
    opposite_ticket_closing_by: int,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OrderCloseByRequest {
  int32 ticket_to_close = 1;
  int32 opposite_ticket_closing_by = 2;
}

Payload message:

message OrderCloseByData {
  double close_price = 1;
  double profit = 2;
  Timestamp close_time = 3;
  Timestamp close_time_utc = 4;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description ticket_to_close int The ticket to be closed. opposite_ticket_closing_by int The opposite-direction ticket used to close it. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseByData
docs.text: Field Python Type Description close_price float Price at which the close-by settled profit float Realized profit from the operation close_time / close_time_utc datetime Close time (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Both legs must be opposite and same-symbol. A BUY and a SELL on the same instrument; close-by nets them.
  • Order of tickets matters. ticket_to_close is the one being closed; opposite_ticket_closing_by is the counter order.
  • Broker support varies. Not all brokers allow close-by (and hedging must be permitted); unsupported setups raise ApiExceptionMT4.
  • Alternative: close each leg independently with order_close_delete if close-by isn't available.
  • Market must be open — a closed session raises ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132).

docs.title: 1) Close one order by another
docs.text:
async def close_by(account, ticket: int, opposite: int):
    res = await account.order_close_by(ticket_to_close=ticket,
                                       opposite_ticket_closing_by=opposite)
    print(f"closed #{ticket} by #{opposite}: profit={res.profit:+.2f} @ {res.close_price:.5f}")
    return res

docs.title: 2) Net a hedge on a symbol
docs.text:
Find a buy and a sell on the same symbol and close them against each other.

import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_account_helper_pb2 as ah

async def net_hedge(account, symbol: str):
    data = await account.opened_orders()
    buys  = [o for o in data.order_infos if o.symbol == symbol and o.order_type == ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_BUY]
    sells = [o for o in data.order_infos if o.symbol == symbol and o.order_type == ah.OpenedOrderType.OO_OP_SELL]
    if buys and sells:
        res = await account.order_close_by(ticket_to_close=buys[0].ticket,
                                            opposite_ticket_closing_by=sells[0].ticket)
        print(f"netted {symbol}: profit={res.profit:+.2f}")
        return res
    print(f"no opposite pair on {symbol}")

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Must be a true opposite pair. Same symbol, opposite directions — otherwise the call is rejected.
  • Hedging may be disabled. Brokers that forbid hedging (or close-by) raise ApiExceptionMT4; fall back to order_close_delete.
  • Market closed. Raises ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132) on a closed session.
  • Exceptions, not codes. Wrap in try/except.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (market open, hedging allowed). Open a BUY and a SELL 0.01 on one symbol, then order_close_by → both leave opened_orders.
  • Unsupported. On a non-hedging broker, assert the call raises rather than silently doing nothing.
  • Result fields. close_price and close_time are populated on success.

docs.title: Order Close / Delete
docs.text:
Close a market order (fully or partially) or delete a pending order — one call for both.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.order_close_delete(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderCloseDelete(OrderCloseDeleteRequest) -> OrderCloseDeleteReply
  • Payload: OrderCloseDeleteData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Closes a filled market order (whole or part) or removes a resting pending order — the server picks the right action by order type.
  • Why you need it. To exit positions, take partial profit, or cancel pendings.
  • When to use. Taking profit/loss, scaling out, or cleanup. MT4Sugar's close / close_all / cancel_pendings wrap this.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Close a market order in full
  • Partially close a market order (pass lots)
  • Delete a pending order
  • Learn which action happened via mode

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def order_close_delete(
    self,
    order_ticket: int,
    lots: Optional[float] = None,
    closing_price: Optional[float] = None,
    slippage: Optional[int] = None,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OrderCloseDeleteRequest {
  int32 order_ticket = 1;
  double lots = 2;            // partial close volume; omit for full
  double closing_price = 3;   // market close price (optional)
  int32 slippage = 4;
}

Payload message:

message OrderCloseDeleteData {
  OrderCloseDeleteMode mode = 1;        // which action happened
  string history_order_comment = 2;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description order_ticket int Ticket to close or delete. lots float, optional Lots to close (partial); omit to close in full. closing_price float, optional Closing price for market orders. slippage int, optional Max slippage in points. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseDeleteData
docs.text: Field Python Type Description mode OrderCloseDeleteMode (int) Whether a market order was closed or a pending deleted history_order_comment str Resulting history/close comment

docs.title: OrderCloseDeleteMode — field mode
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning OCD_MARKET_ORDER 0 A market order was closed OCD_PENDING_ORDER 1 A pending order was deleted

Access via trading_helper_pb2.OrderCloseDeleteMode.OCD_MARKET_ORDER.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call, both actions. You don't choose close-vs-delete — the server does it based on the order type and reports it in mode.
  • Partial close. Pass lots smaller than the order's volume; the remainder stays open as a separate ticket.
  • Pending deletes ignore lots. For a pending order the whole thing is removed.
  • Market must be open to close a market order — a weekend/closed market raises ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132).
  • Bulk exits. For closing many orders use MT4Sugar's close_all / cancel_pendings rather than looping this by hand.

docs.title: 1) Close an order in full
docs.text:
async def close(account, ticket: int):
    res = await account.order_close_delete(order_ticket=ticket)
    kind = "closed market" if res.mode == 0 else "deleted pending"
    print(f"#{ticket}: {kind}")
    return res

docs.title: 2) Partial close (scale out)
docs.text:
Close half of a position, leaving the rest to run.

async def close_half(account, ticket: int, lots: float):
    half = round(lots / 2, 2)
    await account.order_close_delete(order_ticket=ticket, lots=half)
    print(f"#{ticket}: closed {half} lot, rest left open")

docs.title: 3) Close everything on a symbol
docs.text:
Pull open orders, then close each matching ticket.

async def close_symbol(account, symbol: str):
    data = await account.opened_orders()
    for o in data.order_infos:
        if o.symbol == symbol:
            try:
                await account.order_close_delete(order_ticket=o.ticket)
                print(f"closed #{o.ticket}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"#{o.ticket} failed: {e}")

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Market closed. Closing a market order when the session is closed raises ERR_MARKET_CLOSED (132) — pendings can still usually be deleted.
  • Partial close limits. lots must respect the symbol's volume step and be ≤ the order's volume.
  • Exceptions, not codes. Failures raise ApiExceptionMT4; wrap in try/except.
  • Already closed. Closing a ticket that's gone raises — tolerate it in cleanup loops.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Round-trip (market open). order_send then order_close_delete → mode == OCD_MARKET_ORDER; the ticket leaves opened_orders.
  • Pending delete. Place a pending order and delete it → mode == OCD_PENDING_ORDER.
  • Partial. Close part of a 0.02 position and assert a 0.01 remainder stays open.

docs.title: Order Modify
docs.text:
Change an existing order's SL, TP, pending price or expiration.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.order_modify(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderModify(OrderModifyRequest) -> OrderModifyReply
  • Payload: OrderModifyData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Updates SL/TP (and, for pending orders, the entry price / expiration) of an order that already exists.
  • Why you need it. To manage live orders without closing them — trailing stops, breakeven, re-pricing pendings.
  • When to use. Any time you adjust protection or a pending price. MT4Sugar's modify_sl_tp_by_price / modify_sl_tp_by_pips wrap this.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Change SL / TP on a live order
  • Re-price a pending order
  • Update a pending order's expiration

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def order_modify(
    self,
    order_ticket: int,
    new_price: Optional[float] = None,
    new_stop_loss: Optional[float] = None,
    new_take_profit: Optional[float] = None,
    new_expiration: Optional[datetime] = None,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OrderModifyRequest {
  int32 order_ticket = 1;
  double new_price = 2;              // pending-order price
  double new_stop_loss = 3;
  double new_take_profit = 4;
  Timestamp new_expiration = 5;      // (+ new_expiration_utc)
}

Payload message:

message OrderModifyData {
  bool order_was_modified = 1;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description order_ticket int Ticket to modify. new_price float, optional New pending-order price (ignored for filled market orders). new_stop_loss float, optional New SL price. new_take_profit float, optional New TP price. new_expiration datetime, optional New expiration (pending orders). deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderModifyData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description order_was_modified bool True if the change was applied

On failure the call raises ApiExceptionMT4 — e.g. ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130) when SL/TP is too close, or ERR_NO_RESULT/ERR_TRADE_MODIFY_DENIED (145) when nothing changed or the order is too near market.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Prices, not pips. new_stop_loss / new_take_profit are absolute prices — convert from pips yourself (or use MT4Sugar's modify_sl_tp_by_pips).
  • Pass only what changes. Supply just the fields you want to update; leave the rest None.
  • Respect the stops level. New SL/TP must be at least TradeStopsLevel points from price (symbol_params_many).
  • Pending vs market. new_price/new_expiration only make sense for pending orders; for filled market orders, modify SL/TP.
  • No-op is an error on some brokers. Submitting unchanged values can raise rather than silently succeed — only call when something actually changes.

docs.title: 1) Set SL and TP on an order
docs.text:
async def set_stops(account, ticket: int, sl: float, tp: float) -> bool:
    res = await account.order_modify(ticket, new_stop_loss=sl, new_take_profit=tp)
    print("modified" if res.order_was_modified else "no change")
    return res.order_was_modified

docs.title: 2) Trail the stop (move SL only)
docs.text:
Raise the stop on a long as price advances — one trailing step.

async def trail_stop(account, ticket: int, symbol: str, distance_pips: float = 20):
    q = await account.quote(symbol)
    info = (await account.symbol_params_many(symbol)).symbol_infos[0]
    pip = info.Point * (10 if info.Digits in (3, 5) else 1)
    new_sl = round(q.bid - distance_pips * pip, info.Digits)   # for a BUY
    await account.order_modify(ticket, new_stop_loss=new_sl)
    print(f"SL -> {new_sl}")

docs.title: 3) Re-price a pending order
docs.text:
Move a resting BUY LIMIT to a new level.

async def reprice_pending(account, ticket: int, new_price: float):
    res = await account.order_modify(ticket, new_price=round(new_price, 5))
    return res.order_was_modified

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Absolute prices. SL/TP/price are prices, not distances — compute them before calling.
  • Too-close stops. Violating TradeStopsLevel raises ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130).
  • No-change calls. Re-submitting identical values may raise (ERR_TRADE_MODIFY_DENIED 145 / no result) — guard against it.
  • Exceptions, not codes. Failures raise ApiExceptionMT4; wrap in try/except.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (market open). Modifying SL/TP of an open order returns order_was_modified == True and the new values show in opened_orders.
  • Too-close SL. A stop inside TradeStopsLevel raises ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130).
  • No-op. Re-applying the same SL/TP either returns False or raises — assert your code tolerates both.

docs.title: Order Send
docs.text:
Send a market or pending order — the low-level entry point for opening trades.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.order_send(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderSend(OrderSendRequest) -> OrderSendReply
  • Payload: OrderSendData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Opens a market order or places a pending order, with optional SL/TP, comment and magic.
  • Why you need it. Full control over every order field at the lowest level.
  • When to use. When you need raw control. For pips-based SL/TP, normalization and risk sizing, prefer MT4Sugar (buy_market, buy_limit, …) which wraps this.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Open market orders (BUY / SELL)
  • Place pending orders (LIMIT / STOP)
  • Attach SL / TP, comment and magic number
  • Set slippage and pending-order expiration

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def order_send(
    self,
    symbol: str,
    operation_type: OrderSendOperationType,
    volume: float,
    price: Optional[float] = None,
    slippage: Optional[int] = None,
    stoploss: Optional[float] = None,
    takeprofit: Optional[float] = None,
    comment: Optional[str] = None,
    magic_number: Optional[int] = None,
    expiration: Optional[datetime] = None,
    deadline: Optional[datetime] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OrderSendRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  OrderSendOperationType operation_type = 2;
  double volume = 3;
  double price = 4;
  int32 slippage = 5;
  double stoploss = 6;
  double takeprofit = 7;
  string comment = 8;
  int32 magic_number = 9;
  Timestamp expiration = 10;      // (+ expiration_utc)
}

Payload message:

message OrderSendData {
  int32 ticket = 1;
  double volume = 2;
  double price = 3;
  Timestamp open_time = 4;
  Timestamp open_time_utc = 5;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol str Symbol name. operation_type OrderSendOperationType Buy/sell, market or pending (see enum). volume float Lots. price float, optional Entry price — required for pending orders; for market orders it can be omitted. slippage int, optional Max slippage in points (market orders). stoploss float, optional Stop-loss price (0 / omit for none). takeprofit float, optional Take-profit price (0 / omit for none). comment str, optional Order comment. magic_number int, optional Expert/magic id to tag the order. expiration datetime, optional Expiration for pending orders. deadline datetime, optional Absolute UTC deadline for the gRPC call. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to abort the request.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderSendData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description ticket int Ticket of the new order volume float Filled/placed volume price float Fill price (market) or pending price open_time / open_time_utc datetime Open/placement time (server / UTC)

On failure the call raises ApiExceptionMT4 — inspect e.error.mql_error_int_code / e.error.mql_error_description (see the Return Codes Reference).

docs.title: OrderSendOperationType — input operation_type
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning OC_OP_BUY 0 Market buy OC_OP_SELL 1 Market sell OC_OP_BUYLIMIT 2 Buy limit (pending, below price) OC_OP_SELLLIMIT 3 Sell limit (pending, above price) OC_OP_BUYSTOP 4 Buy stop (pending, above price) OC_OP_SELLSTOP 5 Sell stop (pending, below price)

Access via trading_helper_pb2.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Market vs pending. OC_OP_BUY/OC_OP_SELL fill immediately (price optional); the *LIMIT/*STOP variants are pending and require price.
  • Absolute SL/TP prices. stoploss/takeprofit are prices, not pip distances. Respect the symbol's TradeStopsLevel (symbol_params_many) or you'll get ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130).
  • Normalize first. Round volume to VolumeStep and prices to Digits; MT4Sugar does this automatically.
  • Tag with magic_number. It's how you later identify "my" orders in opened_orders.
  • Returns a ticket on success — there is no numeric returned_code (that's MT5); errors are exceptions.

docs.title: 🔗 Usage Examples
docs.text: ⚠️ These place real orders on the connected (demo) account. Use 0.01 lots and clean up.

docs.title: 1) Open a market BUY
docs.text:
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_trading_helper_pb2 as th

async def buy(account, symbol="EURUSD", lots=0.01):
    res = await account.order_send(symbol, th.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, lots)
    print(f"opened #{res.ticket} {res.volume} lot @ {res.price:.5f}")
    return res.ticket

docs.title: 2) Market SELL with SL/TP, comment and magic
docs.text:
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_trading_helper_pb2 as th

async def sell_with_stops(account, symbol="EURUSD", lots=0.01):
    q = await account.quote(symbol)
    sl = round(q.bid + 0.0020, 5)   # 20 pips above for a short
    tp = round(q.bid - 0.0030, 5)   # 30 pips below
    res = await account.order_send(
        symbol, th.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_SELL, lots,
        stoploss=sl, takeprofit=tp, comment="demo sell", magic_number=777,
    )
    print(f"opened #{res.ticket} SL={sl} TP={tp}")
    return res.ticket

docs.title: 3) Place a BUY LIMIT below the market
docs.text:
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_trading_helper_pb2 as th

async def buy_limit(account, symbol="EURUSD", lots=0.01):
    q = await account.quote(symbol)
    price = round(q.ask - 0.0030, 5)   # 30 pips below current ask
    res = await account.order_send(
        symbol, th.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUYLIMIT, lots, price=price,
    )
    print(f"placed BUY LIMIT #{res.ticket} @ {price}")
    return res.ticket

docs.title: 4) Robust send with error handling
docs.text:
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_trading_helper_pb2 as th
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import ApiExceptionMT4
from MetaRpcMT4 import mrpc_mt4_error_pb2 as err

async def safe_buy(account, symbol="EURUSD", lots=0.01):
    try:
        res = await account.order_send(symbol, th.OrderSendOperationType.OC_OP_BUY, lots)
        return res.ticket
    except ApiExceptionMT4 as e:
        code = e.error.mql_error_int_code
        if code == err.MqlErrorCode.ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY:      # 134
            print("not enough money")
        elif code == err.MqlErrorCode.ERR_INVALID_STOPS:        # 130
            print("SL/TP too close to price")
        else:
            print(f"rejected: {e.error.mql_error_description} ({code})")
        return None

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Pending orders need price. Omitting it for a *LIMIT/*STOP order fails.
  • SL/TP are prices. And must respect TradeStopsLevel — too-close stops raise ERR_INVALID_STOPS (130).
  • Un-normalized volume/price. Values off the broker's step/digits are rejected (ERR_INVALID_TRADE_VOLUME 131 / ERR_INVALID_PRICE 129).
  • Rejections are exceptions, not a return code — always wrap trading calls in try/except ApiExceptionMT4.
  • Clean up demos. Close what you open with order_close_delete.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo). A 0.01 market BUY returns a positive ticket; the ticket appears in opened_orders.
  • Round-trip. Open then order_close_delete the ticket; it leaves opened_orders.
  • Failure path. Send an oversized volume and assert ApiExceptionMT4 with a sensible mql_error_int_code.

docs.title: MT4Account — Streaming Methods — Overview
docs.text: Real-time async generators: ticks, trade events, ticket lists and open-order profit.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• Symbol Tick Stream — Subscribe to real-time tick (bid/ask) updates for one or more symbols.
  • Trade Events Stream — Subscribe to trade events (orders opened, updated, removed).
  • Opened Order Tickets Stream — Poll-stream the live lists of open position & pending-order tickets.
  • Open-Order Profit Stream — Stream open-order profit/loss updates (plus an account snapshot).
  • Connection State Stream — Subscribe to terminal connection-state changes.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text:
Method What it does on_symbol_tick Subscribe to real-time tick (bid/ask) updates for one or more symbols. on_trade Subscribe to trade events (orders opened, updated, removed). on_opened_orders_tickets Poll-stream the live lists of open position & pending-order tickets. on_opened_orders_profit Stream open-order profit/loss updates (plus an account snapshot). on_connect_state Subscribe to terminal connection-state changes.
  • Back to: MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Connection State Stream
docs.text:
A live async stream of terminal connection-state changes.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.on_connect_state(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.Connection
  • RPC: OnConnectState(OnConnectStateRequest) -> stream of OnConnectStateReply
  • Payload: ConnectStateData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. An async generator that yields the terminal's connection state — connected/alive flags, server and account, with a timestamp.
  • Why you need it. To react to connectivity changes (drops, recoveries) for health monitoring and auto-recovery.
  • When to use. Supervising a long-running bot. Drive it with a cancellation_event.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Connected / alive flags for the terminal session
  • Server and account context
  • Event timestamps and any error message

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def on_connect_state(
    self,
    terminal_ids: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OnConnectStateRequest {
  repeated string terminal_ids = 1;   // omit for the current session
}

Payload message:

message ConnectStateData {
  string id = 1;
  string state = 2;            // e.g. "Connected"
  bool is_connected = 3;
  bool is_alive = 4;
  bool api_is_alive = 5;
  string server = 6;
  uint64 account = 7;
  string error_message = 8;
  Timestamp timestamp = 9;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description terminal_ids list[str], optional Restrict to specific terminal ids; omit for the current session. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to stop the stream.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — async generator of ConnectStateData
docs.text: Field Python Type Description state str State label (e.g. "Connected") is_connected bool Session is connected to the server is_alive bool Terminal is alive api_is_alive bool API layer is alive server str Server name account int Account login error_message str Error text, if any timestamp datetime Event time id str Terminal/session id

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• state is a string, not an enum — compare against labels like "Connected", or rely on the is_connected / is_alive booleans.
  • Three liveness flags. is_connected (to the broker), is_alive (terminal), api_is_alive (gateway) — a healthy session has all three true.
  • Check error_message when a flag flips false — it carries the reason.
  • Works regardless of market hours — it reports session health, not prices.
  • Always pass a cancellation_event and .set() it to stop — see gRPC Stream Management.

docs.title: 1) Watch connection state
docs.text:
import asyncio

async def watch_state(account, stop: asyncio.Event):
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async def pump():
        async for ev in account.on_connect_state(cancellation_event=cancel):
            print(f"{ev.state} connected={ev.is_connected} alive={ev.is_alive} "
                  f"server={ev.server}")
    task = asyncio.create_task(pump())
    await stop.wait(); cancel.set(); await asyncio.sleep(0.3); task.cancel()

docs.title: 2) Wait until connected
docs.text:
Block until the session reports a healthy state (with a timeout).

import asyncio

async def wait_connected(account, timeout=30) -> bool:
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async def watch():
        async for ev in account.on_connect_state(cancellation_event=cancel):
            if ev.is_connected and ev.is_alive:
                return True
    try:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(watch(), timeout=timeout)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        cancel.set()
        return False

docs.title: 3) Alert on disconnect
docs.text:
Fire a callback the moment connectivity drops.

import asyncio

async def on_disconnect(account, callback, stop: asyncio.Event):
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async def pump():
        async for ev in account.on_connect_state(cancellation_event=cancel):
            if not ev.is_connected or not ev.is_alive:
                callback(ev.state, ev.error_message)
    task = asyncio.create_task(pump())
    await stop.wait(); cancel.set(); await asyncio.sleep(0.3); task.cancel()

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• state is free-form text. Prefer the boolean flags over string matching where possible.
  • No cancellation = leak. Stop with a cancellation_event you .set().
  • Events are sparse. State is reported on change/heartbeat — don't expect a steady stream; use a timeout when waiting.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Healthy session. Shortly after connecting, an event has state == "Connected" with all three liveness flags true.
  • wait_connected. Returns True on a live demo session within the timeout.
  • Clean stop. cancellation_event.set() ends the loop without leaking tasks.

docs.title: Open-Order Profit Stream
docs.text:
A live P/L ticker for open orders, emitted on a timer — plus an account snapshot.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.on_opened_orders_profit(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnOpenedOrdersProfit(OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest) -> stream of OnOpenedOrdersProfitReply
  • Payload: OnOpenedOrdersProfitData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Every timer_period_milliseconds it yields the current floating P/L of each open order.
  • Why you need it. Real-time floating P/L without polling — risk dashboards, trailing/exit logic.
  • When to use. Live P/L monitoring and profit-target automation. Drive it with a cancellation_event.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Per-order live profit
  • Emission interval control
  • Account snapshot alongside each update

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def on_opened_orders_profit(
    self,
    timer_period_milliseconds: int = 1000,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest {
  int32 timerPeriodMilliseconds = 1;
}

Payload message:

message OnOpenedOrdersProfitData {
  MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE type = 1;
  repeated OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo opened_orders_with_profit_updated = 2;
  OnEventAccountInfo account_info = 3;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 4;
}

message OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo {
  int32 ticket = 2;
  string symbol = 15;
  double order_profit = 12;
  double lots = 7;
  double open_price = 9;
  double stop_loss = 13;
  double take_profit = 16;
  SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE type = 18;
  // ... comment, magic_number, swap, commission
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description timer_period_milliseconds int How often updates are emitted. Default 1000. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to stop the stream.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — async generator of OnOpenedOrdersProfitData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description type MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE Event group opened_orders_with_profit_updated list[OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo] Open orders with live P/L

Each OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo carries ticket, symbol, order_profit, lots, open_price, stop_loss, take_profit, and type (SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE).

docs.title: MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE — field type
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning OrderProfit 0 Profit-update group OrderUpdate 1 Order lifecycle change

docs.title: SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE — order type
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning SUB_OP_BUY 0 Market buy SUB_OP_SELL 1 Market sell SUB_OP_BUYLIMIT 2 Buy limit SUB_OP_SELLLIMIT 3 Sell limit SUB_OP_BUYSTOP 4 Buy stop SUB_OP_SELLSTOP 5 Sell stop

Access via subscriptions_pb2.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_BUY and subscriptions_pb2.MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE.OrderProfit.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Profit field is order_profit (not profit) on these items.
  • Timer-driven. Updates arrive on timer_period_milliseconds, independent of ticks — so you get P/L updates even between price changes.
  • Same operation enum as on_trade. Order type is SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE (SUB_OP_*).
  • Works on a closed market (it re-values current orders on a timer), though P/L won't move without price changes.
  • Always pass a cancellation_event and .set() it to stop — see gRPC Stream Management.

docs.title: 1) Live P/L per order
docs.text:
async def live_pnl(account):
    async for ev in account.on_opened_orders_profit():
        for o in ev.opened_orders_with_profit_updated:
            print(f"#{o.ticket} {o.symbol} {o.order_profit:+.2f}")

docs.title: 2) Alert on total floating loss
docs.text:
Stop and alert when aggregate floating P/L breaches a limit.

import asyncio

async def floating_guard(account, max_loss: float = -100.0):
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async for ev in account.on_opened_orders_profit(timer_period_milliseconds=2000,
                                                    cancellation_event=cancel):
        total = sum(o.order_profit for o in ev.opened_orders_with_profit_updated)
        print(f"floating: {total:+.2f}")
        if total <= max_loss:
            print(f"[ALERT] floating {total:.2f} <= {max_loss} — de-risk!")
            cancel.set()
            break

docs.title: 3) Close an order when it hits a profit target
docs.text:
Watch the stream and close the ticket once its profit reaches the target.

import asyncio

async def take_profit_at(account, ticket: int, target: float):
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async for ev in account.on_opened_orders_profit(cancellation_event=cancel):
        for o in ev.opened_orders_with_profit_updated:
            if o.ticket == ticket and o.order_profit >= target:
                await account.order_close_delete(order_ticket=ticket)
                print(f"#{ticket} hit {target:.2f} -> closed")
                cancel.set()
                return

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Field is order_profit. Not profit — a common AttributeError.
  • No cancellation = leak. Stop with a cancellation_event you .set().
  • Acting inside the loop. Closing/modifying from within the stream is fine, but keep per-tick work light.
  • Flat account. With nothing open, opened_orders_with_profit_updated is empty.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• With open orders. Each update lists your open tickets; order_profit moves with price.
  • Total. Summed order_profit roughly matches equity − balance from account_summary.
  • Clean stop. cancellation_event.set() ends the loop without leaking tasks.
