docs.title: Opened Order Tickets Stream
docs.text:
A periodic stream of the live open ticket lists — positions and pending orders.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.on_opened_orders_tickets(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnOpenedOrdersTickets(OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest) -> stream of OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply
  • Payload: OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A lightweight heartbeat: every pull_interval_milliseconds it yields the current lists of open position and pending-order tickets.
  • Why you need it. Cheap "what's open now?" monitoring without pulling full order detail.
  • When to use. Change detection and liveness. For full detail fetch opened_orders when something changes.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Separate position and pending ticket lists
  • Server-side sampling interval
  • Minimal payload for monitoring loops

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def on_opened_orders_tickets(
    self,
    pull_interval_milliseconds: int = 500,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {
  int32 pullIntervalMilliseconds = 1;
}

Payload message:

message OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData {
  repeated int32 position_tickets = 1;
  repeated int32 pending_order_tickets = 2;
  Timestamp server_time = 3;
  Timestamp server_time_utc = 4;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 5;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description pull_interval_milliseconds int How often the server samples the ticket lists. Default 500. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to stop the stream.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — async generator of OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData
docs.text: Field Python Type Description position_tickets list[int] Open position (market order) tickets pending_order_tickets list[int] Pending order tickets server_time / server_time_utc datetime Sample time (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Positions and pendings are split here — unlike the one-shot opened_orders_tickets, which returns a single flat list.
  • Tune pull_interval_milliseconds. 500 ms is responsive; raise it (e.g. 2000) to reduce chatter for slow strategies.
  • Fetch detail on change. When a ticket set changes, call opened_orders once — don't stream full detail.
  • Always pass a cancellation_event and .set() it to stop — see gRPC Stream Management.
  • This heartbeat works even on a closed market (it samples current state, not ticks).

docs.title: 1) Heartbeat of open tickets
docs.text:
async def heartbeat(account):
    async for ev in account.on_opened_orders_tickets(pull_interval_milliseconds=1000):
        print(f"positions={list(ev.position_tickets)} pending={list(ev.pending_order_tickets)}")

docs.title: 2) Detect opened / closed positions
docs.text:
Diff successive samples and act only on change.

import asyncio

async def watch_positions(account, stop: asyncio.Event):
    prev = set()
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async def pump():
        nonlocal prev
        async for ev in account.on_opened_orders_tickets(cancellation_event=cancel):
            now = set(ev.position_tickets)
            if now != prev:
                print("opened:", now - prev, "closed:", prev - now)
                prev = now
    task = asyncio.create_task(pump())
    await stop.wait(); cancel.set(); await asyncio.sleep(0.3); task.cancel()

docs.title: 3) React when a pending order appears
docs.text:
import asyncio

async def wait_for_pending(account, timeout=30):
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async def watch():
        async for ev in account.on_opened_orders_tickets(cancellation_event=cancel):
            if ev.pending_order_tickets:
                return list(ev.pending_order_tickets)
    try:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(watch(), timeout=timeout)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        cancel.set()
        return []

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Ids only. No prices/profit here — fetch opened_orders for detail.
  • No cancellation = leak. Stop with a cancellation_event you .set().
  • Interval trade-off. Too small a pull_interval_milliseconds is chatty; too large is laggy — tune to your needs.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Existing orders. With open orders, position_tickets matches the one-shot opened_orders_tickets.
  • Change detection. Open then close an order and assert the diff reports it once opened, once closed.
  • Clean stop. cancellation_event.set() ends the loop without leaking tasks.

docs.title: Symbol Tick Stream
docs.text:
A live async stream of tick (bid/ask) updates for one or more symbols.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.on_symbol_tick(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnSymbolTick(OnSymbolTickRequest) -> stream of OnSymbolTickReply
  • Payload: OnSymbolTickData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. An async generator that yields a tick every time the price of a subscribed symbol changes.
  • Why you need it. To react to price in real time instead of polling quote.
  • When to use. Live strategies, dashboards, spread/price monitors. Always drive it with a cancellation_event.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Live bid/ask per symbol
  • Subscribe to several symbols in one stream
  • Clean stop via a cancellation event

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def on_symbol_tick(
    self,
    symbols: list[str],
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OnSymbolTickRequest {
  repeated string symbol_names = 1;
}

Payload message:

message OnSymbolTickData {
  OnSymbolMqlTickInfo symbol_tick = 1;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 2;
}

message OnSymbolMqlTickInfo {
  Timestamp time = 1;
  Timestamp time_utc = 2;
  double bid = 3;
  double ask = 4;
  double last = 5;
  uint64 volume = 6;
  int64 time_msc = 7;
  int64 time_msc_utc = 8;
  string symbol = 9;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbols list[str] Symbols to subscribe to. cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to stop the stream.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — async generator of OnSymbolTickData
docs.text:
Each item has symbol_tick (OnSymbolMqlTickInfo):

Field Python Type Description symbol str Symbol bid / ask float Current bid / ask last float Last price (if provided) volume int Tick volume time / time_utc datetime Tick time (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Consume with async for. Each iteration is one tick for one of the subscribed symbols — check tick.symbol to tell them apart.
  • Always pass a cancellation_event and .set() it to stop cleanly, otherwise the stream (and its reconnect loop) keeps running — see gRPC Stream Management.
  • Auto-reconnect. Transient gRPC drops are retried under the hood; your async for keeps yielding across a reconnect.
  • No ticks on a closed market. On weekends/holidays the stream stays open but yields nothing — use a timeout so you don't block forever.
  • For a one-shot price use quote; for several at once quote_many.

docs.title: 1) Stream N ticks then stop
docs.text:
import asyncio

async def first_ticks(account, symbol="EURUSD", n=5):
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    count = 0
    async for td in account.on_symbol_tick([symbol], cancellation_event=cancel):
        t = td.symbol_tick
        print(f"{t.symbol}: bid={t.bid:.5f} ask={t.ask:.5f}")
        count += 1
        if count >= n:
            cancel.set()
            break

docs.title: 2) Keep the latest price per symbol
docs.text:
Maintain a live snapshot dict you can read from elsewhere.

import asyncio

async def live_prices(account, symbols, stop: asyncio.Event):
    latest = {}
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async def pump():
        async for td in account.on_symbol_tick(symbols, cancellation_event=cancel):
            t = td.symbol_tick
            latest[t.symbol] = (t.bid, t.ask)
    task = asyncio.create_task(pump())
    await stop.wait()          # run until the caller signals stop
    cancel.set()
    await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
    task.cancel()
    return latest

docs.title: 3) Alert on a price level
docs.text:
Stop the stream as soon as a target is hit.

import asyncio

async def wait_for_price(account, symbol, target, above=True, timeout=60):
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async def watch():
        async for td in account.on_symbol_tick([symbol], cancellation_event=cancel):
            bid = td.symbol_tick.bid
            if (above and bid >= target) or (not above and bid <= target):
                print(f"{symbol} hit {target} (bid={bid:.5f})")
                cancel.set()
                return True
    try:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(watch(), timeout=timeout)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        cancel.set()
        return False

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• No cancellation = leak. Without a cancellation_event you set, the stream and its reconnect loop run forever.
  • Blocking on a quiet market. Closed sessions yield no ticks — wrap consumption in asyncio.wait_for/asyncio.timeout.
  • Per-tick work must be fast. Heavy processing inside the loop backs up the stream — offload to a queue/task.
  • Distinguish symbols. With multiple symbols, always branch on tick.symbol.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Market open. Subscribing to a liquid symbol yields ticks within a second; ask >= bid.
  • Clean stop. After cancellation_event.set() the async for exits promptly without leaking tasks.
  • Timeout path. On a closed market, a wait_for(..., timeout=5) returns/raises rather than hanging.

docs.title: Trade Events Stream
docs.text:
A live async stream of trade events — orders opened, updated and removed.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account.on_trade(...) (defined in package/MetaRpcMT4/mt4_account.py)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnTrade(OnTradeRequest) -> stream of OnTradeReply
  • Payload: OnTradeData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. An async generator that fires whenever an order's lifecycle changes — new, modified, closed/removed.
  • Why you need it. To react instantly to order activity (monitors, copiers, dashboards) instead of polling.
  • When to use. Any event-driven logic around orders. Drive it with a cancellation_event.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• New / updated / removed order events
  • Per-order operation type (SUB_OP_*)
  • Event group type (profit vs update)
  • Account snapshot alongside each event

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
async def on_trade(
    self,
    cancellation_event: Optional[asyncio.Event] = None,
)

Request message:

message OnTradeRequest {}

Payload message:

message OnTradeData {
  MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE type = 1;
  OnTadeEventData event_data = 2;
  OnEventAccountInfo account_info = 3;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 4;
}

message OnTadeEventData {
  repeated OnTradeOrderInfo new_orders = 1;
  repeated OnTradeUpdatedOrderInfo updated_orders = 2;   // each has previous / current
  repeated OnTradeOrderInfo removed_orders = 3;
  repeated OnTradeOrderInfo new_history_orders = 4;
}

message OnTradeOrderInfo {
  int32 ticket = 2;
  string symbol = 16;
  double lots = 8;
  double open_price = 10;
  double stop_loss = 14;
  double take_profit = 17;
  double order_profit = 13;
  SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE type = 18;
  // ... is_history, comment, magic_number, close_price, close_time
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description cancellation_event asyncio.Event, optional Set to stop the stream.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — async generator of OnTradeData
docs.text:
Field Python Type Description type MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE Event group (profit vs update) event_data.new_orders list[OnTradeOrderInfo] Newly opened/placed orders event_data.updated_orders list[OnTradeUpdatedOrderInfo] Changed orders (.previous / .current) event_data.removed_orders list[OnTradeOrderInfo] Closed / deleted orders event_data.new_history_orders list[OnTradeOrderInfo] Orders that moved to history

Each OnTradeOrderInfo carries ticket, symbol, lots, open_price, stop_loss, take_profit, order_profit, and type (SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE).

docs.title: MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE — field type
docs.text: Constant Value Meaning OrderProfit 0 Profit-update group OrderUpdate 1 Order lifecycle change

docs.title: SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE — order type
docs.text:
Constant Value Meaning SUB_OP_BUY 0 Market buy SUB_OP_SELL 1 Market sell SUB_OP_BUYLIMIT 2 Buy limit SUB_OP_SELLLIMIT 3 Sell limit SUB_OP_BUYSTOP 4 Buy stop SUB_OP_SELLSTOP 5 Sell stop

Access via subscriptions_pb2.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_BUY and subscriptions_pb2.MT4_SUB_ENUM_EVENT_GROUP_TYPE.OrderUpdate.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Four buckets per event. event_data splits changes into new_orders, updated_orders, removed_orders, new_history_orders — iterate the ones you care about.
  • Updates carry before/after. Each updated_orders item has .previous and .current (both OnTradeOrderInfo) — diff them to see exactly what changed (e.g. SL/TP).
  • Order operation enum differs from trading. Streaming uses SUB_OP_* (SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE), not the OC_OP_* used by order_send — same operations, different enum.
  • Always pass a cancellation_event and .set() it to stop — see gRPC Stream Management.
  • No events without activity. If nothing trades, nothing yields — use a timeout when you expect it to be quiet.

docs.title: 1) Log new orders
docs.text:
import MetaRpcMT4.mt4_term_api_subscriptions_pb2 as sub

LABEL = {
    sub.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_BUY: "BUY",   sub.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_SELL: "SELL",
    sub.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_BUYLIMIT: "BUY LIMIT",  sub.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_SELLLIMIT: "SELL LIMIT",
    sub.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_BUYSTOP: "BUY STOP",    sub.SUB_ORDER_OPERATION_TYPE.SUB_OP_SELLSTOP: "SELL STOP",
}

async def log_new_orders(account):
    async for ev in account.on_trade():
        for o in ev.event_data.new_orders:
            print(f"[NEW] {LABEL.get(o.type,'?')} #{o.ticket} {o.symbol} @ {o.open_price:.5f}")

docs.title: 2) Watch SL/TP changes
docs.text:
Use the previous/current pair to report exactly what moved.

async def watch_modifications(account):
    async for ev in account.on_trade():
        for upd in ev.event_data.updated_orders:
            cur, prev = upd.current, upd.previous
            if (cur.stop_loss, cur.take_profit) != (prev.stop_loss, prev.take_profit):
                print(f"[MOD] #{cur.ticket} {cur.symbol} "
                      f"SL {prev.stop_loss:.5f}->{cur.stop_loss:.5f} "
                      f"TP {prev.take_profit:.5f}->{cur.take_profit:.5f}")

docs.title: 3) Fire a callback on any close
docs.text:
import asyncio

async def on_close(account, callback, stop: asyncio.Event):
    cancel = asyncio.Event()
    async def pump():
        async for ev in account.on_trade(cancellation_event=cancel):
            for o in ev.event_data.removed_orders:
                callback(o)
    task = asyncio.create_task(pump())
    await stop.wait()
    cancel.set(); await asyncio.sleep(0.3); task.cancel()

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Wrong enum. Order operations here are SUB_OP_*, not OC_OP_* — mixing them silently mismatches.
  • No cancellation = leak. Always stop the stream with a cancellation_event you .set().
  • Quiet periods. No trading activity → no events; don't block forever, use a timeout.
  • Updates need before/after. Compare previous vs current rather than assuming what changed.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Market open. Open then close a 0.01 order while subscribed — you see it in new_orders then removed_orders.
  • Modification. Change an order's SL and assert it appears in updated_orders with differing previous/current.
  • Clean stop. cancellation_event.set() ends the async for without leaking tasks.

docs.text:
async def trade_stats_equity_history(since: datetime | None = None, exclude_same_bars: bool | None = None) -> StatsWithChartsData

Stats + equity curve + trades in one call (stats, charts, trades, open_trades).

r = await service.trade_stats_equity_history(exclude_same_bars=True)
print(f"charts={len(r.charts)} trades={len(r.trades)} open={len(r.open_trades)}")

docs.title: MT4Service — Orders & History
docs.text:
Open orders and closed history, with string sort modes and datetime windows instead of protobuf enums.

What the facade adds over MT4Account: you pass sort="open_desc" and since=/until= datetimes; the service maps them to the right enum and request fields.

docs.title: opened_orders(sort=None)
docs.text:
async def opened_orders(*, sort: str | int | None = None) -> OpenedOrdersData

All currently open orders (market + pending). sort is a friendly value mapped to EnumOpenedOrderSortType (e.g. "open_asc", "open_desc", "ticket_asc", "ticket_desc"); omit for the default.

Returns: OpenedOrdersData with order_infos — see the field table.

data = await service.opened_orders(sort="open_desc")
for o in data.order_infos:
    print(o.ticket, o.symbol, o.lots, f"{o.profit:+.2f}")

Underlying: MT4Account.opened_orders.

docs.title: opened_orders_tickets()
docs.text:
async def opened_orders_tickets() -> OpenedOrdersTicketsData

Just the open ticket numbers (lightweight). Pass-through.

Returns: OpenedOrdersTicketsData with tickets (list[int]).

t = await service.opened_orders_tickets()
print(list(t.tickets))

Underlying: MT4Account.opened_orders_tickets.

docs.title: orders_history(sort=None, since=None, until=None, page=None, page_size=None)
docs.text:
async def orders_history(
    *, sort: str | int | None = None,
    since: datetime | None = None, until: datetime | None = None,
    page: int | None = None, page_size: int | None = None,
) -> OrdersHistoryData

Closed orders over a window. The service maps sort → EnumOrderHistorySortType, since/until → from_time/to_time, and page/page_size → page_number/items_per_page.

Returns: OrdersHistoryData with orders_info, total_count, next_page_token — see the field table.

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
end = datetime.utcnow()
hist = await service.orders_history(sort="close_desc", since=end - timedelta(days=30), until=end)
print(f"{hist.total_count} closed orders")

Underlying: MT4Account.orders_history — sort enum values and more examples.

docs.title: MT4Service — Symbols & Quotes
docs.text:
Symbols, quotes and bar history — with masks, string timeframes and unpacked lists.

This is where the facade adds the most convenience over MT4Account: it unpacks protobuf containers into plain Python lists, filters by mask, accepts a string timeframe="H1", and auto-computes a history window from limit.

docs.title: symbols(mask=None)
docs.text:
async def symbols(mask: str | Sequence[str] | None = None) -> list

Returns the symbol list as a Python list (not a protobuf container). mask:

  • None → all symbols,
  • str → case-insensitive substring filter (e.g. "usd"),
  • list/tuple → keep only those exact names (case-insensitive).
all_syms = await service.symbols()
usd      = await service.symbols("usd")             # substring
majors   = await service.symbols(["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"])
print(len(all_syms), len(usd), len(majors))

Underlying: MT4Account.symbols (raw SymbolNameInfos).

docs.title: quote(symbol) · quote_many(symbols)
docs.text:
async def quote(symbol: str) -> QuoteData
async def quote_many(symbols: Sequence[str]) -> QuoteManyData

Pass-throughs. quote returns one QuoteData (bid/ask/high/low/date_time); quote_many returns QuoteManyData with quotes.

q = await service.quote("EURUSD")
print(q.bid, q.ask)

data = await service.quote_many(["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"])
for qq in data.quotes:
    print(qq.symbol, qq.bid, qq.ask)

Underlying: quote · quote_many.

docs.title: quote_history(symbol, timeframe="H1", since=None, until=None, limit=100)
docs.text:
async def quote_history(
    symbol: str, *, timeframe: str | int = "H1",
    since: datetime | None = None, until: datetime | None = None,
    limit: int | None = 100,
) -> QuoteHistoryData

OHLC bars with a string timeframe ("M1", "M5", "M15", "M30", "H1", "H4", "D1", "W1", "MN1"). If you don't pass since/until, the service computes a window from timeframe × limit ending now.

Returns: QuoteHistoryData with historical_quotes — see the bar fields.

# last ~100 H1 bars, no dates needed
data = await service.quote_history("EURUSD", timeframe="H1", limit=100)
for b in data.historical_quotes[-3:]:
    print(b.time.ToDatetime(), b.open, b.high, b.low, b.close)

Underlying: MT4Account.quote_history (takes the ENUM_QUOTE_HISTORY_TIMEFRAME enum directly).

docs.title: symbol_params_many(symbols)
docs.text:
async def symbol_params_many(symbols: str | Sequence[str] | None) -> list | SymbolParamsManyData

Per-symbol trading parameters. str → one symbol; None → all (as a list); list → all, filtered to those names.

info = (await service.symbol_params_many("EURUSD"))      # one symbol's params
one  = info.symbol_infos[0] if hasattr(info, "symbol_infos") else info[0]
print(one.Digits, one.VolumeMin, one.VolumeStep)

Underlying: MT4Account.symbol_params_many — the full ~75-field spec and SP enums.

docs.title: tick_value_with_size(symbol=None, symbols=None)
docs.text:
async def tick_value_with_size(symbol: str | None = None, *, symbols: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> TickValueWithSizeData

Accepts a single symbol or a list of symbols (defaults to "EURUSD" if neither given).

Returns: TickValueWithSizeData with infos (symbolName, TradeTickValue, TradeTickSize, TradeContractSize).

d = await service.tick_value_with_size(symbols=["EURUSD", "XAUUSD"])
for i in d.infos:
    print(i.symbolName, i.TradeTickValue)

Underlying: MT4Account.tick_value_with_size.

docs.title: symbol_select(symbol, select=True)
docs.text:
async def symbol_select(symbol: str, select: bool = True) -> SymbolSelectData

Add a symbol to (or remove it from) Market Watch. Pass-through.

Returns: SymbolSelectData with success.

res = await service.symbol_select("XAUUSD", True)
print("selected:", res.success)

Underlying: MT4Account.symbol_select.

docs.title: server_timezone()
docs.text:
async def server_timezone() -> ServerTimezoneData

Trade-server timezone / UTC offset. Pass-through.

Returns: ServerTimezoneData with server, utc_offset_seconds, source.

tz = await service.server_timezone()
print(f"{tz.server}: UTC offset {tz.utc_offset_seconds}s")

docs.title: MT4Service — Trading Operations
docs.text:
Order operations with friendly keyword names, plus the high-level MT4ServiceTrade helpers.

Two levels here:

  • Facade methods on MT4Service — the same four operations as MT4Account, but accepting friendly keys (side, lots, sl, tp, magic, deviation_pips).
  • MT4ServiceTrade helpers — one-call buy_market / sell_limit / close / … built on the facade.

All of these ultimately call MT4Account.order_send & friends, so failures raise ApiExceptionMT4 — see the Return Codes Reference.

docs.title: order_send(**kwargs)
docs.text:
async def order_send(**kwargs) -> OrderSendData

Friendly wrapper over the raw call. Accepted keys:

Friendly key Maps to Notes symbol symbol required side="buy"/"sell" or type="buy_limit"/… or operation_type= operation_type one of these picks the OrderSendOperationType lots or volume volume required price price required for pending orders sl stoploss SL price tp takeprofit TP price magic magic_number deviation_pips slippage comment comment

Returns: OrderSendData (ticket, volume, price, open_time).

res = await service.order_send(symbol="EURUSD", side="buy", lots=0.01,
                               sl=1.0950, tp=1.1050, magic=777)
print("ticket", res.ticket)

Underlying: MT4Account.order_send — the OC_OP_* enum and raw fields.

docs.title: order_modify(ticket, **kwargs)
docs.text:
async def order_modify(ticket: int, **kwargs) -> OrderModifyData

Accepts sl_price → new_stop_loss, tp_price → new_take_profit (plus new_price, new_expiration).

await service.order_modify(ticket, sl_price=1.0960, tp_price=1.1040)

Underlying: order_modify.

docs.title: order_close_delete(ticket, **kwargs) · order_close_by(ticket_a, ticket_b)
docs.text:
async def order_close_delete(ticket: int, **kwargs) -> OrderCloseDeleteData
async def order_close_by(ticket_a: int, ticket_b: int) -> OrderCloseByData

Close a market order / delete a pending (lots=, closing_price=, slippage= pass through), or net two opposite tickets.

await service.order_close_delete(ticket)              # full close / delete
await service.order_close_delete(ticket, lots=0.01)   # partial
await service.order_close_by(ticket_a, ticket_b)      # net a hedge

Underlying: order_close_delete · order_close_by.

docs.title: Trade helpers (MT4ServiceTrade)
docs.text:
Build the helper from a service, optionally set shared defaults, then use one-call entries:

from app.MT4Service import MT4Service, MT4ServiceTrade

trade = MT4ServiceTrade(service)
trade.set_trade_defaults(magic=777, deviation_pips=3, comment="my bot")

docs.title: order_send_with_defaults(**kwargs)
docs.text: Like service.order_send, but fills in the defaults set above.

docs.title: Market & pending helpers
docs.text:
async def buy_market(symbol, lots, sl=None, tp=None, magic=None, deviation_pips=None, comment=None) -> int
async def sell_market(symbol, lots, sl=None, tp=None, magic=None, deviation_pips=None, comment=None) -> int
async def buy_limit(symbol, price, lots, sl=None, tp=None, magic=None, comment=None) -> int
async def sell_limit(symbol, price, lots, sl=None, tp=None, magic=None, comment=None) -> int
async def buy_stop(symbol, price, lots, sl=None, tp=None, magic=None, comment=None) -> int
async def sell_stop(symbol, price, lots, sl=None, tp=None, magic=None, comment=None) -> int

Each opens the corresponding order and returns the ticket. sl/tp are absolute prices.

ticket = await trade.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01, sl=1.0950, tp=1.1050)
pend   = await trade.buy_limit("EURUSD", price=1.0900, lots=0.01)

docs.text:
async def modify_sl_tp(ticket, sl_price=None, tp_price=None)
async def close(ticket)
async def close_partial(ticket, lots)
async def close_by(ticket_a, ticket_b)

await trade.modify_sl_tp(ticket, sl_price=1.0960, tp_price=1.1040)
await trade.close_partial(ticket, lots=0.01)
await trade.close(ticket)

Even higher level? MT4Sugar (service.sugar) adds pip-based SL/TP, lot sizing by risk, trailing stops and close_all.

docs.title: MT4Service — Streaming Methods
docs.text:
The same real-time streams as MT4Account, exposed on the facade.

All are async generators — consume with async for, and always drive them so they can be stopped cleanly (cancel the consuming task). See gRPC Stream Management.

docs.title: on_symbol_tick(symbols)
docs.text:
async def on_symbol_tick(symbols: str | Iterable[str])

Live bid/ask ticks. Accepts a single symbol or an iterable of symbols.

async for td in service.on_symbol_tick(["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"]):
    t = td.symbol_tick
    print(t.symbol, t.bid, t.ask)

docs.text:
async def on_trade()

Trade events — new / updated / removed orders.

async for ev in service.on_trade():
    for o in ev.event_data.new_orders:
        print("NEW", o.ticket, o.symbol)

async def on_opened_orders_tickets(pull_interval_milliseconds: int | None = None)

Periodic snapshots of open position / pending ticket lists.

async for ev in service.on_opened_orders_tickets(pull_interval_milliseconds=1000):

Live P/L of open orders on a timer.

docs.title: MT4Service — Overview
docs.text:
The mid-level facade: the same operations as MT4Account, but with friendlier Python signatures and unpacked results.

MT4Service is Layer 2. It wraps a connected MT4Account and:

  • accepts string enums (timeframe="H1", sort="open_desc") instead of protobuf constants,
  • unpacks protobuf containers into plain Python lists,
  • takes friendly keyword names (side, lots, sl, tp, magic) and maps them to the raw request,
  • fills sensible defaults (e.g. a history window for quote_history).

High-level one-liners and risk sizing live one layer up in MT4Sugar (reachable as service.sugar).

MT4Sugar    (HIGH)   one-liners, risk sizing, watchers
MT4Service  (MID)    friendly facade  ← you are here
MT4Account  (LOW)    raw gRPC / protobuf

docs.title: 🚦 Method groups
docs.text:
Each group is documented in a single page; follow the links.

  • 1. Account Information — account_summary, trade_stats, trade_unrealized_pl, equity_history, trade_stats_equity_history
  • 2. Orders & History — opened_orders, opened_orders_tickets, orders_history
  • 3. Symbols & Quotes — symbols, quote, quote_many, quote_history, symbol_params_many, tick_value_with_size, symbol_select, server_timezone
  • 4. Trading Operations — order_send, order_modify, order_close_delete, order_close_by + the MT4ServiceTrade helpers (buy_market, sell_market, buy_limit/stop, sell_limit/stop, close, close_partial, close_by, modify_sl_tp, set_trade_defaults, order_send_with_defaults)
  • 5. Streaming Methods — on_symbol_tick, on_trade, on_opened_orders_tickets, on_opened_orders_profit, on_connect_state

docs.title: 🔌 Connection & lifecycle
docs.text:
MT4Service wraps an MT4Account; connect through either one.

Method Description connect_by_server_name(server_name, base_symbol=None, timeout_s=None) Connect via broker server name. connect_by_host_port(host, port, base_symbol=None, timeout_s=None) Connect to a terminal host/port. reconnect() Re-establish the session. disconnect(delete=False) Release the session. get_headers() Current gRPC metadata headers. 
import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account
from app.MT4Service import MT4Service

async def main():
    account = MT4Account(user=..., password=..., grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="MetaQuotes-Demo",
                                         base_chart_symbol="EURUSD", timeout_seconds=30)
    service = MT4Service(account)

    s = await service.account_summary()
    print(s.account_balance, s.account_equity)

    await account.channel.close()

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: 🧩 The sugar property
docs.text:
service.sugar returns a ready MT4Sugar bound to this service — the high-level API:

sugar = service.sugar
q = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")

docs.title: ⚙️ Trade helpers — MT4ServiceTrade
docs.text:
The convenience order helpers live in a small companion class, MT4ServiceTrade, built on a MT4Service:

from app.MT4Service import MT4Service, MT4ServiceTrade

trade = MT4ServiceTrade(service)
trade.set_trade_defaults(magic=777, deviation_pips=3, comment="my bot")
# ticket = await trade.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01, sl=..., tp=...)

They are documented in 4. Trading Operations.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Connection & Defaults
docs.text: Session helpers and shared defaults that the rest of the Sugar API reuses.

docs.title: ensure_connected()
docs.text:
async def ensure_connected()

Make sure the underlying session is live (reconnect if needed). Call at the start of a routine; most Sugar methods also guard themselves.

await sugar.ensure_connected()

docs.title: ping()
docs.text:
async def ping()

Lightweight liveness check against the terminal.

await sugar.ping()

docs.title: ensure_symbol(symbol, preload_params=True, require_trade_allowed=False, force_refresh=False)
docs.text:
async def ensure_symbol(symbol, preload_params=True, require_trade_allowed=False, force_refresh=False)

Make a symbol ready to use — selects it in Market Watch and (by default) preloads its parameters. Pass require_trade_allowed=True to also assert trading is enabled.

await sugar.ensure_symbol("XAUUSD", require_trade_allowed=True)

docs.title: set_defaults(symbol=None, magic=None, deviation_pips=None, slippage_pips=None, risk_percent=None)
docs.text:
def set_defaults(symbol=None, magic=None, deviation_pips=None, slippage_pips=None, risk_percent=None)

Set defaults reused across calls — e.g. a default symbol, magic tag and risk_percent. Order entry and risk sizing fall back to these when you omit the argument.

sugar.set_defaults(symbol="EURUSD", magic=777, deviation_pips=3, risk_percent=1.0)
ticket = await sugar.buy_market(lots=0.01)        # uses default symbol & magic

docs.title: with_defaults(**overrides)
docs.text:
def with_defaults(**overrides)   # context manager

Temporarily override defaults for a block, restoring them afterwards.

with sugar.with_defaults(magic=999, deviation_pips=5):
    await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)   # magic=999 only here

docs.title: get_default(key, fallback=None)
docs.text:
def get_default(key, fallback=None) -> Any

Read a current default value.

print(sugar.get_default("symbol"), sugar.get_default("risk_percent", 1.0))

docs.title: diag_snapshot()
docs.text:
async def diag_snapshot() -> dict

A diagnostics snapshot (connection state, defaults, active watchers) — handy for logging/health checks.

print(await sugar.diag_snapshot())

docs.title: disconnect(delete=False)
docs.text:
async def disconnect(delete=False)

Release the session (optionally deleting the terminal instance). In scripts, prefer async with MT4Sugar(service) which cleans up for you.

await sugar.disconnect()

mid = await sugar.mid_price("EURUSD")

async def spread_pips(symbol: str) -> float

Current spread expressed in pips (already converted from price units).

if await sugar.spread_pips("EURUSD") <= 2.0:

docs.title: bars(symbol, timeframe, count=None, since=None, until=None)
docs.text:
async def bars(symbol: str, timeframe: str, count=None, since=None, until=None) -> list

OHLC bars for a string timeframe ("M1", "M5", "H1", "D1", …). Give a count for the most recent N bars, or a since/until window.

bars = await sugar.bars("EURUSD", "H1", count=100)

Historical ticks for a symbol over a window (or the last limit).

docs.text:
async def wait_price(symbol: str, target: float, direction: str = ">=", timeout_s: float | None = None) -> bool

Block until the price reaches target (direction is ">=" or "<="), or the timeout elapses.

hit = await sugar.wait_price("EURUSD", 1.1050, direction=">=", timeout_s=60)
if hit:
    await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Symbol Math & Normalization
docs.text: Pip/point conversions and broker-compliant rounding — the helpers that make pips-first trading work.

docs.title: point(symbol) · digits(symbol) · pip_size(symbol)
docs.text:
async def point(symbol: str) -> float     # smallest price step (e.g. 0.00001)
async def digits(symbol: str) -> int      # price decimals (e.g. 5)
async def pip_size(symbol: str) -> float  # one pip in price (e.g. 0.0001)

print(await sugar.point("EURUSD"), await sugar.digits("EURUSD"), await sugar.pip_size("EURUSD"))

docs.title: pips_to_price(symbol, pips) · price_to_pips(symbol, price_delta)
docs.text:
async def pips_to_price(symbol: str, pips: float) -> float
async def price_to_pips(symbol: str, price_delta: float) -> float

Convert a pip distance to an absolute price delta and back.

delta = await sugar.pips_to_price("EURUSD", 20)      # 20 pips -> 0.0020
pips  = await sugar.price_to_pips("EURUSD", 0.0020)  # 0.0020  -> 20

docs.title: normalize_price(symbol, price) · normalize_lot(symbol, lots)
docs.text:
async def normalize_price(symbol: str, price: float) -> float
async def normalize_lot(symbol: str, lots: float) -> float

Round a price to the symbol's digits, and a lot size into [VolumeMin, VolumeMax] on the broker's VolumeStep.

p = await sugar.normalize_price("EURUSD", 1.098765)   # -> 1.09877
l = await sugar.normalize_lot("EURUSD", 0.0234)        # -> 0.02

Order-entry methods normalize for you — use these when doing your own math.

Money value of one tick for the given lot size (in the deposit currency).

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Risk Sizing
docs.text: Turn a risk budget into a lot size, and reason about per-trade risk.

docs.title: calc_lot_by_risk(symbol, risk_percent, stop_pips, balance=None)
docs.text:
async def calc_lot_by_risk(symbol: str, risk_percent: float, stop_pips: float, balance: float | None = None) -> float

The headline sizing helper: returns the lot size so that hitting a stop_pips stop loses risk_percent of the account (balance is read automatically unless you pass one). The result is normalized to the broker's volume step.

lots = await sugar.calc_lot_by_risk("EURUSD", risk_percent=1.0, stop_pips=50)
ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=lots, sl_pips=50, tp_pips=100)

docs.title: calc_cash_risk(symbol, lots, stop_pips)
docs.text:
async def calc_cash_risk(symbol: str, lots: float, stop_pips: float) -> float

The inverse view: the monetary risk of a given lot size with a stop_pips stop.

risk = await sugar.calc_cash_risk("EURUSD", lots=0.10, stop_pips=30)
print(f"risking {risk:.2f} on this trade")

docs.title: breakeven_price(entry_price, commission=0.0, swap=0.0)
docs.text:
def breakeven_price(entry_price: float, commission: float = 0.0, swap: float = 0.0) -> float

A synchronous helper (no await): the price at which a position breaks even after commission and swap.

bp = sugar.breakeven_price(entry_price=1.10000, commission=-2.0, swap=-0.5)

To move a live order's stop to breakeven, use auto_breakeven / close_by_breakeven.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Order Entry
docs.text:
One-line order entry with pips-based SL/TP, automatic normalization and defaults.

All entry methods return the new ticket (int). lots and the SL/TP arguments are keyword-only. Use sl_pips/tp_pips for pip distances or sl_price/tp_price for absolute prices. Omitted symbol/magic/deviation_pips fall back to defaults.

docs.title: Market orders
docs.text:
async def buy_market(symbol=None, *, lots=None, sl_pips=None, tp_pips=None,
                     sl_price=None, tp_price=None, comment=None, magic=None, deviation_pips=None) -> int
async def sell_market(**kwargs) -> int   # same arguments

# simplest
ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)

# with pip-based SL/TP and a tag
ticket = await sugar.sell_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=40, magic=777)

docs.title: Pending orders
docs.text:
async def buy_limit(symbol=None, *, price, lots=None, sl_pips=None, tp_pips=None,
                    sl_price=None, tp_price=None, comment=None, magic=None) -> int
async def sell_limit(**kwargs) -> int
async def buy_stop(**kwargs) -> int
async def sell_stop(**kwargs) -> int

price (the pending entry) is required.

ask = (await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD"))["ask"]
# buy the dip 30 pips below, with pip-based protection
ticket = await sugar.buy_limit("EURUSD", price=ask - 0.0030, lots=0.01, sl_pips=15, tp_pips=30)

# breakout stop above, absolute SL/TP
ticket = await sugar.buy_stop("EURUSD", price=ask + 0.0020, lots=0.01,
                              sl_price=1.0950, tp_price=1.1080)

docs.title: place_order(...) — the unified entry
docs.text:
async def place_order(side: str, order_type: str, symbol=None, price=None, lots=None,
                      sl_pips=None, tp_pips=None, sl_price=None, tp_price=None,
                      comment=None, magic=None, deviation_pips=None) -> int

The method all the helpers above delegate to. side is "buy"/"sell", order_type is "market"/"limit"/"stop". Handy when the side/type are computed at runtime.

side = "buy" if signal_up else "sell"
ticket = await sugar.place_order(side=side, order_type="market", symbol="EURUSD",
                                 lots=0.01, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=40)

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Order Management
docs.text: Modify, close and clean up orders — individually or in bulk.

docs.title: Modify SL/TP
docs.text:
async def modify_sl_tp_by_pips(ticket: int, sl_pips=None, tp_pips=None)
async def modify_sl_tp_by_price(ticket: int, sl_price=None, tp_price=None)

Set SL/TP by pip distance from entry or by absolute price. Pass only what you want to change.

await sugar.modify_sl_tp_by_pips(ticket, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=40)
await sugar.modify_sl_tp_by_price(ticket, sl_price=1.0950, tp_price=1.1050)

docs.title: Close one order
docs.text:
async def close(ticket: int)
async def close_partial(ticket: int, lots: float)
async def close_by(ticket_a: int, ticket_b: int)
async def close_by_tickets(ticket_a: int, ticket_b: int)

close closes a market order or deletes a pending; close_partial closes part of a position; close_by / close_by_tickets net two opposite orders against each other.

await sugar.close(ticket)
await sugar.close_partial(ticket, lots=0.01)
await sugar.close_by(buy_ticket, sell_ticket)

docs.title: Bulk operations
docs.text:
async def close_all(symbol=None, magic=None, only_profit=None)
async def cancel_pendings(symbol=None, magic=None)

close_all closes open positions (optionally filtered by symbol / magic, or only the profitable ones); cancel_pendings removes pending orders.

await sugar.close_all()                      # flatten everything
await sugar.close_all(symbol="EURUSD")        # only this symbol
await sugar.close_all(only_profit=True)       # take profits, leave losers
await sugar.cancel_pendings(magic=777)        # drop this bot's pendings

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Trailing & Breakeven
docs.text: Automated stop management — trailing stops and move-to-breakeven, run as background workers.

docs.title: set_trailing_stop(ticket, distance_pips, step_pips=None)
docs.text:
async def set_trailing_stop(ticket: int, distance_pips: float, step_pips: float | None = None) -> str

Start a background trailing stop that keeps SL ~distance_pips behind price, moving it in step_pips increments. Returns a subscription id — keep it to stop the trailer later.

sub = await sugar.set_trailing_stop(ticket, distance_pips=20, step_pips=5)
# ... later ...
await sugar.unset_trailing_stop(sub)

docs.title: unset_trailing_stop(subscription_id)
docs.text:
async def unset_trailing_stop(subscription_id: str)

Stop a trailing worker started by set_trailing_stop.

docs.title: auto_breakeven(ticket, trigger_pips, plus_pips=0.0)
docs.text:
async def auto_breakeven(ticket: int, trigger_pips: float, plus_pips: float = 0.0) -> str

Start a worker that moves SL to breakeven (plus plus_pips) once the order is trigger_pips in profit. Returns a subscription id (stop it with unset_trailing_stop / unwatch).

sub = await sugar.auto_breakeven(ticket, trigger_pips=40, plus_pips=1)

docs.title: close_by_breakeven(ticket, plus_pips=0.0)
docs.text:
async def close_by_breakeven(ticket: int, plus_pips: float = 0.0)

A one-shot: close the order if it's at (or above) breakeven + plus_pips right now — useful to lock in a scratch/small win on demand.

await sugar.close_by_breakeven(ticket, plus_pips=1)

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Watchers & Waiters
docs.text:
Callback-based background watchers, and await-able waiters for order lifecycle events.

Watchers register a callback and return a subscription id (stop them with unwatch). Waiters block until something happens (or a timeout).

docs.title: Watchers (callback + subscription id)
docs.text:
async def watch_ticks(symbol: str, on_tick, throttle_ms: int | None = None) -> str
async def watch_trades(on_event) -> str
async def watch_opened_orders(on_event) -> str
async def watch_profit(on_event, timer_period_ms: int = 1000) -> str
async def watch_tickets(on_event, pull_interval_ms: int = 500) -> str
async def unwatch(subscription_id: str)

Unlike the low-level async for streams, watchers hand each event to your callback and run in the background — your code keeps going.

def on_tick(t):
    print(t)

sub = await sugar.watch_ticks("EURUSD", on_tick, throttle_ms=200)
# ... later ...
await sugar.unwatch(sub)

# live P/L callback
pid = await sugar.watch_profit(lambda ev: print("floating:", ev), timer_period_ms=1000)
# trade events
tid = await sugar.watch_trades(lambda ev: print("trade:", ev))
Watcher Fires on watch_ticks(symbol, on_tick) each tick (optionally throttled) watch_trades(on_event) trade events (open/modify/close) watch_opened_orders(on_event) changes to the open-order set watch_profit(on_event, timer_period_ms) periodic open-order P/L watch_tickets(on_event, pull_interval_ms) periodic ticket-list snapshots

docs.title: Waiters (await until an event)
docs.text:
async def wait_filled(ticket: int, timeout_s: float | None = None) -> bool
async def wait_closed(ticket: int, timeout_s: float | None = None) -> bool

Block until a pending order fills, or an order closes.

ticket = await sugar.buy_limit("EURUSD", price=1.0900, lots=0.01)
if await sugar.wait_filled(ticket, timeout_s=300):
    print("filled!")
    await sugar.wait_closed(ticket)   # then wait for it to close

See also wait_price to wait on a price level.

docs.title: find_orders(symbol=None, magic=None, side=None, state=None, min_profit=None)

async def find_orders(symbol=None, magic=None, side=None, state=None, min_profit=None) -> list[dict]

Search orders by filters, returned as a list of dicts. side is "buy"/"sell", state is "open"/"pending"/"closed", min_profit keeps only orders at/above a profit.

mine   = await sugar.find_orders(magic=777)
buys   = await sugar.find_orders(symbol="EURUSD", side="buy", state="open")
winners = await sugar.find_orders(min_profit=0.0)
for o in mine:

All current orders on one symbol (shortcut for find_orders(symbol=...)).

orders = await sugar.orders_for_symbol("EURUSD")
print(len(orders), "order(s) on EURUSD")

Aggregate value / floating P/L of matching open positions.

pnl = await sugar.positions_value(symbol="EURUSD")
print(f"EURUSD floating: {pnl:+.2f}")

A summary of net exposure — per symbol (by_symbol=True) or overall. Handy for a risk dashboard line.

summary = await sugar.exposure_summary(by_symbol=True)

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Master Overview
docs.text:
The high-level API: one-liners, pip-based SL/TP, risk sizing, trailing stops, watchers and waiters. The best starting point for most strategies.

MT4Sugar is Layer 3. It sits on top of MT4Service and turns the raw operations into ergonomic one-liners — you pass symbols, lots, pips and prices, and it handles normalization, enum mapping and plumbing.

MT4Sugar    (HIGH)   one-liners, risk sizing, trailing, watchers  ← you are here
MT4Service  (MID)    friendly facade over MT4Account
MT4Account  (LOW)    raw gRPC / protobuf

Get an instance from a connected service:

import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account
from app.MT4Service import MT4Service

async def main():
    account = MT4Account(user=..., password=..., grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="MetaQuotes-Demo",
                                         base_chart_symbol="EURUSD", timeout_seconds=30)
    service = MT4Service(account)
    sugar = service.sugar                 # ← the high-level API

    # one-liners:
    q = await sugar.last_quote("EURUSD")
    lots = await sugar.calc_lot_by_risk("EURUSD", risk_percent=1.0, stop_pips=50)
    ticket = await sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots=lots, sl_pips=50, tp_pips=100)

    await account.channel.close()

asyncio.run(main())

MT4Sugar(service) also supports async with for scoped use.

  • 3. Symbol Math & Normalization — point, digits, pip_size, pips_to_price, price_to_pips, normalize_price, normalize_lot, tick_value

  • 5. Order Entry — buy_market, sell_market, buy_limit, sell_limit, buy_stop, sell_stop, place_order
  • 6. Order Management — modify_sl_tp_by_pips, modify_sl_tp_by_price, close, close_partial, close_by, close_by_tickets, close_all, cancel_pendings
  • 7. Trailing & Breakeven — set_trailing_stop, unset_trailing_stop, auto_breakeven, close_by_breakeven

docs.title: 🧩 Conventions
docs.text:
• Pips, not points. SL/TP and distances are in pips (sl_pips, tp_pips, distance_pips); Sugar converts to prices via the symbol's pip size.
  • Lots are keyword-only on the entry methods (buy_market("EURUSD", lots=0.01)).
  • Normalization is automatic. Lots are snapped to the volume step and prices to the symbol's digits.
  • Defaults. set_defaults(...) sets a default symbol/magic/deviation/risk reused across calls; with_defaults(...) is a scoped override.
  • Errors raise MT4Error subclasses (OrderRejected, ModifyRejected, …) — see the Return Codes Reference.

docs.title: Strategies — Master Overview
docs.text: One page to orient fast: the ready-made orchestrators and presets that ship with PyMT4, how to pick one, and links to each spec.

docs.title: ⚠️ Educational & demonstration only
docs.text:
The orchestrators and presets here are demonstration examples — templates for building your own strategies, not production trading systems.

  • Simplified logic, no portfolio-level risk controls, no economic-calendar integration.
  • Demo accounts only. Study the code, test on demo, add your own risk management before considering anything live.
  • Trading involves substantial risk of loss; you are responsible for your decisions.

They live in the repo under Strategy/orchestrator/ and Strategy/presets/, and are driven by MT4Service / MT4Sugar. The numbered examples 11–16 run them.

docs.title: 🚦 Orchestrators
docs.text:
Each orchestrator is a single async def run_*(service, strategy, risk, ...) coroutine that takes a StrategyPreset (what/where to enter) and a RiskPreset (how much to risk / protect), and returns a dict result.

Orchestrator Entry What it does Demo Market One-Shot run_market_one_shot Open a market order with an automatic SL/TP bracket. python main.py market (11) Bracket + Trailing run_bracket_with_trailing_activation Entry with a bracket; trailing stop switches on once price is far enough in profit. python main.py trailing (12) Grid DCA (common SL) run_grid_dca_common_sl A grid of averaging entries sharing one common stop-loss. python main.py grid (13) OCO Straddle run_oco_straddle Buy-stop above + sell-stop below; one triggers, the other cancels (breakout). python main.py oco (14) Pending Bracket run_pending_bracket Place a pending order with an automatic bracket, wait for fill. python main.py pending (15)

docs.title: 🎛️ Presets
docs.text:
Two small dataclasses configure every orchestrator (see Presets):

  • StrategyPreset — symbol, use_market, entry_price, lots, magic, deviation_pips, comment.
  • RiskPreset — risk_percent, sl_pips, tp_pips, trailing_pips, be_trigger_pips, be_plus_pips.

Ready-made presets and factories ship too — MarketEURUSD, LimitEURUSD(price), BreakoutBuy(...), Conservative, risk profiles (ScalperEURUSD(), SwingEURUSD()), per-symbol factories (strategy_symbols), plus ATR- and session-based risk. Example 16 (python main.py presets) prints them all.

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (Python async/await)
docs.text:
import asyncio
from MetaRpcMT4.mt4_account import MT4Account
from app.MT4Service import MT4Service
from Strategy.orchestrator import run_market_one_shot
from Strategy.presets.strategy import StrategyPreset
from Strategy.presets.risk import RiskPreset

async def main():
    account = MT4Account(user=..., password=..., grpc_server="mt4.mrpc.pro:443")
    await account.connect_by_server_name(server_name="MetaQuotes-Demo",
                                         base_chart_symbol="EURUSD", timeout_seconds=30)
    service = MT4Service(account)

    strategy = StrategyPreset(symbol="EURUSD", use_market=True, lots=0.01, magic=101)
    risk = RiskPreset(risk_percent=1.0, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=40)

    result = await run_market_one_shot(service, strategy, risk)
    print(result)

    await account.channel.close()

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: 🧭 Which orchestrator?
docs.text:
• Simple entry with protection → Market One-Shot
  • Let winners run → Bracket + Trailing
  • Average into a range → Grid DCA
  • Trade a breakout either way → OCO Straddle
  • Wait at a price with a bracket → Pending Bracket

docs.title: Bracket + Trailing Activation
docs.text:
Enter with an SL/TP bracket; the trailing stop switches on only once the trade is far enough in profit.

  • Source: Strategy/orchestrator/bracket_trailing_activation.py
  • Entry: run_bracket_with_trailing_activation(service, strategy, risk, ...)
  • Demo: examples/4_orchestrators/12_bracket_trailing.py · python main.py trailing

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Opens an order (market or pending per the StrategyPreset) with a bracket.
  2. Polls the position's profit in pips.
  3. When profit reaches activate_trailing_at_pips, it activates a trailing stop at trailing_distance_pips (falling back to risk.trailing_pips), trailed in trailing_step_pips steps.
  4. Returns a dict result.

Use it to protect open profit and let winners run without trailing from the very first pip.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
async def run_bracket_with_trailing_activation(
    svc,
    sp: StrategyPreset,
    rp: RiskPreset,
    *,
    side: str = "buy",                              # "buy" or "sell"
    activate_trailing_at_pips: float = 12.0,        # profit needed before trailing turns on
    trailing_distance_pips: float | None = None,    # trail distance; falls back to rp.trailing_pips
    trailing_step_pips: float = 1.0,                # trail step
    wait_fill_timeout_s: int = 1200,                # pending-fill timeout
    max_spread_pips: float | None = None,           # optional spread guard
    poll_interval_s: float = 1.0,                   # profit poll cycle
) -> dict

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from Strategy.orchestrator import run_bracket_with_trailing_activation
from Strategy.presets.strategy import StrategyPreset
from Strategy.presets.risk import RiskPreset

strategy = StrategyPreset(symbol="EURUSD", use_market=True, lots=0.01, magic=102)
risk = RiskPreset(risk_percent=1.0, sl_pips=25, tp_pips=80, trailing_pips=15)

result = await run_bracket_with_trailing_activation(
    service, strategy, risk,
    side="buy",
    activate_trailing_at_pips=12,   # start trailing after +12 pips
    trailing_step_pips=1,
)

Trailing uses MT4Sugar's set_trailing_stop; the bracket SL/TP come from the RiskPreset.

docs.title: Grid DCA (common SL)
docs.text:
A grid of averaging (DCA) entries that all share one common stop-loss.

  • Source: Strategy/orchestrator/grid_dca_common_sl.py
  • Entry: run_grid_dca_common_sl(service, strategy, risk, ...)
  • Demo: examples/4_orchestrators/13_grid_dca.py · python main.py grid

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Places a ladder of steps pending orders, step_pips apart, from base_price (mid price if None), in the side direction.
  2. As legs fill (at least arm_when_filled_at_least), it manages one common stop-loss anchored per sl_anchor.
  3. Splits risk across the grid (risk_mode="split_total") or risks each leg fully ("per_leg_full").
  4. Returns a dict result.

Use it to average into a move with a single, controlled risk envelope — best in ranges / mean-reversion.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
async def run_grid_dca_common_sl(
    svc,
    sp: StrategyPreset,
    rp: RiskPreset,
    *,
    side: str = "buy",
    steps: int = 5,
    step_pips: float = 10.0,
    base_price: float | None = None,         # None -> mid price
    arm_when_filled_at_least: int = 1,       # manage common SL after N fills
    sl_anchor: str = "lowest_leg",           # "lowest_leg" (BUY) / "highest_leg" (SELL)
    risk_mode: str = "split_total",          # "split_total" | "per_leg_full"
    risk_total_percent: float | None = None, # total risk when splitting
    # ... further tuning knobs
) -> dict

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from Strategy.orchestrator import run_grid_dca_common_sl
from Strategy.presets.strategy import StrategyPreset
from Strategy.presets.risk import RiskPreset

strategy = StrategyPreset(symbol="EURUSD", use_market=False, lots=0.01, magic=103)
risk = RiskPreset(risk_percent=2.0, sl_pips=60, tp_pips=40)

result = await run_grid_dca_common_sl(
    service, strategy, risk,
    side="buy", steps=5, step_pips=10,
    risk_mode="split_total", risk_total_percent=2.0,
)

⚠️ Grids increase exposure as more legs fill — keep steps modest and the common SL tight.

docs.title: Market One-Shot
docs.text:
Open a market order with an automatic SL/TP bracket — the simplest orchestrator.

  • Source: Strategy/orchestrator/market_one_shot.py
  • Entry: run_market_one_shot(service, strategy, risk) -> dict
  • Demo: examples/4_orchestrators/11_market_one_shot.py · python main.py market

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Reads the StrategyPreset (symbol, lots, magic) and RiskPreset (sl/tp in pips).
  2. Opens a market order via MT4Sugar.
  3. Attaches a bracket — stop-loss and take-profit derived from the risk preset's pips.
  4. Returns a dict describing the opened order / result.

Use it when you simply want a protected market entry in one call.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
async def run_market_one_shot(
    svc: MT4Service,
    strategy: StrategyPreset,
    risk: RiskPreset,
) -> dict
Parameter Type Description svc MT4Service A connected service (or service.sugar is used internally). strategy StrategyPreset symbol, lots, magic, deviation_pips, comment. use_market=True. risk RiskPreset risk_percent, sl_pips, tp_pips — sizing & bracket.

Returns: a dict with the result (ticket and the keys the orchestrator reports).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from Strategy.orchestrator import run_market_one_shot
from Strategy.presets.strategy import StrategyPreset
from Strategy.presets.risk import RiskPreset

strategy = StrategyPreset(symbol="EURUSD", use_market=True, lots=0.01, magic=101,
                          deviation_pips=3.0, comment="pymt4 market_one_shot")
risk = RiskPreset(risk_percent=1.0, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=40)

result = await run_market_one_shot(service, strategy, risk)
print("result keys:", list(result.keys()))

If lots is omitted in the StrategyPreset, sizing can come from risk_percent + sl_pips via MT4Sugar's calc_lot_by_risk.

docs.title: OCO Straddle (breakout)
docs.text:
A bi-directional breakout: buy-stop above + sell-stop below the price; when one triggers, the other is cancelled (OCO).

  • Source: Strategy/orchestrator/oco_straddle.py
  • Entry: run_oco_straddle(service, strategy, risk, ...)
  • Demo: examples/4_orchestrators/14_oco_straddle.py · python main.py oco

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Places a buy stop offset_pips above and a sell stop offset_pips below the current price, each with its own bracket.
  2. Waits up to timeout_s. When one side triggers, it cancels the opposite pending order.
  3. Sizes each leg per risk_mode ("per_leg_full" = full risk on each leg).
  4. Returns a dict result.

Use it to catch a breakout in either direction (e.g. around news or a consolidation).

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
async def run_oco_straddle(
    svc,
    sp: StrategyPreset,
    rp: RiskPreset,
    *,
    offset_pips: float = 10.0,          # distance above/below price for the stops
    timeout_s: int = 1200,              # how long to wait for a breakout
    risk_mode: str = "per_leg_full",    # "per_leg_full" | "split_total"
    max_spread_pips: float | None = None,
) -> dict

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from Strategy.orchestrator import run_oco_straddle
from Strategy.presets.strategy import StrategyPreset
from Strategy.presets.risk import RiskPreset

strategy = StrategyPreset(symbol="EURUSD", use_market=False, lots=0.01, magic=104)
risk = RiskPreset(risk_percent=1.0, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=40)

result = await run_oco_straddle(
    service, strategy, risk,
    offset_pips=10, timeout_s=300, risk_mode="per_leg_full",
)

Slippage during fast breakouts can briefly trigger both legs — the orchestrator cancels the loser as soon as one fills.

docs.title: Pending Bracket
docs.text:
Place a pending order at a chosen price with an automatic SL/TP bracket, then wait for it to fill.

  • Source: Strategy/orchestrator/pending_bracket.py
  • Entry: run_pending_bracket(service, strategy, risk, *, timeout_s=900) -> dict
  • Demo: examples/4_orchestrators/15_pending_bracket.py · python main.py pending

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Places a pending order (limit/stop) at strategy.entry_price with a bracket from the risk preset.
  2. Waits up to timeout_s for the order to fill.
  3. Returns a dict result (filled / still pending / timed out).

Use it for "set your price and wait for the market to come to you" entries.

docs.title: Signature
docs.text:
async def run_pending_bracket(
    svc,
    strategy: StrategyPreset,
    risk: RiskPreset,
    *,
    timeout_s: int = 900,   # how long to wait for a fill
) -> dict
Parameter Type Description svc MT4Service Connected service. strategy StrategyPreset use_market=False, entry_price set (the pending price), lots, magic. risk RiskPreset sl_pips / tp_pips for the bracket. timeout_s int Cancel/stop waiting after this many seconds.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from Strategy.orchestrator import run_pending_bracket
from Strategy.presets.strategy import StrategyPreset
from Strategy.presets.risk import RiskPreset

mid = await service.sugar.mid_price("EURUSD")
entry = round(mid - 0.0030, 5)   # a BUY LIMIT ~30 pips below the market

strategy = StrategyPreset(symbol="EURUSD", use_market=False, entry_price=entry,
                          lots=0.01, magic=105, comment="pymt4 pending_bracket")
risk = RiskPreset(risk_percent=1.0, sl_pips=25, tp_pips=50)

result = await run_pending_bracket(service, strategy, risk, timeout_s=300)
print("result keys:", list(result.keys()))

In a short demo the limit usually won't fill — use a short timeout_s and clean up the pending order afterwards with cancel_pendings.

docs.title: Strategy & Risk Presets
docs.text:
The two small dataclasses that configure every orchestrator, plus ready-made presets and factories.

  • Source: Strategy/presets/ (strategy.py, risk.py, risk_profiles.py, risk_atr.py, risk_session.py, strategy_symbols.py)
  • Demo: examples/4_orchestrators/16_presets.py · python main.py presets

Orchestrators take one StrategyPreset (what/where to enter) and one RiskPreset (how much to risk / protect):

result = await run_market_one_shot(service, StrategyPreset(...), RiskPreset(...))

docs.title: StrategyPreset
docs.text:
What and where to enter.

@dataclass
class StrategyPreset:
    symbol: str
    use_market: bool = True             # True = market, False = pending (needs entry_price)
    entry_price: float | None = None    # pending-order price
    lots: float | None = None           # None -> size by risk
    magic: int = 0
    deviation_pips: float = 2.0
    comment: str | None = None

from Strategy.presets.strategy import StrategyPreset
sp = StrategyPreset(symbol="EURUSD", use_market=True, lots=0.01, magic=101)

docs.title: Ready-made / factories (strategy.py)
docs.text: Name Description MarketEURUSD Market EURUSD preset (magic 777). LimitEURUSD(price) A BUY/SELL LIMIT EURUSD at price. BreakoutBuy(symbol="EURUSD", offset_pips=10) A breakout-style pending preset.

docs.title: Per-symbol factories (strategy_symbols.py)
docs.text:
Limit/breakout factories for many instruments — LimitGBPUSD(price), LimitXAUUSD(price), BreakoutGBPUSD, BreakoutXAUUSD, … plus a REGISTRY dict of them.

from Strategy.presets import strategy_symbols
sp = strategy_symbols.LimitGBPUSD(1.2600)
print(list(strategy_symbols.REGISTRY.keys()))

docs.title: RiskPreset
docs.text:
How much to risk and how to protect.

@dataclass
class RiskPreset:
    risk_percent: float
    sl_pips: float
    tp_pips: float | None = None
    trailing_pips: float | None = None
    be_trigger_pips: float | None = None   # move to breakeven after N pips
    be_plus_pips: float | None = None      # breakeven + N pips

from Strategy.presets.risk import RiskPreset
rp = RiskPreset(risk_percent=1.0, sl_pips=20, tp_pips=40, trailing_pips=15)

docs.title: Ready-made / profiles
docs.text:
Name Source Description Conservative risk.py risk_percent=0.5, sl_pips=25, tp_pips=50. ScalperEURUSD() / ScalperXAUUSD() risk_profiles.py Tight scalping risk profiles. SwingEURUSD() / SwingXAUUSD() risk_profiles.py Wider swing risk profiles. 
from Strategy.presets import risk_profiles
rp = risk_profiles.ScalperEURUSD()

docs.title: ATR- and session-based risk
docs.text:
• risk_atr.py — builds a RiskPreset whose stops scale with recent volatility (ATR).
  • risk_session.py — adjusts risk by trading session (e.g. tighter outside liquid hours).

docs.title: Build your own
docs.text:
sp = StrategyPreset(symbol="USDJPY", use_market=True, lots=0.02, magic=1234,
                    deviation_pips=4.0, comment="my strategy")
rp = RiskPreset(risk_percent=1.0, sl_pips=30, tp_pips=60,
                trailing_pips=20, be_trigger_pips=20, be_plus_pips=1)

result = await run_market_one_shot(service, sp, rp)
